The Zagłębie Anti-Hitler Committees — What must they be for the people, and what must the people be for them

[Article — Zagłębie, the Anti-Hitler Committees; the boycott of German goods.]
What must they be for the people, and what must the people be for them.
Actually, when one talks about Hitlerism and its deeds, one says nothing new. People have already grown used to all of it, as if it simply could not be otherwise. When one writes about the matter, it arouses no great interest in Jewish circles. We have become indifferent and apathetically disposed towards everything that degrades our honour, so much so that we have stopped reacting as we should to the wrongs done to us; and it is possible that this has also led to the inner demoralisation, which, by the way, is making enormous [?] progress and already today occupies quite an honoured place.
Here in Zagłębie, Jewish circles have completely stopped taking Hitler-land into account. People trade frankly and freely with the merchants and manufacturers there, as if nothing had happened there to our brethren. The Germans come over here and do quite tasty business, and to our great shame and disgrace the business is done almost exclusively with Jewish firms. True, some are embarrassed and do not want the public to know about it, and the Germans understand this perfectly. For business they are cunning enough and arrange matters properly, so that one cannot tell that the goods come from Hitler-land. They do it in the best order and even give you Polish labels, as long as the contact is not broken off.
We have Anti-Hitler Committees in Zagłębie, which are supposed to stand on guard and see to it that this has no place among us. And here one must ask: do these committees stand at the proper level, and do they safeguard what ought to be their task and duty? To this one must answer: no, they are far from fulfilling their responsible tasks. A separate matter is that we, the Jewish community and even the individual, are also not a little to blame for this, because just as the committee should not have been separated from the masses, so too the masses, the whole community as such, should have stood in close contact with the leading committee members. But since the community does not understand its tasks and does not insist that the committees properly fulfil their duty-laden tasks... Moreover, only the single Będzin committee comes into consideration, because Sosnowiec until not long ago did not by any means want to decide to set up such a committee. But now that we also have such a committee in Sosnowiec, it would be possible to work together much better and more strongly. For there were, for example, cases in which goods were brought from Będzin [?] and immediately transferred to Sosnowiec, so that in Będzin nobody knew about it at all, and so it was also the other way round. Thus the contact between the two towns was lacking — towns which are closely knit together both geographically and in commerce. One may say that Będzin and Sosnowiec are exactly [?] like one big city, whose committee is active in one quarter and not in the other. So it is no wonder if the Będzin committee did not have the possibility to concentrate the work.
The situation looks quite different now, when we already have such a committee active in Sosnowiec as well; in that case it will be possible to concentrate forces and to set up planned activity, which should serve the benefit of the Jewish community and the honour of the Jewish people.
There are no two opinions about it: in the face of a government we are weak and inferior to the highest degree; we do not want to doubt this for a single minute, we know it perfectly well; but one must take stock of the situation: firstly, we have no other way out, and secondly, in the course of the year we have shown the world that we are not at all so helpless and that we have influence — to such an extent that the mighty German industry, the commercial world and the Leipzig World Fair have suffered deadly blows; to such an extent that already now, while they are still engaged in the holy race-work that is supposed to bring salvation to the German people, they are nevertheless not ashamed to invite the Jews of the whole world and to tell them that they are welcome and that they will be granted all conditions, as long as exports are not stopped. Evidently, in the course of the year they have seen enough that this weak weapon of ours is enough for them to break the Hitler regime. Otherwise they would surely not have shown us any sympathy; and according to their tactics, according to the bitter hatred of Jews, which consists in "destroying him", as they proclaim at every opportunity and in all circumstances, they would by no means have needed to want to trade with any Jewish firm whatsoever, wherever it may be. And had it [Germany] not considered this dangerous for itself, such a law would no doubt have been officially issued.
The conclusion, then, is that Germany as an export country must have its exports and cannot manage without Jewish help; this one sees [?] plainly. It is clear to every conscious businessman.
Of course, we should not talk ourselves into too much; we must not overestimate our fairly weak forces too much, we must not do so either for ourselves or for others; on the other hand, we must not help to destroy ourselves, to kill ourselves, to put a rope around our own necks.
Those of our brethren who trade with Hitler-Germany today — they help to destroy the Jewish people, they help with their own hands to put a rope around their own necks and those of their own brethren, in order to kill them; and this is done with the sole awareness that German articles now come out cheaper. So the appetites for money cannot be sated. And let the danger of the destruction of the Jewish people grow greater and more dangerous — it does not bother these dregs of society; they give themselves no account of any of it.
But the question arises: what will our Anti-Hitler Committees in Zagłębie do with these defilers? And what will we [printed: "help"], the Jewish people, do with such "brothers in the flesh" of our own? What sort of Jews are these, when they sell the whole Jewish people for a pot of lentils, for mere pennies? Can such creatures be counted as our brethren? Must not the Jewish community distance itself from them?
And therefore a duty lies on our local committees, first and foremost, to register these defilers of the Jewish people, to follow them, to take all possible measures in order to influence them, to explain what crime they commit by trading in goods stained with Jewish blood; and if the measures taken do not move their cold hearts, then the committees should react as they ought, and Jewish Zagłębie will surely conform to the adopted resolutions and shun those who are not with the people, who go against it and against its most vital existential interests [literally "bloodiest"] as soon as their pocket, their penny, is concerned.
The committees have adopted resolutions, first and foremost, to publish in the columns of our newspaper the firms that trade with Hitler-Germany. We will gladly fulfil their demands and put in the pillory those who have relations with the Nazi Germans. We for our part must have no dealings whatsoever with the defilers of the Jewish people. We must not come within their four cubits, we must not stretch out a hand to them; for us they must not exist as brethren.
There is therefore no doubt that the committees must stand on guard and see to it that German goods are not brought in by various routes. The truth must be told: our committees have taken the question too lightly, and it has thus been neglected to such a degree that the smuggler, the dealer and the merchant are sure that they commit no crime whatsoever thereby; therefore this opinion must be uprooted, and the individuals must be told what it is they are doing.
In order to safeguard all this properly, one must first of all see to it that the committees are set on a firm basis, both in Będzin and in Sosnowiec. There must be both cash and human material; the latter is actually more important — the most important thing for the committees. If they lack people, let them co-opt such, and those who will take the mission upon themselves should remember [?] that they must fulfil it; if not, they had better not accept it at all, because in that case they do nothing and others do not take their place.
As we have thus shown above, with our modest, poor forces we are in a position to do something, and, as we see, the world reckons with this "something" of ours, so that we must certainly take it into account and act both inwardly and outwardly. We must not let ourselves lose heart; we must do what we can, what is in our possession [?] and ability.
For purely understandable reasons we must now preserve and strengthen the Anti-Hitler Committees, in which persecutions of Jews should be recorded, to which one must react. The committees thus have more than enough work, and they must stand in close contact with the people. We must therefore guard and strengthen the committees, and they must be given the possibility of protecting our human and national interests.
The people must therefore be for the committees, and the committees — for the people.
R. Let.
No More Pedigree...

[Satirical feuilleton — artificial insemination.]

In short — we are already getting to the point where children will be born without a father...

You have surely read in the newspapers about the new artificial method of impregnating women, so that they need not have recourse to a man should they take a fancy to having a child.

Thirteen children have already been born that way in America without a father lately, and over the years the number of fatherless children will grow and grow.

It is becoming a very simple matter: if a girl or a young wife wants a child and a comfort in her old age, she goes to a laboratory and starts getting pregnant from science...

An end to barrenness, an end to childlessness! Woman strides with firm steps towards progress! Until now she has waged all her battles against man for independence and always come out the winner, but her latest victory is the greatest of all victories!

And the greater the victory of the female world, the greater the defeat of the male sex. Until now a man could lord it over his wife, he could stick his thumbs into his waistcoat pockets and proclaim himself before her tsar and master, he was the very top of the heap [?]... No small thing — a pair of trousers! The father of mankind! Without him the world could not have existed! How many millions he used to have hauled out in dowry for impregnating the daughters of anxious fathers and mothers, and how hard it used to be until at last they managed to break in [?] the creature — under the wedding canopy...

But now — wszystko skończone [everything is over], it is all finished. An end, a finish. The role of the man is a thing of the past, his mission is ended — no more pedigree in the world.

And if a man does get married after all in the future, his sole task will be to make a living — the laboratory will take care of the children...

* * *

Let us just try to treat the matter precisely [?] and in order:

If a child has no father, then the child is, of course, an orphan. It follows that every child who comes into the world by the means of the laboratory is born a ready-made orphan.

And that is the greatest sorrow and the great misfortune of the future: the whole world will become one big orphanage, for which the generosity of the Sosnowiec rich men will not suffice.

And another trouble: until now a grown-up child could expect a big, fat inheritance from a father deceased after a hundred and twenty years, but a laboratory child cannot expect any inheritance.

* * *

And now just imagine what future generations will look like: you will not be able to say of anyone that he is "a father's child"; one will not be able to mark this one or that one as a grandson of the Fürstenbergs or of the Gerer Rebbe — all pedigree will go back solely to the machine, and if the machines have numbers, one will at most be able to say that he descends from "apparatus number 714" or some other number, nothing more.

The whole world will have a glass past.

* * *

Among Jews these reforms will cause a complete upheaval. Old customs and traditions will be wiped out. Here, for instance, a Jewish boy will become bar mitzvah, and can you imagine how it will sound when the shammes calls out at the summons to the Torah:

— "Ya'amod, the youth Zalman son of the laboratory — maftir!"

And who will say the "Blessed be He who has released me from the punishment of this one" [misprinted "menshu shalvah"]? And who will hand out lekakh [honey cake] and brandy?

And not only customs and traditions will be changed — the whole holy Torah will have to be rewritten. Even the Ten Commandments will have to adapt themselves to the new times; you may expect that some time later the Torah reader, reading the portion of Yitro, will sway over the Torah scroll and chant with the cantillation:

— "Honour the laboratory and thy mother, that thy days may be long..."

* * *

One of the doctors whom I asked about artificial pregnancy explained that the whole business is old, that in America it has already been practised for over thirty years, and that the method has been known in the world for the last two thousand years.

And if it is true that laboratory children already existed two thousand years ago, it may also be true that the whole of mankind arose from an artificial pregnancy.

In this way Jews have suffered greatly because of the artificial pregnancy of two thousand years ago, and that is why I am indeed afraid that the new artificial pregnancies may also bring us a lot of trouble. In other words it means that it is not good for the Jews.

It may also be possible that the children who will now be born of artificial pregnancy will grow up to be gods, and then it will be an entirely different world — every person will be a god unto himself and will be able to worship himself alone.

(There are people who worship only themselves as it is. — Remark by the typesetter lad.)

And if the gods cannot agree about "peace on earth", they will probably make war and tear out each other's beards. But that, you see, no longer bothers me. When gods quarrel, it is no worry of my grandmother's.

My only worry is that the laboratory will in the end destroy mankind, and that would be a catastrophe, because together with mankind my bit of immortality, for whose sake I live and toil, would also be destroyed.

But before the end of the world and of mankind comes, have, meanwhile, a good Shabbes.

Tz. H. Rubinsztajn.
Back to Work!

[Zagłębie — anti-German boycott; article.]
Remarks on the halted anti-Hitlerite economic boycott action in Zagłębie.
1.
For 14 months the Jewish people has been waging a stubborn struggle against one of the greatest enemies our martyrological history has ever known. A large part of the German people, led and misled by its chancellor Adolf Hitler, is conducting a planned, merciless policy of extermination towards its Jewish fellow citizens.
The bloody anti-Jewish struggle is not confined to the borders of the German state alone. Hitler and his followers hate not only the German Jews; he strives with his "idea" to conquer the whole world. Hitler is fighting "world Jewry".
The poisoned arrows of Hitler's camps[?] unfortunately fall on favourable soil in various countries.
The form of the swastika may change at times into the shape of a lightning bolt, or into another sign; the brown shirts may at times take on a cherry colour, or another colour. But the content, the essence, the poison of hatred and enmity towards the Jew remains unchanged.
Sharing in the physical and moral sufferings of the German Jews and duly appraising the danger that threatens the whole of Israel from its German enemies, the Jewish people throughout the world declared a struggle against the Hitlerite regime and recognised, as one of the means of struggle, an unconditional boycott of German goods and German services.
2.
World Jewry has passed the examination brilliantly. Everywhere where there is a more or less sizeable Jewish community, a boycott committee has been founded, which stands guard over Jewish honour and does not permit any import of German goods. Proud and conscious Jewish firms are breaking off their business relations of many years with German factories.
One sometimes even pays higher prices in other countries, one sometimes accepts lovingly goods of poor quality, but one does not want to know of any German "bargains", which are stained with the blood and tears of our tormented brothers. The boycott is a duty of honour of every hundred-percent Jew, and in paying debts of honour one does not calculate and one does not reckon whether the "business" pays or not...
3.
The Hitlerite government has been feeling for some months already the great counter-pressure exerted on it by the worldwide Jewish boycott. It is already speaking ever louder and more clearly about the enormous damage caused to it by the boycott of German goods, and about the catastrophic fall of German exports, which threatens an increase in unemployment and a collapse of the entire economic life in Germany.
But "the wicked do not repent even at the gates of Gehenna": instead of repenting and changing the antisemitic course, they try to go on terrorising the unfortunate hostage, the German Jew, and in this way to influence the sense of pity of world Jewry so that it gives up the boycott.
But the Jewish blockade of German exports will not be weakened because of the new persecutions of Jews in "Hitleria". On the contrary — everywhere there is a tendency to sharpen the boycott and to fight the modern inquisitors until a final victory.
Whoever reads the press attentively knows that the boycott is being conducted very energetically along the whole length of the front, and that the struggle is growing stronger and more intensive.
4.
And in Zagłębie?
Zagłębie, together with the first towns in Poland, reacted to the cries of woe of our brothers who find themselves in the Hitlerite hell: committees were founded to conduct the anti-Hitlerite economic action. The Będzin committee set to very energetic work and showed rare initiative and self-sacrificing activity. Various branch sections were founded, a large number of consultations were held and a very ramified correspondence was developed with many economic institutions.
The result was a gratifying one. At various conferences the voice of the Będzin committee was taken into account, and it was honoured with compliments for its splendid organisation. But the enthusiasm for the work, the joy of creation, lasted in all one "season"; the fervour began to die out, until of the committees and their work, especially in Sosnowiec, there remained a [—] [—] [—] [—] to a complete falling asleep of a useful institution which at the beginning had shown so much life and liveliness. It is a fact that for several months the committee has been almost no longer active.
And the result? Complete lack of discipline, an intensified lawlessness in various irresponsible circles; goods from Germany are brought in quite comfortably by the wagonload, people have lost[?] the sense of shame and do "business" with our mortal enemies.
I therefore turn to the representatives of the Zagłębie Jewish economic organisations with the proposal to put an end as quickly as possible to the present catastrophic[?] state of affairs, which is a desecration of God's name (chillul ha-Shem) for the commercial and industrial spheres. You, responsible economic leaders, have the duty to rehabilitate the good name of the Zagłębie Jewish merchant, by taking over the leadership of the boycott action and continuing the activity which has been paralysed for some time.
No problem whatsoever is at the present moment as topical as the struggle for Jewish honour. And on the other hand there are not many such actions that are as rewarding as this one.
So — get to work!
Resign Your Mandates

[Będzin — City council elections; open letter.] An unheard-of scandal! A scandal without equal in the history of elections! Our faces burn with shame and our hearts contract with grief. This is a spit in the face of the entire Jewish population of Będzin — by our own representatives, by the lawlessness and demoralisation that now reign in the Jewish street.
For the latest city council elections, which have only just taken place, we created a National-Economic Bloc, and taking into account the grave, bitter hour of destiny that Jewry is living through — when thousands of Jewish livelihoods burst like soap bubbles, when Jews are systematically pushed out of trade, crafts and work, when there is an enormous mass of people left without trade and without work, and now, when before our very eyes a mighty antisemitic intrigue is being woven that threatens to swallow and destroy us — in this grave hour of destiny we understood — knowing that the city council is a strong power and an important factor in public life, that the city council must look after a good and sound economy, the school system and the education of the coming generation, and must satisfy the cultural and social needs of the population — we understood that we must elect a Jewish representation able, both by its authority and by its Jewish national consciousness, to defend the vital (lit. "blood") Jewish interests, and able to demand proudly, courageously and with dignity what is due to the Jews as citizens with equal rights, as citizens who bear all the duties and demand their rights as well.
It goes without saying that as first candidate we considered our meritorious public worker of many years, the well-known Sejm deputy of many years, Dr. Weinzieher, highly esteemed everywhere. We approached him with our proposal. Although Dr. Weinzieher had decided years ago not to take any part in political life any more — now, bearing in mind the difficult situation in which Jewry finds itself and how badly strong characters, intellectual forces and self-sacrificing people are needed precisely now, he gave up his earlier decision and magnanimously accepted our proposal — to our greatest satisfaction.
As we have already mentioned above, we had created a National-Economic Bloc, which the Revisionist representatives also joined — but unfortunately they are irresponsible people, for whom the seat stands higher than the most painful Jewish interests, and who firmly hold to the Jesuit principle that the end justifies the means. And these irresponsible people — and the young men of Torah va-Avodah followed their example — robbed [?] our first, finest and most meritorious citizen, Dr. Weinzieher, and dishonoured and defiled his honour.
What, in fact, did they do?
One's face simply burns with shame to answer this question, but we must make it public: let society judge them and brand them, and let society take account of our decline, of the terrible demoralisation and lawlessness now reigning in the Jewish street, and ask [?] into what deep abyss this can hurl us!
And here is what happened: although we Zionists noticed from the very first moment that they were weaving a net behind our backs, that they were not loyal to our bloc, and we drew attention to it many times and warned the chairman of the committee, Mr. Rubinlicht, that they would lead him into a swamp from which he would no longer be able to get out — they were so crafty that they simply blinded Mr. Rubinlicht, and he noticed nothing until the very last minute. They supposedly "handed over" [sic] and helped with the technical work and with sending more than four thousand ballot papers and propaganda material to all the Jewish citizens, on which, naturally, their candidates also figured; but last Saturday night, when we met after the last rally, we learned — to our greatest surprise and shock — that the Revisionists had betrayed us in an ugly and shameful way: namely, already on Thursday they had printed their own ballot papers, on which their candidate, Mr. Montag, figured eighteen times. The betrayal becomes even uglier and more shameful in that, having already cheated our four thousand votes, which belonged to our respected first candidate Dr. Weinzieher and also to Mr. Jakub Gutman, they still had the nerve to come on Saturday night to the last meeting of the committee, supposedly as innocent lambs, "to help" send out the rest of the material with the ballot papers, on which their representative figured, so as to secure their "victory" all the more.
And their "victory" did indeed come: they "grabbed" mandates — but do you know at whose expense? At the expense of the defiled honour of our highly esteemed, meritorious and long-serving public worker, Dr. Weinzieher!
Our Dr. Weinzieher remained "outside", and the representatives of the Revisionists and of Torah va-Avodah got "in". Great is the grief, and greater still the shame!
And therefore we turn to you, highly respected and meritorious Mrs. Z. Szajn and Mr. Rubinlicht:
Do not accept the mandates in the city council, because they have been defiled by the defiled honour of Dr. Weinzieher, so highly esteemed by all of us.
I believe that I express the opinion of the whole progressive, conscious and national Jewish society, which will in this way express its protest and verdict against the traitors — if you, the representatives of Jewish Będzin, do not accept your mandates!
Your honour and the honour of Jewish Będzin demand that you not sit in the city council together with the seat-grabbers at the expense of Jewish interests!
Y. Wygodzki.
Election Snapshots.

Snapped up by Ben Amoz.
"It is time to act for the Lord"...
The election campaign in the streets — a weak one; the old fervour is gone. The former interest has been lost; "against your will you live" — and "against your will" one goes to the elections. One does it to fulfil an obligation, a second — to do a good friend a favour, and a third — to save the prestige of his party.
The only ones making "atmosphere" are the "Agudah"; with that party the well-known methods were kept up in these elections too, in all their fine points and details: not only the older members — dozens of cheder boys and young lads were sent out into the streets, and they took part in the holy work with Agudist enthusiasm.
— But you are transgressing a prohibition of the Torah — says a Radomsk Hasid to one of the active Agudah men.
— Never mind — answers the Agudist — for Abraham Leib to become a councillor ("ratman") it is worth even setting aside the Torah; it is, after all, an explicit verse:
— "It is time to act for the Lord; they have made void Thy Torah"...
"I want the President"...
A family quarrel on Sanczewska [?] Street. Taking part in this "spectacle" are a mother and 2 children, a son and a daughter.
— "I don't need no party" ["patey"] — the mother shouts — "I want the President."
— And what is your quarrel about? — I ask the woman, whose face bears witness that [—] [doubtful reading].
— "You see, these are my children; they are in the party, and they tell me to vote for the party [—] — they say — they're going to Palestine; but I don't want party stuff [?], only the President. I even have complaints against him: more than once he would not hear me out and left me standing for hours behind the door of his office in the Magistrat, but still I want to give him my vote
— 'I want the President'..."
"We'll stay with the child"... [Polish: "My będziemy przy dziecku"]
2 young lads with long [?] sidelocks over their ears come into a flat on 3rd of May Square [Plac 3 Maja].
The children of the household are not at home. [—]
[—]
The Christian servant, an elderly gentile woman, whom the lads set about persuading to go and vote...
At first the "Agudist goye" won't listen to what the young "Żydki" [little Jews] are saying to her:
— "Don't bother me, I have no time" [Polish: "Nie zawracajcie mi głowy, nie mam czasu"].
But when they deliver a "speech" [Polish mowa] to her and give her to understand that if she does what they ask, the Lord God [Pan Bóg] will repay her twice over, the Christian woman agrees. But — she says — if she leaves the little child, the lady will surely be angry with her.
— "I'd go already — she says — but the child" [Polish: "Poszłabym już, ale dziecko"].
— Nonsense — explain the Hasidic lads — we have a remedy for that too:
— "Let the lady go and vote, and we'll stay here with the child" [Polish: "Niech pani idzie głosować, a my będziemy tu przy dziecku"]...
"Vote me in" ["Makhts mekh"].
In the present elections most of the "leading" [Polish czołowe] candidates used the American system — went out onto the street themselves and worked on their own behalf.
— 18 times "turnus" [?]!
At the corner of [—] and Małachowskiego Streets stands the main figure of the [—] [line hidden by a fold in the page] [—]; his angry [?] glances fall on Jews, passers-by, and whoever finds favour in his eyes he honours with a ballot slip, saying the words:
— "Vote me in"...
He, the candidate, fulfils a second mission as well: he is the commander of the little band of cheder boys who come running to him so that he will give them the ballot slips.
He beams with pride at them; he places great hopes in the little army, which will bring victory to the Agudah.
— Here you are, children; don't dawdle [bałamucić], run into all the houses, crawl into all the cellars, and remember
— "Vote me in."
"It's already after Yom Kippur."
Coming to Sosnowiec on election day, I had the impression that I had landed in Geneva, the city of "peace".
Such a cosy atmosphere, such living together with one another — so that the pavement on Modrzejowska [?] Street "spoke" of peace.
But the disappointment soon came. The first person of the "peaceful city" whom I "congratulated", instead of answering me "Aleichem shalom", told me the following anecdote:
— Motl [?] — he says — 2 bitter enemies made peace on Yom Kippur, shook hands and wished each other all the best.
At the close of Yom Kippur, in the middle of the night, one enemy knocks at the other's window and announces to him that the peace is over — war again.
— What has happened again? — wonders the other — how so [?], we made peace.
— True, we made peace, but that was on Yom Kippur, whereas today
— "it's already after Yom Kippur"...
He is "insured"...:
An agitator of the Jewish list in Dąbrowa is leading a voter, a young man who is already far, far away from the bourgeois world, so far that he already looks with both eyes towards Moscow.
— What are you agitating him for? He's from the party that runs away from the "Jewish [—]" ["pshium"?] like a devil from incense!
— Rest assured — the agitator triumphs — I am a hundred-percent believer that he will vote for Neufeld; I searched all his pockets and found no other ballot slip, yes
— "I'm insured" [?]...
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Beha'alotcha)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion (Beha'alotcha).] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Beha'alotcha
The Portion
—o—
a) "And we will do thee good" (Num. 10:32)
Jethro did not want to go with Moses to the Land of Israel, although Moses had told him "for the Lord hath spoken good concerning Israel", because he thought to himself: what can be called "good", a good thing, for this wandering tribe, for the Jews! They[?], whose lot is so bad and dark that for them a ray of light is like a sun...
To this Moses told him: "And we will do thee good." We have a promise[?] to settle ourselves there in such a way that even for you, Jethro, who have a home, it too will be called good. Not merely a ray, but really a sun...
Imrei Mordechai.
* * *
"When the Lord turned again the captivity of Zion... then said they among the nations, The Lord hath done great things for these; the Lord hath done great things for us" (Psalm 126).
Jews will build themselves such a Zion that not only for us, the homeless, will it be a great thing, but even for them, for the nations, it will be a great thing. They too will say "The Lord hath done great things for us, then we were glad", for even if a land-owning people were to receive such a built-up land, for them too it would have been "The Lord hath done great things"...
Chen Tov.
b) "And the mixed multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again" (Num. 11:4)
The children of Israel, the "fine Jews" [the respectable ones], always send the mixed multitude (asafsuf) ahead. The rabble makes the uproar, and only afterwards "the children of Israel also wept". But behind the rabble there always stand the fine Jews...
Ktav Sofer.
c) "There is nothing at all, beside this manna, before our eyes" (ibid. 6)
One of the Arab caliphs had a Jewish physician, Rabbenu Meshullam. Once the caliph said to him: just look how ungrateful the Jews were in the wilderness. They had the manna, in which one could taste whatever flavour one wished, and yet they longed for the cucumbers, melons and onions — for the sake of an onion they made such a revolution!
R' Meshullam gave the caliph no answer at all, but went to the master cook and ordered him no longer to season the caliph's dishes with the various vegetables with which one flavours, for example, a broth. The unseasoned dishes did not taste good to the caliph, and he complained to his personal physician as to why he had imposed such a strict diet on him. If the food is not seasoned with the proper vegetables, the whole food has no taste.
— Now Your Majesty the caliph will understand — R' Meshullam answers jestingly — why the Jews in the wilderness were not satisfied with the manna, although it comprised all dishes in itself, and why they longed so much for the onions and cucumbers. You know, after all, that without seasoning no dish has any taste.
Tzror HaMor.
* * *
R' Yaakov Emden wrote a book "Lechem Shamayim" ("Bread of Heaven"), in remembrance of the manna, in which one could taste all sorts of flavours... Once an ignoramus (am ha'aretz) said to him:
— Rabbi, in the "HaMotzi" blessing one does not say "bread from heaven" but "bread from the earth".
R' Yaakov Emden answers him:
— "Bread of heaven" is for Torah scholars, and "bread from the earth" for the ignoramuses (amei ha'aretz)...
d) "But there remained two of the men in the camp... and the spirit rested upon them" (ibid. 25 [recte 26])
Precisely those who remained in the camp, those who were the last to stay behind in the camp, who did not push themselves forward — they merited a spirit of prophecy.
Orach Chaim.
e) "Now the man Moses was very meek" (Num. 12:3)
Rabbi Mendele of Kotzk once, as was his way, picked a quarrel with a certain rebbe. The latter said to him[?]:
— Do you know who I am? I am great, and my hand reaches up to the seventh heaven.
R' Mendele had him answered:
— And I am so small that all seven heavens bow down before me.
On Summer Camps for Poor Children of Zagłębie.

[Zagłębie — article; welfare, children and summer camps.] We have already once touched on the question of summer camps from this place, in passing, when we discussed the state of Zagłębie society and illustrated its attitude to the most vital interests of the population.
The question of summer camps for Jewish children, however, deserves special attention: the end of the school year is approaching, only some 3–4 weeks of study remain, the children will be freed from the strenuous work at school — but together with that they will also lose even that part of sanitary-hygienic supervision with which the school as such concerns itself[?].
Many children, weak, anaemic, will remain stuck in the dark, often damp and stifling "dwellings", because they will have no material possibility to recuperate in the fresh air, under proper supervision and in a suitable sanitary-hygienic environment.
One must also remember that for the children of Zagłębie the summer camp has great importance, because it protects the child from serious complications and infectious diseases such as tuberculosis, etc., and not for nothing are children's camps everywhere regarded as a first-rank duty of social welfare.
In Zagłębie a large-scale campaign must absolutely be undertaken to organise the summer camps. For this purpose all possible funds for social and public aid must be used. Flower days and various other collections must be arranged.
We believe that, however hard and critical the time may be, the Jewish population of Zagłębie will nevertheless show understanding for such an important matter, and together with that it will also succeed in obtaining the necessary means that will enable a larger number of needy children to attend the camp.
Who should take the initiative for the relief work for the children's camp?
We hold that in the first place the "TOZ" [Society for the Protection of the Health of the Jewish Population] should take this up, as it already has a tradition of fruitful work in this field and has shown understanding and devotion in this field. The above-mentioned society should now too continue with fresh energy the campaign of placing as many poor children as possible in the camp.
We know very well: times today are extremely hard, and work in every public field is now thankless. But one wishes to believe that through planned and well-organised work the "TOZ" will find help and cooperation among all social strata, and with joint forces it will succeed in carrying out the campaign, which belongs among its most urgent and most important tasks.
And let the old Jewish rule apply here regarding the "TOZ":
He who begins a good deed — is told: finish it!
—M.
Andrzej Strug in Eretz Israel

[Eretz Israel — literature and Polish–Jewish relations; the visit of the writer Andrzej Strug.]
A. S. Juris.
(Special to the "Zaglembier Tsaytung").

It is surely a strange historical misunderstanding — the attitude of the Polish creative intelligentsia towards the more-than-three-million-strong community of Polish Jewry, which has lived for centuries rooted in Polish soil. Two peoples live on one ground, bound together by a thousand economic [?] threads. And yet only rarely have the Jewish mentality [?], the Jewish character, the Jewish soul, the Jewish spirituality, the Jewish human being in his true light found expression on the pages of Polish literature. Always it was Jankiels and Moszkes, but never a "Jacob" or a "Moses". Certainly there were bright exceptions — such as, for example, an Eliza Orzeszkowa [printed "Orzeszka"], but the exceptions only confirmed the rule — and the rule was either silence, or disparagement and falsification, from which even the greatest and best artists were not always free.
And one more factor. For decades a Zionist movement has existed, and colonization is under way in Eretz Israel. In this renaissance process of people and land, Polish Jewry has come to play a first-rank role. Year in, year out, Polish Jews leave in their thousands, old and young, the narrow, hopeless towns and shtetls and turn to productive work in village and town, becoming creators and builders of the Jewish national home. This tremendous social-psychological upheaval, too, has not until now found its due echo in journalism, its expression in Polish literature.
No wonder, then, that with special [?] joy the Yishuv in general, and the Polish Jews in Eretz Israel in particular, received the happy news that a poet and artist of the stature of Andrzej Strug had accepted the invitation of the "Keren Hayesod" and come to see our work with his own eyes and his own heart.
Polish literature could not have found a better choice than to send precisely Andrzej Strug as its first spiritual ambassador to Eretz Israel. For the ideology of the new Poland is so similar to our ideology — and the struggle for Poland's freedom so akin [?] to our struggle. And most important: Poland went through a national tragedy: the three partitions and unfreedom for over a century — and the Polish intelligentsia — the best poets, thinkers and fighters — went through its "Galut" [exile]. This tragedy and this exile created a Polish ideology so blood-akin to our ideal of renaissance. The Polish idea of freedom became saturated with prophetic elements — and the dream of the freedom fighters was that a Poland rising anew from the dead [?] should be a redemption not only for the Poles but also for all of mankind. This is how one must understand the "messianism" in Polish literature, Poland as the "Winkelried of the nations" — in Słowacki, the messianism [?] in Mickiewicz, which led him even as far as founding a Jewish legion for the liberation of Eretz Israel for the Jewish people.
This Polish freedom-romanticism passes by inheritance to the P.P.S. [Polish Socialist Party], whose ideology Andrzej Strug helped to hammer out and to create. In the ideology of the P.P.S., in its heroic struggle for Polish independence and its simultaneous struggle for social justice, the echo of Polish romanticism and of the Polish "diaspora" resounds very strongly. And who, if not a romantic Polish socialist and poet, is able to understand and to compare with that which is happening in our own land — for it is precisely the Halutz movement that undertook not only to revive the petrified, swamped land, but also to carry out a deep social-psychological revolution in Jewish life by transferring the Jewish masses, first and foremost the Jewish youth, to productive work in town and village — and last but not least, — by building a new and just social order.
The expectations were fulfilled in full measure. Strug had the opportunity to see the land from Dan to Beersheba. I had the good fortune and honour of accompanying him on his wanderings through the Jewish homeland. He saw the youth from the small Polish shtetls on the fields of the Jezreel Valley [printed "Yorael"], he saw the Hasidim of Jabłonna by the Kishon stream as simple farm labourers, he saw Jewish daughters, so well known in Polish literature, preparing themselves at "Hallel" [probably Nahalal] for hard work on the land; he saw Upper Galilee redeemed by the Shomrim workers, and the Sharon, the work of the Polish Jews. Each time a new page and a precious miracle revealed itself to him. He was the guest of the whole Yishuv — especially of those who come from Poland. Whether at the first reception, at a Keren Hayesod banquet in Jerusalem, or the Shomer kvutza "Morah" [probably Mizra] or "Mishmar HaEmek", or the delegation of Polish rabbis in Safed and Meron, or a reception at the PEN Club, or a gathering in Haifa, or his May Day appearance in Tel Aviv — every encounter with Strug was one great holiday — and with Strug.
There is no doubt — and Strug's several public appearances are the best proof of it [?] — that in Strug we have won a warm and devoted friend for our cause. On the basis of his creative intuition he quickly found his way among our achievements, problems and worries. The boundaries of race and language were blurred. Strug wandered here through towns and villages like a deeply moved [?] brother, rejoicing in our joy and grieving in our grief. Most of all he was captivated by the miracle of liberated labour — and the miracle of the revived language. And there is no doubt that the misunderstanding and unfamiliarity which have disturbed a peaceful understanding between the Jewish and the Polish peoples, who have lived, live and will yet live for a long time on one ground — that this will be changed for the good and the better along the paths of the spirit, because when Jews become a normal people in a land of their own, normal peoples begin to understand us and to perceive us as equal and equal-valued human beings. That is the great miracle of a renewed people on renewed soil. In this sense Strug's visit will be an important cornerstone in the Jewish–Polish problem, on the road to mutual understanding.

And Mr. Cossack Is Not Ashamed

[Essay — Jews and Germany; the boycott.] A strange people, we Jews — so abstractly lost in the clouds, so unrealistic, and — so naive. A people that still believes in miracles. As "old Saul of Tarsus," the "Pharisee, disciple of Pharisees," said when he grew angry with his former colleagues: the Greeks want proofs[?], the Jews seek signs and wonders. And whether it is a Jew of old or one of the modern ones — in the hour of trial the old optimism awakens in him, the old faith in — the miracle.
Do you remember the old saying of the German Jew who was a witness or a victim of Cossack brutality? He gave the Cossack a look with stern, reproachful eyes and said to him: "Shame on you, Mr. Cossack." He said it — and waited for the miracle, but the miracle did not happen. The Cossack was not ashamed. He did not even blush. He merely burst into wild laughter[?] — and his answer was — the nagaika, the whip.
The Jews console themselves: never mind. Some day a day will surely come when Mr. Cossack will after all be ashamed; if not today, then tomorrow, if not — then at the end of days.
But that too is an illusion. Mr. Cossack is not ashamed — not even after generations upon generations. Here we read in our books, in the pinkasim and chronicles of the Khmelnytsky era, about the terrors and horrors of the massacres the Haidamaks perpetrated, about the countless Jewish victims who fell — so we read, and naively think that the grandchildren of the Haidamaks read it too and also feel a moral revulsion, because — why, how could it be otherwise?
Mr. Cossack is not ashamed of his yesterday, and still less of his today.
Here we stand now in the midst of a bitter struggle, not begun by us, forced upon us. A people has risen against us, a people with mighty fists and hobnailed boots, a people without mercy and without a soul.
A war at home, a war all over the world; everywhere there are Germans they conduct an embittered anti-Jewish propaganda, incite to pogroms and annihilation.
Incomprehensible — from our standpoint, beyond the grasp of reason, whence and why such hatred. But the fact remains: there is no other people in the world so stubbornly antisemitic as the Germans. A danger to the whole world. It is not at all hard to persuade anyone whatsoever that one must hate Jews. And we know, after all: "In the beginning was the Word"; the fist and the boot come later.
Must one defend oneself? Can one stand up to them with a little Book of Psalms and the "Pachad Yitzchak" in hand, and preach morals to Mr. Cossack? Or must one also become active — set might against[?] might, put out the fire not with magic spells but with water?
When we come to Jews, wherever they may be, and tell him: defend yourself as best you can, and defend yourself so that the other feels it. The Cossack beats. But the next day he comes to you and sells you his goods — do not buy from him. Perhaps he will suffer from it — why not? Why should he not feel the bitterness of life? Why should he not feel the effect of his own deeds? And when on the German ships Hitler gangs are organised among the sailors and the ship's staff — when a Jewish passenger is not sure that he will not be insulted, mistreated, in the middle of the sea, when he is not sure of his life among Germans — should one not tell him, the Jew: avoid German ships?
And when Jews are in the most terrible danger in German towns and villages, should one perhaps not tell the Jew from Poland: do not travel to Germany, let your foot not cross the threshold of a German spa?
And when Jews are thrown out of all professions, out of trade and production — have we no right to tell the Jewish person: "an eye for an eye" — that is, the "for an eye" — money for an eye? Who will suffer from it when Jews will not buy German goods, not patronise German firms? The German manufacturers who stand behind Hitler, the German industrialists who support his wickedness, the German merchants who all over the world are the carriers of antisemitism.
People answer: it is a stick with two ends. Today against Germany — tomorrow others against us. But is that stick not used against us day in, day out? Does not, in the end, the whole Jewish livelihood consist in our supporting one another — has not "go and earn your living from one another" become a reality?
And even if there were such a danger — can one sacrifice everything, honour, dignity, character? Everything that is dear to a person — for a couple of złoty? Is that not "for the sake of life to lose[?] the savour of life"?
And I want to ask: can a Jew really sit and enjoy Wagner's music, melt away in German-Germanic sentimentality, knowing all the while that this is the music of a man who hated the Jew to the blood? And can one applaud Mr. Richard Strauss, who was not ashamed to take over Bruno Walter's post and did not even protest?
Yes — it is high time that the Jewish people reorientated itself; it has lived too long in the sphere of Eastern European[?] culture. Too long Russian, German, above all German. There is no need at all for the Jews of Prague still to parade their German language and culture, to pride themselves on it.
It should have been so long ago. Political reason should have dictated it to the Jews of the new states in Europe. But the force of inertia was too great, and old habits are not overcome so quickly.
Now comes necessity and breaks up[?] the old, intimate fellowship of the Jews with the German and Germandom.
The curse of Balaam is what they want — the majority of the German people, the spreaders of poison all over the world — we turn the point around, and — Balaam's magic word falls back. And when Mr. von Cossack comes to feel the bitterness of being alone — the tragedy of loneliness — perhaps then he will be ashamed, but not before.
Dr. A. Coralnik.

[Advertorial — Radion.] With such words[?] the housewife receives every piece of news from which she learns that it helps her save time, work and money. That is why she greeted with grateful joy the appearance of small packets of Radion, which are brought to her for only 45 gr. Radion is a product that washes by itself. Radion for 45 gr. washes plenty of handkerchiefs, collars and other small things, which otherwise would have lain waiting for a big wash.

Boarding house for out-of-town pupils at the crafts school in Piotrków Trybunalski

[Piotrków — education; vocational school and boarding house.] The Piotrków [Piotrków Trybunalski] crafts school of the Society for the Spread of Crafts and Agricultural Work among Jews — licensed by the Ministry of Education — is holding a new enrolment for its departments of mechanical locksmithing and furniture joinery.
The course in each trade lasts 3 years.
Boys aged 14 to 17 are admitted.
Attached to the crafts school there is a boarding house for out-of-town pupils, where for a modest sum — at cost price — they receive full daily board and lodging and are under the supervision of the school director.
In the current school year the boarding house held pupils from a whole series of towns, such as Warsaw [Warszawa], Poznań, Kielce, Będzin, Włocławek, Ostrowiec and others.
Applications for admission to the new school year 1934/35 must be accompanied by a birth certificate (metryka) and a school report.
On completing the school and passing the examinations, the graduates receive the "czeladniczy patent" [journeyman's certificate].
Detailed information can be obtained from the school office: Piotrków-Tryb. ul. Leonarda 12, on sending a postage stamp.
The False Messiah (3)

[Serialized historical tale — David Alroy, the false messiah; installment 3.]
Sh. Berg.

In anger Rabbi Shmuel drove him out.
He could no longer, and did not want to, stay in Baghdad. Before leaving he comforted Menuha and told her:
"The time has not yet come for me to reveal my secret to you. But know that I will come with an army to take you."
David Alroy went back to Amadiya, withdrew from people and went off into the mountains. For several years he sat in a cave [?] with a kabbalist and immersed himself in the secret lore.
And when he felt that he was already saturated with the knowledge of the secret lore, he returned to his uncle, the "Rosh ha-Golah" [Exilarch] of Persia. He arrived on the day when his uncle, in a great parade, was bringing the Jewish tribute to the Persian sultan. Everyone was sure that the heir to the Jewish princely seat, David Alroy, would take part in the parade, ride beside his uncle and be presented to the sultan. But he stayed at home; the people murmured in astonishment. When his uncle returned from the sultan, he reproached him for it.
"I do not want to be a slave," David Alroy sharply answered his uncle. "You are no prince, only the sultan's slave; he forces you to flay the skin of your own brothers for him; you wring heavy taxes from your brothers on his behalf. You are no nasi [prince] — a slave is what you are!"
The uncle did not get angry with him, but told him that in former times the "Rosh ha-Golah", forged in chains, used to bring the tribute to the sultan. Today it is done with honour. But David Alroy told him that once only the body had been forged in chains, while the soul was free. The Jews longed for freedom. Now they no longer long for freedom.
And when the uncle told him that he himself would after all one day become "Rosh ha-Golah", David Alroy leapt up, aflame, and said:
"I will not be 'Rosh ha-Golah'! I will be the head of the Redemption [Rosh ha-Geulah]! I will redeem my people!"
And soon David Alroy took the first step on his road of uprising and redemption. Outside the town there was a tomb where, the people believed, Mordecai and Esther lie. In the evening the young Jewish daughters used to come there and play. David Alroy liked to go to that tomb. So he went there, lost in his dreams, and suddenly he heard a terrible scream.
The ruler of the town, the sultan's younger brother, had burst in among the Jewish girls and seized one of them. David Alroy knew that no words would have any effect. He had to act, and he swiftly drew his sword and plunged it into the ruler's heart. The ruler's bodyguard threw itself on David Alroy. But they fell to the ground in terror, for suddenly David Alroy vanished; he spoke to them, they heard his voice, but him they did not see.

David Alroy takes the sultan's wives captive.

The ruler's bodyguard lay a long time on the ground, their teeth chattering. Meanwhile the Jewish girls ran back into town and no harm befell them.
Like wildfire the news spread through the town. The Jews rejoiced that the Jewish daughter had not been defiled; but they were afraid that this would bring them great troubles — the ruler had been the sultan's brother. The sultan would take revenge on all the Jews.
Their fear was not in vain. That same night the ruler's deputy arrested the most respected Jews and the "Rosh ha-Golah" with his household. David Alroy remained at large; the sharpest spies searched for him and could not find him.
The sultan of Persia heard what had happened and burned with rage. "A dog of a Jew," he shouted, "a base [?] slave has murdered the ruler of the town, the brother of the sultan of all Persia, the king over all kings — this is outright rebellion"; the rebellious slave must be brought to him alive, he ordered, for he wanted to settle accounts with him with his own hands.
He held the arrested Jews as a pledge until he should get David Alroy into his hands. He set a deadline: if within thirty days the Jews did not deliver David Alroy to him, he would thresh the bodies of the arrested and then hang them.
The thirtieth day drew near; twenty-nine days had passed; in the prison the threshing instruments were already being prepared, gallows had begun to be built in the middle of the market — when the capital was shaken by a new surprise. The sultan raged wildly and buried his face in shame, for since Persia has existed no such thing had happened as on that morning.
The sultan's wives and concubines with the children had been taken captive. As every day, that morning they had driven out beyond the town for an outing, when an armed band attacked them, scattered the eunuchs and the soldiers, and carried off the sultan's wives and children, and no one knows where they have gone.
"I will hang [?] them all!" the sultan shouted, "the eunuchs and the soldiers and the viziers too! Such is the order that reigns in my capital!"
And as the sultan raged so and everyone in the palace had gone dumb with terror, suddenly David Alroy came in. No one had seen him enter. Rather, as if down from heaven, he appeared, and stood upright and proud before the sultan, and in a firm voice demanded:
"Sultan of Persia! I, David Alroy, king of the Jews, demand of you that you free the arrested Jews! You hold them as a pledge for my head — I have captured your household, and I hold your wives and children as a pledge until you free the innocent Jews. They are clean of sin. I killed your brother. He wanted to defile one of my sisters."
Astounded, with gaping mouth, the sultan heard out David Alroy's terrible words, and panic fell upon the courtiers.
"What is your answer, Sultan of Persia?" David Alroy asked. "I warn you. Whatever you do to the Jews, I will do to your wives and children."
For a while the sultan was silent. Suddenly he began to scream, like one out of his mind:
"Bind him! Put him in chains! Why do you stand silent and listen to a slave blaspheming the 'King over all kings'? I will exterminate you all!"

The overall result of the town-council elections in Zagłębie.

Jewish success in Sosnowiec. — 15 Jewish councillors in Będzin. — 1 in Dąbrowa. — 3 in Zawiercie. — Victory of the Sanacja. — Defeat of the Endeks.
Sunday's town-council elections in Zagłębie brought unexpected results, which should serve in future as a moral lesson: with Jewish unity one can — despite all restrictions — achieve a great deal in every field.
We saw this in the elections in Sosnowiec, the town of the „7-year war“: but as soon as a united bloc was formed, Jewish Sosnowiec achieved for the first time a victory of 10 councillors. This is a success of very great significance, because nobody, not even among the optimists, expected such Jewish representation; and had the Jewish population taken a more active part in the elections, they would have won an eleventh seat (80 votes were missing).
The victory is all the greater because the people elected are proud Jews who have the courage and are capable of coming forward with a bold word and demanding our rights.
As we already reported in our special edition, Messrs. Józef Safer, K. Kramałowski, L. Szwajcer, Herman Aliner, Zylberszlag, B. Majerczyk, M. Lubelski, S. Lejzerowicz, L. Bajtner and A. D. Kajzer[?] were elected.
List no. 1 received 24 seats, the PPS — 9 seats, the Communists — 4, and 1 little Endek...
The „Kurier Zachodni“ really cannot bear the „great injustice“ and sheds crocodile tears that the Jews received such a number of seats as they never had until today.
Great too is the disgrace of the Endek house-owners' association. An association that has existed for decades did not win a single seat, while the Jewish house-owners' association, which has existed barely a few months, will be represented by 3 of its leaders...
———
Jewish Będzin left behind it after the elections a sad chapter of immaturity, of under-development[?] and above all — of irresponsibility.
In quantity the result is a satisfactory one, one cannot deny the truth. 15 Jewish councillors are a significant victory, but in quality the line-up is a poor one; what came out is a strong body „without a head“...
It occurred to nobody that such a scandal could happen in our town: that the person who, after many interventions, had finally agreed to put forward his candidacy should, because of electoral machinations, fail to obtain the necessary number of votes — which any good-for-nothing did obtain...
Like a thunderbolt out of a clear sky the news in our special edition struck every conscious Jew, that the so esteemed and deserving communal worker had not been elected. It was unbelievable to everyone; people read the news in black and white and still did not want to believe it. It even happened that well-known Będzin communal workers came to our printing house and demanded[?] that we stop the press: „It is impossible — they shouted — that such a scandal should happen“; but when we convinced the „optimists“ with official material, they left the printing house like mute mourners...
Elected were:
From list 3 (Right Poale Zion) Aron Hampel (551 votes).
From list 4 (Bund) Dr. Perel (321 votes).
From list 5 (Bloc) L. Rubinlicht, Mrs. C. Szejn, Ch. S.[?] Zylberberg, J. Montag (1342 votes).
List 6 (Artisans) H. L. Goldsztajn, A. D. Balimowski and Ch. Jakubowicz (1220 votes). List 6 lost the fourth seat because of 2 votes; it went to the „Agudah“.
List 7 (Small Traders' Association) Gerszon Rechnik, Jehoszua Klajman (756 v.)
List 8 (New Artisans' Association) Ch. D. Grosman (510 votes). In first place had figured Mr. Efraim Klajman, but a „miracle“ happened and Mr. Grosman came out.
List 9 (Agudah) A. L. Grynwald, B. Zylberszac and Sz. Piekarski (918 votes). The victory was a foregone one. In the election campaign the „Bnos“ and the „Tseirim“ of the „Agudah“ took part, as did almost all the „9-ers“ of the Ger shtibl.
List no. 11 (Left Poale Zion) received 300 votes; it was short of a seat by no more than 7 votes.
The elections also showed sad figures — the growth of the Hitlerite gang in the Zagłębie area: on their disqualified lists many hundreds of votes were cast...
About 65 per cent of those entitled to vote took part.
Of the other, non-Jewish lists: no. 1 — 18 seats, PPS — 5, and 2 Communists.
A great „victory“ was achieved in Dąbrowa, thanks to the system of „neither mine nor thine“ (gam li gam lekha lo yihye): instead of 5—6, barely 1 Jew was elected...
The credit for this „victory“ must be ascribed to the few members of the so-called Jewish intelligentsia who remember only at election time that there is a Jewish mass; then they come to the mass and deliver „lectures“ to them (naturally also not in the Jewish language — it is hardly fitting to „lower“ oneself so...) that precisely they will be the true emissaries of the public and defenders of the people. And when the „providers of the people“ came a little too late and reached the mass on the eve of the elections, when the prospects of standing as candidates had already melted away, they called on the masses not to vote for the Jewish candidates but for a non-Jewish list — rather that than such councillors as are standing — they said, so that no Jew should be elected.
And their wish was almost fulfilled. Only one Jew was elected, Mr. Najfeld.
The „popular wrath“ also poured out on „Reden“, where the long-serving councillor Mr. L. Szczegowski was a candidate. There too Jewish hands did their work (the Zionists boast that this is their merit...) so that Mr. Szczegowski should not be elected.
During the week respected Hasidic Jews from Dąbrowa, great Torah scholars, came to the editorial office and expressed their bitterness at what had happened. It is true — they argue — that the candidates do not have one-hundred-per-cent qualifications as councillors, but where were the gentlemen doctors and dentists when the candidate lists had to be put forward? Why did they not organise any protest meetings then, rather than only on the eve of the elections? Is that honest work, when one knows for certain that 3—4 Jewish seats will be lost?
The overall result is: Sanacja — 18, PPS — 8, Communists — 3, Endeks 2 and 1 Jew.

The Będzin kehilla board permitted to collect 50 per cent of the budget.

Because of the kehilla's bad financial situation, the board turned with a request to the starosta [district governor] that he permit it to collect 50 per cent of the new budget.
The starosta granted the request and at the same time ordered that the board should submit to him a report on the income and expenditure of each month.
A group of „Brit ha-Hayal“ members travelling by car to Palestine.

This week the group of 7 „Brit ha-Hayal“ members from Warsaw, who are travelling by car to the Land of Israel, stayed in Będzin.
The group is at the same time conducting propaganda throughout Poland and founding a branch of „Brit ha-Hayal“ in every town.

The Central Merchants' Association in Warsaw is organising, on 15—31 August of this year, a trade excursion to Soviet Russia. The price of the excursion is from 570 to 870 złoty, including the passport and all expenses.

The Sosnowiec Synagogue Is Finally Getting a Repair...

[Sosnowiec — Kehilla, the synagogue.]
In the columns of our paper the worthies of Sosnowiec have more than once been called upon to bring the municipal synagogue to a decent appearance, but both the gmina [the Jewish community board] and the synagogue gabbaim made light of the matter, and the inner appearance of the synagogue became ever more wretched, so that it was simply frightful to look at the state of things in the synagogue.
This last Shavuot Rabbi Hager touched in his sermon on the synagogue question and also appealed to the worshippers that they should paint [?] the "little sanctuary" as befits a synagogue in Sosnowiec.
One of the worshippers, Reb Yehoshua Pachter, took an interest in the matter, and he decided, without the knowledge of the gmina, to paint the synagogue at his own expense.
The work began last Wednesday. Some dozory [members of the kehilla board], seeing that "their work is being done by others" — that their task is being carried out by someone who is not a dozor — dared to interfere and ordered the beadles not to let the workers in with their tools.
Mr. Pachter, who has goodwill for the cause, beat off the "attack", went into the synagogue with the workers, and the work goes on..
Tragic Death of an Unemployed Young Jewish Man near Zawiercie

[Zawiercie — accidents.]
Behind Zawiercie the dead body of an unknown young man was found. The investigation established that the deceased is a certain Moshe Pozna-ski [?] [Poznański?] from Piotrków, an unemployed man; he had no money for a ticket and travelled "na gapę" [as a fare-dodger] to Sosnowiec. At a certain moment, afraid of the ticket inspector, he jumped down from the carriage steps and fell under the wheels of a passing train, which killed him.
The tragically deceased was 22 years old.
Big Political Trial before the Local District Court / Demonstration by the Accused in the Sosnowiec Courtroom

[Sosnowiec — Court, politics (communist trial).]
Demonstration by the accused in the Sosnowiec courtroom.
On Monday a big political trial began at the local district court. On the defendants' bench sit 45 men who are accused of anti-state activity in the territory of the Zagłębie district.
In the course of Monday and Tuesday a series of witnesses supporting the indictment were heard; among the witnesses, 17 were heard who had informed the investigation office. Secret agents and informers [konfidenci][?] — former members of the Communist Party.
The chief witness is a certain Avraham Stikała, who collaborated with the accused.
After the opening of the session the witnesses are called; when Stikała appears before the court, a shout is heard from the accused: "Down with the provocateur!"
Order in the hall was soon restored thanks to the vice-chairman threatening that if the accused would not keep quiet they would be excluded from the courtroom.
After a short recess the witness Stikała was heard; he related in detail the activity and development of the Communist Party in the Zagłębie territory and the function of each defendant.
On Wednesday the witnesses for the defence were heard.
The verdict is expected today or tomorrow.
Two Tram Accidents

[Sosnowiec — road accidents.]
On Piłsudski Street in Sosnowiec two accidents happened involving two cyclists.
The first incident was with one Welner [?], who, while riding a bicycle, collided with a passenger car. Welger [?] [so printed] was injured in the head.
On the same street, a few hours later, an incident happened with a second cyclist, who, while riding a bicycle, went under the tram.
The tram wheels cut off several of the young man's fingers.
Beggar-Women as Accomplices in Carrying Out Thefts

[Sosnowiec — crime.]
Last week a theft of 6.700 zł. was carried out in Mr. Bierfreund's apartment in Sosnowiec.
Thanks to the energetic investigation the thieves fell into the hands of the police.
During the interrogation the thieves declared that the Jewish beggar-women Hübscher and Moszkowicz, both from Będzin, had pointed out when and how to carry out the theft.
The accomplices are under police supervision.
Suicide of a Jewish Merchant in Wolbrom

[Wolbrom — suicide.]
In his own shop the 38-year-old [?] merchant Isser Fergricht [?] committed suicide by hanging himself. Before Fergricht carried out the terrible deed, he settled his business accounts and took leave of his 2 small children.
The Property Levy for the Year 1934 / Będzin "Gordonia" Prepares for the Summer Colonies / Tragic Death of 2 Workers / Extraordinary Meeting of the Chamber of Commerce

[Taxes — property levy; Będzin — youth movements; Zagłębie — work accidents; Sosnowiec — economy.]
The Finance Ministry has already sent a circular to all tax offices about collecting [?] this year's property levy [danina majątkowa] as quickly as possible.
For merchants and manufacturers the assessment notices [nakazy] must be sent out no later than 15 June [czerwiec] of this year, with the final payment date of 30 June.
Immediately after 30 June they will at once proceed to distraints [egzekucje]. So the ministerial circular demands.
Merchants and manufacturers whose turnover for the year 1933 was assessed at from 20 thousand zł. up to 50,0000 [so printed] zł. will pay 0.8 per mille. And the merchants whose turnover was greater than 50,000 zł. will pay 1:2 [so printed; = 1.2] per mille.
—o—
Będzin "Gordonia" Prepares for the Summer Colonies
The annual colonies, which the district leadership of "Gordonia" in Będzin organizes in the Beskid mountains, will as always arouse due interest.
The three colonies begin already together with the school holidays, on 25 June.
In this year's colonies the comrades David Saerlov [?] (a leader of the Histadrut in Eretz Israel), Oor [?] Abarozanski (a leader of the kvutzot in Eretz Israel) and an instructor from the world union "Maccabi" are to take part.
Concerning the organization of the colonies, a consultation with all the parents of "Gordonia" members will take place this Saturday evening in the organization's own premises.
—o—
Tragic Death of 2 Workers.
In the so-called "bieda-szyby" [primitive pits dug by the unemployed] 4 unemployed men were digging coal. At a certain moment, when they wanted to take out the coal they had dug, a wall of coal collapsed and buried two of the workers beneath it.
—o—

Next Tuesday an extraordinary plenary meeting will take place in the Chamber of Commerce in Sosnowiec. On the agenda a series of economic questions will be dealt with.

The State Lottery — a social necessity!

Playing is an eternal question. Ever since mankind has existed, people have played and gambled [?]. That alone already explains that in the human heart there exists a need to play; the point is only that this need should express itself in the way that is best for the person — and harmless for the public. And these conditions are present in the most ideal way in playing the State Lottery.
When the player wins and receives the prize — he takes no money from anyone and does no one any harm, and the stake is so minimal that every person, even one who is utterly without means and lives solely from his own work, can allow himself it. The stake is small and one has to buy a ticket. In each class a ticket costs 40 zł., a quarter — 10 zł. That is surely no danger! And for those few złotys one can win: in the 1st class — 100,000 zł., in the 2nd class — 200.000 zł., in the 3rd class — 300,000 zł., and in the fourth — up to a million. So as to be able to multiply the stake, in case of a lucky win, 250,000 times — such chances no game other than the lottery offers.
And now let us discuss the matter from another standpoint. A man works, has a post and receives a pension; for an ordinary life the pension will suffice, but apart from that the man has no other interests, has no hopes of some inheritance from America — there can of course be no talk of his becoming well-off in this way or that, and the man dreams, for instance, of a little house of his own in old age.
The only way of realising that dream is — only the State Lottery. One must admit that the lottery is a social necessity, and already today tens and hundreds of thousands of people are grateful to it.
F327

Jewish Zagłębie Protests against the Aliyah Decrees
Police Break Up the Meeting on Targowa Street in Sosnowiec

[Zagłębie — Zionism and aliyah.] Together with world Jewry, the Jews of Zagłębie too have voiced their sharp protest against the Mandatory power in connection with the aliyah decrees. Unfortunately, in this field as well our public showed its fragmentation [?] (if we were united, the decrees might perhaps not have been so hard on us...).
In Sosnowiec the Zionist Organisation and the League for Labour Palestine did not want to take part in the protest action of the other Zionist trends and economic organisations, but held on Sunday a separate meeting in the “Mizrachi” courtyard, which was packed full.
The meeting was opened by Mr. Buksbaum, and after the substantial speeches of Messrs. A. Kan, Dr. Meladysta [?], Krawczyk and Rozman, Mr. Yosef Goldberg read out the protest resolution, which was adopted unanimously.
With the singing of “Hatikvah” and “Techezakna” the meeting was closed.
———
On the same day a protest meeting took place in Będzin, in the courtyard of Mr. Gotfryd (Kościuszki Street). After the speeches devoted to the aliyah decrees, delivered by Messrs. N. Landner, Herszlewicz, Zygrajch, Hampel and a member of the local kibbutz, an appropriate resolution was adopted.
———
A grave impression was made on the Jewish population of Sosnowiec by the protest meeting broken up by the police, which was to have taken place on Monday towards evening in the courtyard of house No. 4 on Targowa Street. The courtyard was overflowing with all strata of the Jewish population; merchants closed their shops, craftsmen threw down their work and went to the protest meeting, which had been called by Zionist groupings, religious and economic organisations.
But as soon as Mr. L. Jungster had uttered the first words, the police declared the meeting dissolved, because it was taking place late. Later mounted police arrived and dispersed the crowd.
———
In Dąbrowa the League for Labour Palestine held a protest meeting. The opening speech was given by Mr. Weissalz, and after the speeches of Messrs. Lemkowicz, Gottesfurcht and Tenenbaum the appropriate resolutions were adopted.
Appeal of the Jewish Charitable Society in Będzin

[Będzin — charity.] Most esteemed citizens, men and women!
We turn to you, most esteemed citizens, men and women, as every year so this year too, with the fervent request to enable the poorest and neediest of our town to get away, whether to the countryside or for a cure.
We know that times are bad, we know that our citizens are heavily burdened by various institutions, but this concerns such unfortunates who live and work all year round in the hardest, bitterest conditions; it concerns persons who cannot stretch out their hand for alms and who are mostly suffering from lung or heart disease.
More than once those few weeks of fresh air or a cure decide their further existence for a whole year.
Therefore we turn to you, esteemed citizens, men and women, with the fervent request: support the Help-Ring!
The Committee of the Jewish Charitable Society in Będzin.
