“Kurier Zachodni” Laments
The Defeat of the Endeks in the City Council Elections
(From the Polish Press)

[Sosnowiec — city council elections; press review.] The tremendous defeat that the Endeks suffered in the last elections to the city council, especially in Sosnowiec, where officially not a single councillor of theirs got through, gives them no rest. Day after day, the poor things, they shed crocodile tears in the columns of “Kurier Zachodni” over the great misfortune that has befallen them.
In No. 150 of the “K. Z.” we find an interesting article on the outcome of the elections. In a lengthy introduction the author of the article, Ćwierk [?], demonstrates how the bourgeois Jewish lists came out of the elections victorious, since they obtained 23 per cent of the mandates, whereas the Endeks obtained only 9 per cent of the mandates.
“In this respect Sosnowiec is a classic example. The ‘Non-Party Bloc for Economic Work’ (B. B.) has 24 mandates, the Jews 10 mandates, the P. P. S. 9 mandates, the communists 4 mandates and the House-Owners' Association 1 mandate, whereas the Christian-national ‘Abw’ [?] has not a single mandate! After the Sanacja bloc the largest club in the city council will be the Jewish one. Then the P. P. S. and the communists, who in some electoral bodies put Jewish candidates on their lists, and who according to their internationalist programmes will not distinguish between Polish and Jewish interests.
After a lengthy beating about the bush [?] it turns out that the only nationalists on the council are the Jewish councillors.
It appears that the Endeks are indeed very much afraid of this, because:
“Under the new statute Sosnowiec will be able to have two vice-presidents, and rumours are going round the town that one of them is to be a representative of the Jewish population.”
In the further part of the article the author can by no means reconcile himself with the idea that the Jews obtained 10 councillors (of the 10 only 9 have remained for the time being, because the tenth was taken by the Sanacja). For proportionally they were not entitled to so many — and at the same time he gives a lesson to the Sanacja, in whose eyes, in his opinion, the Jewish bloc found great favour.
“At a historic moment for Sosnowiec, when the city fathers enter the new town hall (ratusz), for the first time in the history of our self-government there will not be a single Endek, but on the other hand there will be ten Jewish councillors, and that for the first time since the Sosnowiec city council has existed.”
Poor Endeks and foolish [?] people! Not a single councillor! How terrible it must be that the pillar of the party, the former president, vice-president and councillor Michel, must, poor fellow, sit at home!
Poor fellow...
S. Szach.
What Is Heard in Upper Silesia?

[Upper Silesia — Katowice, artisans.]
From the Artisans' Association in Katowice.
(H. S.) On Sunday afternoon a large artisans' meeting took place in the premises of the Jewish "Merchants' Association" in Katowice, devoted to the merger (fusion) with the artisans' association of the German Jews, which failed to materialise.
The chairman, Mr. Szymon Kaufman, explains to those assembled the purpose of the meeting, and that it was the conduct of the German Jews that caused the union not to materialise.
After the speech of Eng. Żmigród, our townsman Mr. Rudaler, a member of the Warsaw headquarters, enters the hall and is greeted by Mr. Kaufman.
Mr. H. L. Goldsztajn (Będzin) calls in his speech for joint help to the board. The Jewish artisan — he says — must exist without "pritsim" [noble patrons], because we are too poor to hand out honour to everyone. We must provide for our children, because in this way we raise for the government a productive, healthy generation.
Dr. Konarek declares that their association will always protect the Jewish artisan with lawyers, lecturers, etc.
The floor is given to Mr. Rudaler, who stresses that only the unification of the artisans can bring the proper results.
After Mr. Goldsztajn's motion to express thanks to the board is carried, a discussion develops, in which Messrs. Zajersztrom, L. Goldwasser, Dam[?] and others take part.
Mr. Goldwasser puts forward a motion to thank Eng. Żmigród for his voluntary collaboration and for donating 3 months' rent, so that the association can develop properly.
Conference of Jewish Merchants' Associations

[Upper Silesia — Katowice, merchants.]
(H. S.) In the premises of the Katowice Jewish Merchants' Association a conference took place of all Jewish merchants' associations in Silesia, with the participation of all economic organisations in Katowice.
Besides Bielsko, representatives of Mysłowice, Królewska Huta, Tarnowskie Góry, Siemianowice, Skoczów, Wodzisław, Cieszyn and others also took part in the conference.
The president of the local Jewish Merchants' Association, Eng. Żmigród, opens the meeting and greets the guests and delegates, among whom we see Dr. Chameides, president of the Rabbis' Union in Upper Silesia; Dr. Lampel, long-time head of the local economic organisations; Messrs. Dr. Konarek and M. Adler of the Ex-Servicemen's (Combatants') Association; President Szymon Kaufman and Zajersztrom of the Artisans' Association; President Goldwasser, Waltuch, Adler and L. Basler of the Small Traders' Association; Dr. Sortan of the Jewish Bank; Perec and Schiff of the Zionist Organisation; Director Neuman[?] of the B'nai B'rith lodge, and others.
Eng. Żmigród explains that the purpose of the conference is to create a united force able to stand up to the tide of local antisemitism; to create a body with the proper authority, so that in the name of all Jewish merchants in Silesia it can demand and defend Jewish rights, and also see to it that the shaky positions of the Jewish merchant in Silesia do not collapse entirely.
The floor is given to Dr. Schaier for his very interesting and popular lecture on "The situation of merchants in general and of Jewish merchants in particular". The lecture is heard by all with great interest.

In the courtyard of a house on Piastowska Street in Królewska Huta a fight broke out among children who were playing. Because of the children, the landlord, a certain Niespor, and his tenant, also a Christian, who stood up for her children, were drawn into the fight too. Unity and Fragmentation

(After the city-council elections in Zagłębie.)
That is to say: now that the fair is over, after the hullabaloo, after the chasing and rushing about, after the grabbing of seats, one can at last stop and form an idea of where we stand in the world and what exactly we have accomplished.
Jewish Zagłębie went to the city-council elections this time broken, splintered and torn as never before. No one took into account that unity had perhaps never been as necessary as this time, and no union could be achieved; and where it was partially achieved at the last minute in Będzin, each tried to dupe the other. In the process the lawlessness reached such a degree that people altogether forgot that public questions were at stake.
Thus in Będzin at the last moment it looked as if a fight were being waged between persons, each wanting to outdo the other. It looked like private firms competing with one another, advertising themselves, each wanting to prove that it offers better goods, that it is more reliable. It was completely forgotten that this was a public problem, to be approached with reverence and with the fullest responsibility toward the community. Moreover, no one took account of the fact that municipal representation stands far above — let us say — the representatives of some Jewish institution or other, where problems of taxing this or that category of citizens are not dealt with; [here] at the first opportunity an antisemitic blow from behind[?] comes, and one must fight so that the bullets are not aimed at our camp. And if they are aimed at us after all, one must have courage, ability and orientation to fend them off, to evade them.
Unfortunately none of this was taken into account, and quite simply the trivial was made into the essential. People forgot, or pretended to forget, where they were going and whom they must represent. Had they been willing to take stock, had they not wanted merely to represent the party, many Będzin councillors would have understood that their place is not in the city council, that they will be able to achieve absolutely nothing there and represent no one, since at least there no one will be talking about Jewish parties. But, let us say, if they are talked about after all, it is even worse, since the greatest number will then be unable even to open their mouths. So what was all this scrambling for — all to grab a seat and bring no benefit to the masses? May one act this way toward the Jewish community, toward the broad population?
That is what is called lawlessness, that is what is called irresponsibility; otherwise persons without full one-hundred-percent qualifications would not have been allowed to give their consent to become councillors in a city council, where one must not only have perfect command of the Polish language in speech and writing, but must also be refined socially and economically; for, after all, a city council today is no Hasidic shtibl, where everyone talks at once and the "Shh! Shh!" drowns out all the speeches.
Regrettably we keep sinking, and the more dangerous the Jewish situation becomes, the more antisemitism grows stronger, the less responsibility toward the community we get, the less respect is shown to the public.
And this comes from the fact that ideals, sacred problems, have been exchanged for small change. Once, representatives were held in esteem, because the finest and best were elected by the community; later people began to take this lightly, everyone wanted to climb to the highest rung, and "groundwork"[?] began until the desired goal was achieved. It did no harm at all that in this way one or another degraded Jewish honour and we were simply disgraced; but once each was already riding the communal nag, no one could say a word to him, and he did as he pleased and as suited him best...
In this way the lawlessness began in the public sphere, and when a party wanted to have its own representative, it did not consider at all that he is not needed and that it does not even have the right person. They took the first Shmerl at hand, sent him and said: go, go, it will be fine, you'll manage; and if you fail once, that doesn't matter either — what doesn't happen to a person.
It was done as in Russia in the old days. There is a Russian anecdote: once the polkovnik [colonel] had no feldsher in his regiment; what does one do? He takes the first Jewish soldier at hand and tells him: "Ty budesh' fel'dsherom!" [Russian: "You will be a feldsher!"] — "What do you mean, I'm not a feldsher?" — "Go[?], you'll be one." And he went and indeed became a feldsher...
By this very same system we now get communal workers and councillors and kehilla representatives and all kinds of representatives. They were not raised in public life, did not grieve for the Jewish community, did not share in Jewish troubles and sufferings; they came off the street, and therefore they did not lack the nerve to say that they would somehow manage with the Jewish people.
On the other hand, it never entered their minds that perhaps they are not called to be Jewish representatives, that they cannot take upon themselves the great national responsibility. And therefore our public life has become so cheapened and the former esteem and reverence have vanished.
It is interesting: who among us nowadays becomes a ringleader, a noisemaker and a regular "cooking spoon" [busybody]? Of course only he who possesses a rather large dose of impudence, and the greater the brazenness, the more chances he has of becoming great. And if now and then a serious, modest representative is found among this gang, he will not be noticed, so small is he among the shouters. And you may be sure that at the first opportunity he will be pushed aside; it makes no difference what benefit he brings — it is enough that one will not [see/want?] him.
Allowing such lawlessness, it is therefore no wonder that no compromise can ever be reached, and the results are that at whatever election it may be we come with a wealth of lists, and of course because of this "wealth" we are impoverished in the public sphere.
It is enough to point to the huge defeat that Będzin, the heart of Jewish Zagłębie, suffered in the last city-council elections. And worse still is that we do have, kein ayin hara, fifteen councillors. A fairly considerable number, it would seem, and yet we do not see who will steer here and who will find his bearings, who will be able to fend off the bullets that will, as usual[?], be aimed at our camp by the antisemites. There is thus no authority that could replace Dr. Weigzieher [sic; Dr. Salomon Weinzieher], to whom everyone, willy-nilly, had to listen.
That is where the tragedy lies, that is where our backwardness and poverty lie. We have no intelligent representatives and thereby we are spiritual and political illiterates.
Sosnowiec, on the other hand, the city of Jewish fragmentation and strife, ought to receive a medal of honour for the role it played in the present city-council elections, so that thanks to unity it came out with a victory. Ten Jewish councillors in the present elections is a triumph that must be recorded in golden letters in the history of Jewish Sosnowiec.
Moreover, we pride ourselves that we got the finest people in the city, not according to their pedigree but according to ability. We have intellectuals and such as will know how to defend Jewish honour as soon as it is needed. We are therefore satisfied with the human material, for after all we must have conscious people, people with orientation, honest people, people who command respect and whom others must reckon with.
A different question is that we pin no great hopes at all on the new city councils, for even with the best will not much can be done in our favour, if only because our representatives will always be in the great minority; but what matters to us is that there will be someone to speak, someone to persuade, someone to find his way on the spot. And that plays one of the most important roles.
We believe that it was by chance that Jewish Sosnowiec managed to play so well in the present elections, for to reckon and calculate so that it should be for the good of the community — for that Jewish Sosnowiec is not cut out; on the contrary, they always like to act on the jump[?], and it always turns out that Shmerl says day and Berl says night. Therefore one must welcome the present unity that prevailed in the elections, so that the initiators deserve a hearty yasher-koyach from the public.
May the deeds of unity and oneness be a moral lesson not only for Sosnowiec but for all of Jewish Zagłębie. Let people see how much can be built with unity and, conversely, destroyed with fragmentation.
R. Let.
Heard and Seen.

[Będzin and Sosnowiec — weekly feuilleton.] By Ben Amotz.

"New times, new songs"...
They come to the editorial office, the Jews — beaten, wounded; the mute gaze of their frightened eyes speaks. They tell us that it is not safe to walk through the town at night; Hitler's people parade in the streets with their swastika badges. The air is charged. The wave of hatred surges and tears, the ground is undermined, "Down with the Jews" — that is the most popular little song nowadays...
Other Jews, too, come and tell their stories; they do not report on the antisemitic wave that rages over our life — rather they complain about
— the "Jewish Hitlerites"...
About those whose hearts turn to stone and whose ears refuse to hear when the delegates come to ask them for the self-imposed contributions on behalf of our most unfortunate brothers from Germany.
— I don't want to give — is the answer — what are the German refugees to me? That's my grandmother's worry...
When we doubt what we hear, the delegate of the anti-Hitler committee shows us a list of a whole row of newly risen rich men whom he visited; and instead of recording the sums of the donations, he wrote at the side of the slip:
— Refused...
— What do you demand of us? — we ask the money collectors for the German refugees.
— We demand that you put the traitors of the people in the pillory — those who will not hear the people's sorrow, those who persuade themselves that with their fortunes they are already secure for the future...
— Oh, how naive you are — we say — you still believe there is a bit of shame on the Jewish street? That the "Cossack" is ashamed when he is caught with the transports of goods he brings in from Hitler's land? On the contrary: if business goes well, he buys himself the finest aliyah [honour of being called to the Torah] in the "shtibl", sits up front beside the rebbe and laughs up his sleeve at the "idlers" who thought up some foolish word:
— Boycott...
The Jews, the spreaders of the "atrocity propaganda", shake their heads and say:
— "New times, new songs"...

In a modest way...
— Come with me and I will show you the deed of a simple Jew, an ordinary flesh-and-blood man, an everyday Jew. — So a Sosnowiec Jew says to me, and talking thus he takes me and leads me up to the second floor of M. Trapeuier's [?] house on 3 Maja Street in Sosnowiec.
— Why have you brought me here? If I'm not mistaken, we are now in the "Hotel Warszawski"?
— True, this is indeed the same hotel, but I have not brought you in here so that you should eat lunch here together with me — says my friend — rather, my intention is that you should see with your own eyes how little poor children are fed.
I did not wait long for it. At the set hour they came, the little eaters — among them also several children and one mother. Soon the proprietor comes in, who bustles about his "guests", seats them around the special little tables on which the dishes already stand ready, cooked especially for them. "Eat, children, eat" — the hotel owner encourages them — perhaps a little more?
— "Not potatoes, I want another plate of trupnik [krupnik, barley soup] — says a little boy, about 7–8 years old. Oh, "the trupnik is dit [?] today"..
From the "conversation" I had with the little "glutton and guzzler" it becomes clear that his father lies sick and his mother is the breadwinner; from early morning until the night hours she stands on Dekerta Street with a few greens...
— When does mummy cook "lunch"?
— She makes it in the evening, only potatoes, no trupnik...
A "better" sort also come here to eat — my companion informs me. There — he says — in the big dining room, eat the children of respectable families, children who study at the gymnasium...
Yeshiva students from out of town and elderly Jews, former craftsmen who today can no longer earn a living by the labour of their hands, come here and eat lunch every single day. They, the privileged, receive better dishes, decent lunches, even compote too...
— Has everyone already had sweets? — the owner asks (the little company receive sweets after every lunch...)
— "Not me yet" — calls out a little "lad" whose cheeks are flushed from the hot food.
— "Give me some for my little sister too, she couldn't come to eat, she goes barefoot"...
Few people know of these holy and useful deeds, because the benefactor of the undertaking — Izaak Erlich is his name — does not boast that for 10 years now he has been feeding dozens of poor children. "Don't write about it" — he asks me — I am not one of those who give a poor man a piece of bread or alms only when they are sure that the newspaper will publicise it...
I promised him so, but did not keep my word... because at a time when the feeling of compassion has become so blunted, when the most terrible tragedies no longer arouse any sympathy, and there is a man — Izaak Erlich is his name — who feeds poor hungry children, this must serve as a moral lesson for the moneybags, among them also the "fine" God-fearing ones who bless themselves behind closed doors, in their innermost chambers, and do not want to know what is happening on the Jewish street...
You must bow your heads in shame before the man who fills the stomachs of hungry Jewish children.
— Izaak Erlich — is his name
— Tehezakna yedeikhem [may your hands be strengthened]... Blessed be the hands that do such deeds and more
— in a modest way...

The gmina — a superfluous thing...
It is a mistake to think that the result of the city council elections in Będzin aroused discontent and bitterness in everyone; on the contrary, there are some who are quite satisfied with the outcome and prove in black and white that thanks to the "brilliant" result — or more precisely, thanks to the victory won by the Agudah list — the Jewish kehilla will "gain" many thousands of złoty and at the same time be spared a great many troubles.
The first gain for the kehilla will consist in our finally getting rid of the gmina [the Jewish community board]; what on earth for — a Hasidic Jew argues to us — do we still need the gmina? When the freethinkers sat on the city council — he says — those who want to "uproot" the faith, we had, as a counterweight, to have the gmina with God-fearing dozors [board members] who would provide for the religious needs of the Jewish population; but now, when loyal, kosher citizens of the "Agudah" will sit on the city council, especially those who have a foothold at the "high windows", we will see to it that on the forum of the "Rada Miejska" [city council] the question of the shochtim be settled, new morei hora'ah [rabbinic judges], paying out the pensions of the rabbinate, and above all — finishing the mikveh. I swear to you by my beard and sidelocks — says the Hasidic Jew — that the mikveh will be completed already in the present term, because "our own Jews" can accomplish anything... They can manage not only to obtain a subsidy for the mikveh, but even to get rid of a Zionist vice-president as well...
— What do you say to this opinion? We are beginning to reflect that the Jew is right: when an Agudah majority sits on the city council, then
— the gmina is a superfluous thing...
A Little More Sincerity

[Będzin — city-council elections; polemic.] (A reply to Mr. Wygodzki.)
The outcome of the elections to the city council in Będzin caused tremendous agitation among the Jewish population of Będzin, because of the already well-known sad fact that so meritorious a public worker and intellectual force as the honoured [?] Dr. Weinzieher will not be on the city council, and the Jewish population is losing, at so hard and critical a time, when we are threatened by various enemies, a courageous and proud defender, who, unfortunately, will not have the opportunity to let his strong word be heard from the municipal tribune.
It is superfluous to repeat how great the loss is for the Jewish population in general and for the national camp in particular. The public scandal found an echo in the sharp article by Mr. Wygodzki (Z. Ts. No. 22), which expresses the agitation over the fact that a national bloc was created and our own people betrayed it. Certainly this agitation has grounds, and every honestly thinking person must condemn such electoral manipulation and be outraged by such an electoral trick.
But if Mr. W. wishes with his revelations to enlighten the Jewish public about the electoral fraud that took place, and to try to hold someone responsible, we can gladly help him in this; but one must also make clear who those are who deserve to be condemned as breakers and betrayers of the bloc. And this we have the right to demand of so honest a Zionist worker as Mr. Wygodzki.
First of all, a few words about Mr. W.'s irony at the expense of the Torah ve-Avoda young people. We are not at all concerned with the honour of this movement, for it is well enough known not only in the Zionist world but also in the Zionist street of Będzin, since they contributed their share to more than one Zionist victory in our town [printed "איז"], not to speak of their role in general Zionist life in the Diaspora and in the work of building up the Land of Israel.
Still more vexing is the fact that precisely Mr. W., who knows the role of these young people in creating the general Jewish bloc and later the national one — they were not at all out to obtain an honourable place on the list or a safe seat on the city council, but always renounced the various personal [?] prestige questions which, among other groupings, were the main problems, on account of which the integrity of the bloc was more than once threatened — nevertheless finds for the T.v.A. movement only disdain and irony; which, by the way, we can grant him.
And when the same Mr. W. permits himself to accuse the members of T.v.A. publicly of being the first imitators of the Revisionist treachery, here we must say that from a man such as Mr. Yitzchak Wygodzki one may demand more honesty when accusing a movement before the public, and we say — be honest! If you say something, then tell everything, so that we may indeed learn the whole truth! And see who the real culprits are in this public electoral scandal.
Tell, then, also that 1) the T.v.A. young people agreed to the 8th place on the list of candidates, even though their candidate was no weaker than some of the candidates ahead of him, and their numerical strength was certainly no smaller than that of the others.
2) That T.v.A. won the 5th place in the drawing of lots and nevertheless took the eighth. That throughout the negotiations we renounced the honour of our party and paid no attention to the various ironic remarks of certain leaders at the expense of T.v.A., but strove for the strengthening and cementing of the bloc, which was to bring into the city council the proper representatives (first and foremost Dr. Weinzieher), who would be able to give expression to Jewish suffering and to the hard situation of the Jewish population on the forum of the city council.
And if one speaks of electoral fraud, why should one not have the courage to ascribe this fraud to all those who received a larger number of votes than the first candidate?
It was, after all, the T.v.A. delegates who proposed that Dr. Weinzieher's name should appear only once on the ballots, as head of the list, which would have made any fraud whatsoever impossible; and against this proposal were, after all, all those who now want to throw the responsibility upon us.
And why indeed should the public not know the course of the last meeting of the bloc, the night before the elections, when it emerged that a certain gentleman, a candidate of the bloc, had printed ballots and was campaigning for himself. This discovery led to extremely dramatic moments, and we were all sure that this gentleman or his group would — as public discipline and ethics dictate — be removed from the bloc and branded as traitors and bloc-breakers; but we witnessed a new kind of morality: instead of condemning, the leading persons of the bloc actually found it necessary to negotiate with this breaker, and even promised [?] him, as "recompense" for his fine [deed], that if the first 4 candidates were elected he would get the fifth place, that of Comrade [?] Buchweitz [?].
And at that very meeting came the second sensation: that other important candidates, too, were preparing to campaign on their own and had printed ballots of their own. So who, Mr. Wygodzki, followed the Revisionist example?
And the public may also know that after Sunday, the day of the elections, our candidate wished to hand the chairman of the bloc a letter of resignation, regardless of the election result; but the gentlemen of the Hitachdut refused, and the Revisionists did not come any more at all (despite the promise of the fifth mandate).
Surely you will admit, honoured [?] Mr. Wygodzki, that in our whole conduct, from the first minute to the day of the elections, there was no intention whatsoever of any kind of fraud, for too great are the morality and ethics of the ideology we represent for us to stoop to a base electoral fraud for the sake of a seat. From all this it is clear that precisely the young people of T.v.A. clung with all their strength to loyalty towards the bloc and [?] by no means wanted to betray the bloc; and if we nevertheless conducted the elections for our candidate, it was because the bloc had been torn apart and all the candidates or their parties (except the first) were campaigning for their own representatives — for it is self-evident that we, as a party, could not show our weakness at a time when others had forced the fight upon us and we had to show our strength in the Jewish street.
When you, Mr. W., speak of responsibility, then responsible in the first place are those who put Dr. Weinzieher on the list at his expense [?]. But these gentlemen [?] desecrated the honour of the doctor, who answered the call of his brethren in a difficult hour. By their conduct they brought about this election result.
One must be sincere and honest when dealing publicly with a public scandal.
In the name of the "Torah ve-Avoda" movement in Będzin
M. Lewin.
Important Decisions of the Supreme Court

[Law — decisions of the Supreme Court; regular column.]
A tenant's (lokator's) obligations for rent
A tenant is released from the duty to pay rent from the moment the agreement is dissolved. Wishing to dissolve an agreement, the tenant must give notice of it at the agreed term, or at least a quarter in advance. Even in the latter case the tenant's obligation towards the landlord for rent ends only when he places the vacated apartment at the landlord's disposal.
If, however, a tenant moves out at the set term and leaves a sub-tenant (sublokator) in the apartment, the landlord has the right not to take cognizance of the notice and to go on collecting rent from the tenant for the whole premises.
What counts as a separate warehouse
Premises used „temporarily“, for example up to 3 days, for repacking or storing goods cannot be regarded as a separate warehouse, and consequently one need not purchase a registration card (karta rejestracyjna) for such premises.
Personal liability for a bill-of-exchange debt
If someone signs a bill of exchange (weksel) on behalf of another without proper authorisation, he bears personal liability for the debt precisely in the case where the person or firm he represented refuses to honour the debt.
Postponing administrative penalties
The cases in which the execution of criminal sentences is postponed also apply to administrative penalties. In the case of a refusal[?] the decision cannot be appealed.
Great Heroes... — A Conversation between Two Married Men

[Humorous feuilleton — married life; dialogue.]
Two married men sit and talk about their wives.
The wives are not present; they have gone off to do some shopping.
They live, as it happens, in the same building, the two couples, door to door.
One of them we shall call Yosl and the other Asher (though their names are different).
Yosl complains:
„You know, Asher, what a scandal I'm going to make when mine comes back. I won't let her walk all over me any more, I won't be her footstool any more, her „pantoffel-man“ (henpecked husband) — six years I've suffered from her, enough! And her mother, that witch with the narrow little mug, with the thin little wart[?], I'll throw out and tell her that her foot may never again cross my threshold! When she comes into the house, she makes a hell of it; she gives her daughter lessons in how to keep me on a short rein. She buried the father-in-law too, she says — so her daughter may bury me as well. You know, Asher, what a „wedding“ I'm going to throw her today! All my troubles, all my pains I'll let out on my wife and her mother. I kept silent and suffered, but today, Asher, it will all come to an end; troubles can make a tiger out of a little lamb. In such bitter times, when you can't earn a single gulden [złoty], she goes and borrows fifty gulden and travels to Katowice to buy rags. Asher, don't go away, wait, I want you to be present, I can't stand it any more. Don't go away, Asher!“
Asher heard Yosl out and took the floor himself:
„Don't think, Yosl, that I'm happy with mine. I won't keep quiet with her either. I'm not working either, and I have even more troubles than you. Nevertheless she went off to spend the last 5 zł. I still had in the house. You know, Yosl, today I'm going to play her the real comedy; anger can break iron walls, and the anger has been boiling in me for a good few years now, but today, for your sake, I'll unload my heart! Even if I knew they'd arrest me and send me away for twenty years! Either way, life with her isn't worth anything; in prison I'll be much freer than I am with her. Don't go there, and don't stand here, and don't sit there, and don't look at that one, and don't greet this one — as if I'd been sold to her, a real slave! You know, Yosl, what I'm going to do today! The street will be black with people. I can keep silent and endure, but everything comes to an end. Everything has to have a limit! I'll tell you the plain truth, Yosl: y o u r s is still an angel, a dove of peace compared with m i n e. Yours at least sometimes cooks you a spoonful of food, keeps the house clean; mine doesn't even do that. At my place it's a shambles (hekdesh), everything flung about and thrown around, and for food she gives me sausages; cook something she won't. She doesn't want to spoil, she says, her manicure; she can insist, she says, that I eat bread with frankfurters (parówki). Is that what you call a wife? Enough! Today it will come to an end, an end!... and...“
Here Yosl takes the floor again:
„Asher, I don't believe you! You were a melamed and you'll die a melamed; you've told me this hundreds of times already and never once carried it out. You're a shlimazl, a shmendrik; anyone can make anything of you. Me — when I can't carry anything out, at least I shout, at least I stamp my feet, at least I bang my fist on the table, at least I throw a plate on the floor; I must do something to express my protest, my anger; but you don't even dare! That's why I don't believe a single word you say; you're a hero only when your wife isn't home.“
„And you're any better? When do you stamp your foot? — When she goes out into the street, or to the butcher's; when do you break a plate? — When she tells you to wash the dishes; you're not one of the great heroes either!“
„Oh, stop it, stop it! I hate it when someone takes all the credit for himself and gives the other nothing! You can tell somebody else tall tales („little birds in the bosom“), but not me; we've lived together some four years in the same house, door next to door — what is said at my place, you hear, and what is said at yours, I hear. I know one thing: you tremble before your wife as before death; you've never yet dared to open your mouth to her!“
„And you?“ — the other won't let it go — „you're the conqueror? Don't make anyone laugh! How many times have you lain hidden in my wardrobe? Have you forgotten already? True, yours chased after you with a flat-iron, that's true... but I wouldn't hide from a flat-iron; I'd have torn it out of her hands, that's what I'd have done; you've got a mouth — you babble, a mouth-hero is what you are!“
„And what about you? How many times have you lain under the bed? If you don't remember, I'll remind you; I have a good memory. Don't make yourself out to be such a hero and don't make fun of me! But what's been — has been. Enough! Once and for all it has to come to a...“
Just then footsteps were heard and the voices of both their wives.
The two „heroes“ gave a start, frightened, trembling, and quickly went their ways; each man into his own room[?]. Quiet as „cats...
* * *
Such Yosls and Ashers there are, thank God, in the millions; in the heavy millions; almost as many as there are married people, and perhaps even more. We are great conquerors when we get together without the women; when we are among ourselves; when we don't see them — but when they, the women, are here with us — we are the real lemeshkes (milksops).
I'll let you in on a secret, and I hope the secret won't go any further — do you hear? I myself, the writer, the great man, as I am[?], am also one of these heroic husbands.
We are, and we'll stay that way as long as married life is not abolished.
And I go even further: even when married life no longer exists, we shall still be slaves to the fair sex.
We shall always be the little goldfish flapping about in their net. — — —
Related by B. K—r.
The Ellenberg Affair.

[Article — the boycott of Nazi Germany; Zionism.] By Sz. Rotenberg.

The Zionist party court has acquitted Ellenberg of the charge of breaking the boycott and has merely sentenced him to pay a fine of 1800 zł. for not having troubled to obtain a permit from the central boycott committee (from the press).

Ever since Hitler came to power, the most varied slogans about boycotting Hitler Germany have been shouting from the front pages of almost the entire Jewish press. Thousands of articles by journalists of the most varied tendencies and shades have already been written about it; they play upon the national instincts of the Jewish masses, they appeal to the non-Jewish world for help in the fight against the barbarians. Sound human reason was therefore bound to believe that a court of a party which claims to represent the whole of Jewry [klal Yisroel] would condemn in the sharpest manner every attempt to break the boycott front.

The question arises: by what right does one come to thousands of small merchants and[?] agents, who really drew their livelihood only from German imports, and demand that they tear up every contact with Germany — at a time when, for a payment of 1800 zł., a firm of millions like the Ellenbergs' is allowed freely to do colossal business with the Hitler bandits?

How can one preach boycott to others day in, day out, at a time when one takes a millionaire under protection only because he is a man of one's own family?

For such conduct one can surely find no more fitting expression than "toyvl ve-sheretz be-yado" [one who immerses while holding the unclean creature in his hand].

For us the "just" verdict was no surprise, because it had to come. As a consequence of the Zionist "logical" and "consistent" high politics, which has already for the second time sanctioned the sadly famous Transfer Agreement with Hitler Germany. One must, after all, stay consistent: if one makes transactions of millions with the Nazis oneself, why should one not allow a private firm, which also operates with millions, to do so?

The consequences of the Transfer Agreement are already being felt very strongly in Palestine, where a tragicomic, paradoxical situation has arisen. In all the countries of the whole world imports have fallen more or less; only in Palestine have they doubled. A country which should have served as an example with an absolute, 100-percent boycott against everything that comes from Hitler's land presents itself as a classic model of the most shameful boycott-breaking and of direct support for the cannibalistic Hitler regime.

The verdict of the Zionist party court becomes all the sadder in that it can have an enormous demoralising effect on the whole boycott campaign. The whole boycott phraseology now looks like bitter mockery. It is surely a spit in the face of the Jewish masses, who really carry out the boycott. From now on every scoundrel will be able to break the boycott for a relatively small payment and go on being a respected citizen and holding distinguished offices in Jewish public life. It recalls those characters who commit the greatest crimes all year round, and on Yom Kippur they come into the synagogue, pledge "eighteen times a hundred gold pieces" and become momentarily "gleichgeschaltet" [brought into line] as regards God and men.

But the swindle is too blatant for the masses — whom the "leaders" regard as a herd of blind sheep with whom one can do anything — not to see that this was no objective, honest trial, but a "din-toyre" [rabbinical arbitration] cut after the fashion of Urke Nachalnik, where, when it comes to money, it stayed among one's own.

It is therefore the task of the millions of consumers, who do not want to become in the nearest future the prey of the million-headed hydra spreading at a frightening pace over the whole world, to boycott everything that comes from Hitler's land.

This is for the time being the only weapon in the hands of the helpless Jewish masses to help the international working class, as well as the best part of humanity, in the fight against the Hitlerite plague, which flows like poisonous lava and threatens to flood the whole world.
A Little Feuilleton. — On Shirts and Little Shirts

[Feuilleton — fascism around the world.] By G. Kupfer.

If it goes on like this, we are in danger of being left without a shirt on our backs.
I don't mean it because of the crisis. I mean it because of the fascists of the whole world, who have taken the shirts on lease and so befouled them that it has become impossible to wear a shirt.
There were times when an intellectual, especially a Russian-Jewish intellectual, wore a black shirt. Firstly, one wanted to show by it that one was no aristocrat, no white-hands, no white-shirt, that one was equal with all the proletarians who cannot afford to always wear white linen. Secondly, it really was an advantage for poor students and paupers: a black shirt one can wear and wear and it doesn't turn black, as is the nature of a white shirt.
Then[?] Mussolini came and grabbed the black shirt for his fascists. The black shirt became the symbol of blackness, of dark reaction, and no decent person can put on such a shirt any more.
If one wants to put on a shirt of brown colour, one can't do that either. This very colour Hitler snatched up for his Nazis and Jabotinsky for his Revisionists; the brown colour is the expression of everything bad and ugly and of hooliganism — the colour can no longer be worn.
If one should want to wear a red shirt, which was once the expression of popular spirit in Russia, one can't, because in Poland the Polish social-nationalists have grabbed this colour for themselves — they cannot bear to leave Germany alone with the blessings of Hitlerism and want to plant it at home.
A shirt of green colour one cannot wear, because this very colour has been snatched up by the American hero of the khaki shirts. Perhaps one fancies wearing a shirt of grey colour, silver colour — no good again, because that colour already belongs to the second home-grown American Nazi.
Lately all kinds of fascist-Nazi groups have been organising themselves non-stop in every country: in France and in Lithuania, in Belgium and in Estonia, in Brazil and in Japan; the breed grows like mushrooms after rain. And just as fascists cannot manage without hooliganism and without hatred of socialists, Jews and pacifists, so they cannot get by without a shirt. And since every fascist group separately must have its own special shirt colour, they seek out for themselves wherever a colour is lying around anywhere. Often several groups of the same breed form in one country, and one snatches the colour from the other. As of today we already have little shirts black and red, green and blue, silver and yellow, white and of every outlandish colour[?] — except dirty ones.
Fascism is like an epidemic, like every contagious disease that infects, that spreads everywhere alike, especially where it is dirty and unclean, and lasts for a time until it vanishes. And since the plague is now raging, and bacilli, parasites that carry the ugly disease, are not lacking, one can expect that the breed will multiply a good deal more.
One can imagine what a chase after shirts there will be. There will be no colour left that these characters won't grab for their shirts.
So there is no other remedy than to root out, the sooner the better, the shirt-characters of the whole world — otherwise we shall be left naked and bare, without a shirt on our backs.
G. Kupfer.

Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Shelach)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Shelach
The Portion
—o—
a) "Send thou men" (Num. 13:2)
"Why is the portion of the spies placed next to the portion of Miriam? Because she was stricken mriv [?] on account of the slander she spoke against her brother, and these wicked men saw it and did not take the lesson." Rashi.
On this the Rebbe R' Heshel said, by way of wit:
The Gemara in Berakhot, folio 5b, says that afflictions sometimes come upon a person as chastisements of love. All this applies when the afflictions are in private (on an unseen place). If the afflictions are in public (on a visible place), they are not chastisements of love, but come because of evil talk (lashon hara).
With Miriam, as the verse relates, her afflictions were in public ("And Aaron looked upon Miriam: and behold, Miriam was leprous"). From this it follows that the afflictions came upon her not as chastisements of love, but because she had spoken against Moses. That is what Rashi points out precisely: "and these wicked men saw it and did not take the lesson" — they saw: Miriam's leprosy was then visible, so they surely knew that it had come upon her because she had spoken evil of Moses — and they did not take the lesson... and they spread evil talk about the Land of Israel... Rosh Yosef.
—o—
b) "And Moses called Hoshea the son of Nun Joshua" (ibid., 16)
"He prayed for him: may [God] save you from the counsel of the spies." Rashi.
And why did Moses not pray in the same way for Caleb?
But the Zohar (on this portion, folio 158) says that the spies spoke ill of the Land of Israel because they were afraid that in the Land of Israel Moses would appoint other leaders and they would lose their leadership.
The question arises: what reason was there to think that Moses would appoint other leaders in the Land of Israel?
But they knew that in the Land of Israel a Jewish kingdom would surely be formed, and when there would be a king, they, the princes, would surely no longer rule; therefore they spoke ill of the Land of Israel.
About Caleb, however, Moses was certain. Caleb, after all, came from the tribe of Judah, of which it is said "The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet", and he was, after all, the prince of the tribe of Judah — so he himself would be chosen king. Therefore Moses knew that Caleb would not speak ill of the Jews... Knesset Yehezkel.
—o—
c) "For they are bread for us" (Num. 14:9)
These words are incomprehensible, and many interpretations are given of them. "Fear ye not the people of the land, for they are bread for us" — "You shall not be afraid of the people of that land, because they are our bread" — what does this mean?
But the spies argued that the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the Land of Israel, look like giants, and they, the spies, looked beside them like grasshoppers; so Joshua and Caleb argued: do not judge by appearance, "for they are bread for us" — take this very bread that we eat, the manna: can one judge it by its appearance? In appearance it looks "like coriander seed, white", and yet it contains within itself all good flavours; so too do not judge people by their image, by their appearance. "Their shadow is departed from them" — take the image away from them; do not look at a person's image, at his appearance and his shadow... Dvash ve-Halav.
—o—
d) "Pardon, I beseech thee, the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of thy mercy" (ibid., 19)
"Pardon, I beseech thee, the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of thy mercy, and as thou hast forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now" — these words we also say in our prayers: "Forgive the sins of this people as Your mercy is great, just as You have borne the sins of this people from Egypt until now" — the question arises: what sense do these words make? Because God has forgiven us from Egypt until now, must He go on forgiving us? On the contrary, if He has forgiven so many times, it must surely come to an end some time...
But we say: forgive us; perhaps we are too sinful to be worthy of forgiveness? "And as thou hast forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now" — in Egypt You did forgive us, and today we are no more sinful than in Egypt, when the Jews served idols... No difficulty: if You, God, forgave the Jews then, we today are all the more better and more worthy of forgiveness... R' Moshe Sofer.
—o—
e) "How long shall I bear with this evil congregation" (ibid., 27)
The Gemara in Sotah, folio 35, says that the death of the generation of the wilderness was such "that worms came out of their mouths and entered their navels". The Gemara does not derive this from any verse. But R' Hayyim Yosef David Azulai derives it from a gematria: "ad matai la-edah"... MaTaY La'EDaH are the initial letters of: M — from their tongues, T — worms, Y — came out, L — to their navels, ' — on account of, D — the slander of, H — the land... Nahal Kedumim.
—o—
f) "They found a man that gathered sticks upon the sabbath day" (Num. 15:32)
The Sages say: "The gatherer intended it for the sake of Heaven", and yet he was condemned, although with the transgression he meant it for the sake of Heaven. Because we do not possess the criterion of who commits a crime for the sake of an idea and who truly for the sake of crime. Every criminal must be condemned, though he may say that he intended it for the sake of Heaven. Imrei Yirmiyahu.
—o—
g) "That they make them fringes in the borders of their garments" (ibid., 38)
The Kelmer Maggid, R' Moshe Yitzhak, once came to Dubulti [Dubbeln] in the summer. Dubulti lies near Riga and on the seashore. In summer thousands of people come there from Riga to the sea. And as at all summer resorts, thousands of men whose wives are staying there come out to Dubulti for the Sabbath.
On Sabbath morning the Kelmer Maggid goes to the synagogue to pray. He sees how all the Sabbath summer-visitors are praying without their prayer shawls, because, arriving late on Friday by the last train, they always forget their tallitot... The Kelmer Maggid goes up onto the bimah and tells a parable in his manner:
Gentlemen! I will tell you a story. That Sabbath I was in Riga and wandered into a householder's home. I am told that he is not at home, he is in Dubulti [printed: "Rublin"]. As I stand there in the room I hear weeping; I look around: on the cupboard lies the tallit bag, and from the tallit bag comes the weeping... The tallit is weeping because the master of the house forgot to take it along; everything he took along, all the trifles for his wife, all kinds of food and fruit, and the tallit he forgot... So I say to the tallit:
— Do not weep, do not weep. A day will come when your owner will travel a longer road than to Dubulti; then he will leave everything behind, and only you alone, tallit, will he take along...
The False Messiah (4)

[Serialized historical tale — David Alroy, the false messiah; installment 4.]
Sh. Berg.

The assembled [?] began to move quietly toward him, and in an instant he had vanished.
Before the sun went down the sultan released the Jews from prison, and their [?] wives and children returned home.
What had happened here?
Here is what had happened. As soon as David Alroy had killed the ruler of the city, he knew that the sultan would want to take revenge on the Jews. So he went at once to the mountain Jews [printed "mountain-yurn"], who were heroes, fearless and outstanding warriors, and told them what had happened and what danger hung over the heads of all the Jews. He called on them to compel the sultan by force not to vent his anger on the Jews.
With his fiery words he lit a fire in their hearts, and they said to him thus:
— Lead us, trusted one of God, messiah of the Jews, and we will follow you!
So he chose three hundred mighty men and told them that this would be the sign: if they succeeded, it would be proof that God had taken pity on His children and would redeem them. If not, they would perish for the sanctification of the Name; after all, they wanted to save the Jews from their cruel ruler.
They hid their swords under their cloaks and set off on the road; by day they hid in caves and pits, and they walked only at night. David Alroy knew that the sultan's wives and children went out driving every day, so he lay in wait for them with his band and fell upon them suddenly.
The sultan was afraid to do the Jews harm, but he was uneasy: who knows what else the sorcerer might do to him. So he summoned the wisest people of the land to a consultation on what to do.
David Alroy and his three hundred mighty men returned to the mountains, and he began to organize an army to go up to the Land of Israel. He dispatched emissaries throughout Persia, to Babylonia, Baghdad and Arabia, and had the Jews told that the time of redemption had come; God had chosen him as messiah, he already had an army, and many Jews already believed in him. And he called on all the Jews to join him and enlist in his army.
The tidings of redemption set the Jews of those lands aflame, and they began to believe that these were the last days of exile. In masses [?] they joined the messiah. Everywhere they began preparing for the redemption.

David Alroy Conquers Persia.

David Alroy already had an army of a hundred thousand men, horsemen and foot soldiers, well armed; Jews from every corner of the world came to the messiah and enlisted in his army. Many non-Jews also joined him. All the oppressed and persecuted came to David Alroy and hoped that through him they would be redeemed. A whole tribe, known as the "Gwiyer" [?], which worshipped [?] the dog (neither Jews, Christians nor Mohammedans), also came to David Alroy's aid. Most outstanding of all were the mountain Jews. They were the best soldiers, and they were ready to go through fire and water for the messiah. Twenty heroes of the mountain Jews David Alroy chose for his bodyguard. They carried [?] great curved swords from Damascus and long sharp spears on the right shoulder.
David Alroy kept the army in a desolate city in the Persian desert.
When he already felt strong enough to go out to the battlefield, he first began with peace. He sent word to the sultan of Persia that he was the messiah of the Jews, that he was going up to the Land of Israel to conquer the land for the Jewish people, and that he wanted the sultan, like Cyrus, the king of Persia, to help the Jews — to help them with arms, with money, and certainly not to hinder them from going to Jerusalem.
The sultan was already afraid of David Alroy, thinking that he was a sorcerer, but he laughed at his demand: for where would he, David Alroy, get an army to take Jerusalem?
David Alroy saw that by kindness he would achieve nothing and that he would have to use force, so he led his army out on the road. First he marched on the fortress of Amadiya, his native town. He took it without a battle. The ruler saw the great armed host, took fright and surrendered at once.
Proudly, on a white horse, David Alroy rode in triumph at the head of the army and occupied the town. He assured the inhabitants that he would not hold the town permanently — his goal was the Land of Israel. Meanwhile he freed everyone, Jews and non-Jews, from the heavy taxes, and the townspeople received him with great joy, blessed his name, and many joined him.
In Amadiya he left a detachment of soldiers, and he himself went on further into the country. He took one fortress after another, one town after another. Many surrendered to him without resistance. Those who opposed him he defeated easily; he conquered all of Persia, drove out the forty-five rulers of the land together with their overlord, the sultan of Persia, the "king over all kings". He already stood near Babylon.
David Alroy was the unlimited ruler of Persia; he made his temporary residence-city at Shushan, which lies on the border of Persia and Babylonia. His name as a conqueror reached distant lands, and many rulers were frightened of him. Even the caliph of Baghdad.
The Jews of Baghdad, as of other cities and lands, rejoiced greatly at the messiah's victory. They were certain that this was the beginning of the redemption. Many yeshiva students, young rabbis and scholars, shut their books and went off to David Alroy.

A Call for Brotherhood

A protest against Hitler's persecution of the Jews by the famous American poet Edwin Markham, who is now 82 years old.
They came out of the night, with visions[?] stilled in their blood,
hatched out of the mystery before the Flood.
They saw how Egypt withered[?], how other lands were laid waste,
how the scarlet-red East is wiped over with grey sand.

Through the ancient years the Jewish people felt the knout;
in black Syria and blacker Spain their blood was shed.
The tribes of horror, slaves [literally "negroes"] of hate and of exile's bitter bread,
lived in the shadow of ever-felt death.
They built mausoleums for the Pharaohs,
mixing the bricks with tears and toil.
And now in Germany we see anew how the heavy hand
presses the Jewish necks and chokes.
And yet this wondrous people had a genius mind
and endowed the earth with a glory-rich seed;
from their spiritual seed
came the Bible — and not single is the luminous name:
Moses, who stood above the holiest place,
saw the name of Jehovah and heard His word;
then sent down the Ten Commandments,
a law for men of every land and town.
The word of wisdom came down;
centuries and continents have heard it.

Others too come of the Jewish stock:
Isaiah, whose voice thundered like the sea —
David too, who with heavenly radiant songs
breathed upon earth the calm of harmonious sounds.
Then Spinoza, who raised his shining hand
and still carries his light from land to land.
See the wisdom of its judge-philosophers,
whose punishments hold an eternal splendour.

Shall not the people of such beautiful spirit
be shielded from hatred and find consolation?
After all, they do not have their sought-for place in the sun;
they who knew Pharaoh and now know the Hun.
Protest against the injustice and horror
through stormy song and fiery spoken word.
Let protests thunder from all the corners of the world,
to terrify the tyrant's heart and hand.
Let protests be carried on until the happy moment
when justice will unveil her mighty hands.

Let all men rise up and attain holiness,
where they can see God's face in every face.
Let brotherhood reign; let this cry of pain
be carried over the earth and into every heaven.

Translated [into Yiddish] by S. Landoy[?].

The programme consists of: 1) Jankiel's "Omnom ken", 2) "Darkekho", 3) "Ki anu amekho", 4) "Sason ve-simkha", performed by the orchestra of Polish Radio under the direction of Mr. Henryk Szpilman; solo sung by Mr. Stanisław[?] Goldfarb. 5) A. Krein — "Melisalda"[?], 6) the folk song "Three Young Lads", 7) M. Tsemenershver[?] — "Kroytertsel"[?], 8) the folk songs "Little Fishes" and "The Wedding", performed by Mrs. Frida Lurie. 9) L. Liov — "We Carry a Song", 10) A. Gelbart — "I Love Work", 11) M. Szneur — "Ezekiel", 12) A. Gelbart — "The Tavern", performed by Szneur's choir; solo sung by Mr. Herman Litera[?].
Sound films on the radio waves.
The English newspapers now report on the wonderful achievements of the English scientist Baird in the field of television.
His apparatus has already been so perfected that with its help one can already transmit over the radio waves moving scenes simultaneously in picture and sound.
Recently Baird transmitted a motion picture from his television studio, and those who had a television set in their home received the whole film splendidly on the "silent screen". The impression was colossal.
Things have already come to the point that very soon everyone will be able to "catch" the finest sound films over the radio waves at home and will not have to trouble to go to the cinema at all.
People will soon begin to be enthralled by television just as happened with radio a few years ago.
Did radio exist in the times of... the Talmud?
It is quite easy to imagine the strange face every reader will make on reading such a question: "Did radio exist in the times of the Talmud, i.e. some 2,000 years ago?"...
People will shrug their shoulders in astonishment and think: probably it is some joke or simply a silly fable.
And yet it is a question that lately simply interests many scholars, and it came about because of a chance discovery that someone made while studying the tractate Yoma of the Babylonian Talmud.
And this sensational story is as follows:
In tractate Yoma, folio 20, side b (on the second side of the 20th leaf), there is a very remarkable passage which reads: "Three sounds travel from one end of the world to the other, and these are they: the sound of the sun's orb, the sound of the tumult of Rome, and the sound of a soul leaving the body; and some say also of birth[?]; and some say also Ridya."
In literal translation it means: three sounds reach from one end of the world to the other end of the world, and these are they: the sound when the sun turns, the sound of the multitude in Rome, and the sound when the soul leaves the body. And some say that also the sound when one is born, and some say that also "R-i-d-y-a".
So runs the text of the Gemara in literal Yiddish translation. And this very last sentence of the quotation has greatly interested many scholars.
— What can the sound of "R-i-d-y-a" mean, which is heard from one end of the world to the other? Might not this mysterious "R-i-d-y-a" have some connection with our present-day "R-a-d-i-o" of the 20th century?...
It is truly a very remarkable matter, which in any case sounds very strange and odd.
And when one also takes into account that lately people have in general reckoned[?] with the revelations of some Talmudic scholars that many of today's modern inventions in the fields of technology, physics, medicine and astronomy were already known to the authors of the Talmud — the whole story around the question truly comes out very striking:
— Did people in Talmudic times, thousands of years ago, really have a notion of radio?...
May a gas pipe serve as an earth for the radio?
In the big cities earthing [literally "burial"] is done in such a way that, instead of digging a deep pit in the ground, the radio amateur connects the wire of the radio set to the water pipes. Very often radio listeners also use the gas pipes to earth the aerial.
We point out that while the water pipes are an excellent means of earthing the aerial, one must beware of using the gas pipe for the same purpose. Firstly, the gas pipe does not connect the aerial with the earth as well as the water pipes do, so that the radio broadcasts are heard much more weakly; besides, the gas pipe also becomes dangerous in case of a storm. Lightning [literally "thunder"] may strike the gas pipe, which may cause a gas explosion.

“All may slaughter” — even a butcher too...

That tremendous lawlessness reigns in the field of ritual slaughter is no secret at all. It seems that since the Będzin kehilla has existed, shechita and kashrut have never been as neglected as in recent months: slaughtering goes on without supervision in cellars and little back rooms, and where not? The butcher was summoned to the rabbinate, where he declared that it was not he who had slaughtered the calf but a Christian.
The rabbinate regards the butcher's statement with distrust and informs the butchers that henceforth they are not to buy any veal from this butcher.
In this connection a consultation of several members of the kehilla board and of the council took place on Wednesday afternoon; they decided to ask the rabbinate what measures it intends to apply in order to put an end to the prevailing lawlessness in the field of kashrut.
Should Jewish children not also benefit from the summer colony through the sick fund?

Every year a certain number of children are sent to summer colonies at the expense of the sick fund (Kasa Chorych). Among the total number there was always also a certain number of Jewish children who were maintained by the sick fund.
This year — so we are informed — this privilege has been taken away from the Jewish children: among the 250 children who will be sent by the sick fund there is not a single Jewish child.
And the question arises: does the Jewish population not have the right to demand of the sick fund that Jewish children, too, should benefit from the summer colony just like the Christian children?
A board member or vice-chairman?

The kehilla board has sent Mr. N. Landner a written inquiry as to whether he wishes to become a member of the board in place of Mr. D. Rudzin, of blessed memory, or to retain his present function as vice-chairman of the council.
If Mr. Landner remains on the council, Mr. N. Tenenberg will join the board (dozór).
A festive dedication of a Torah scroll at “Sha'arei Zion”.

On Sunday the completion of a Torah scroll (siyum ha-sefer) was celebrated in Mr. Ch. Szajn's minyan called “Sha'arei Zion”. The writing of the letters took place “according to programme”; the badchan, Mr. Pozamentier[?], did the “calling up”, and the orchestra played a lively tune for each one.
The carrying of the new scroll into the minyan room passed off festively. After Mr. Baum, accompanied by his choir, sang “Le-David mizmor” and “Ki lekach tov natati lachem”, Mr. Yitzchak Wygodzki gave a short but substantial speech, in which he offered a historical survey of the time when the Jewish people fought its enemies with the sword, and later with the Torah, with Jewish culture, thanks to which it has [endured] in our existence as the People of the Book to this very day.
Later a banquet was held, in which only the worshippers with healthy stomachs took part, whereas the “weaker” part, those who “must rest after 10 o'clock”, soon left...
At the “table” Mr. Baum entertained the company by singing several prayers, and at the very end Mr. L. Goldsztajn delighted them with Jewish folk songs.
Bojarska's commercial school passes to the Small Traders' Association.

This week the agreement was signed under which Miss Bojarska's commercial school passes into the ownership of the Small Traders' Association.
In this connection it is already being said that this year's (women) graduates are to do practical training in the shops during the vacation.
Jewish candidates for the elections to the Chamber of Crafts

This week a conference took place at the Chamber of Crafts in Kielce, at which the candidates for the elections to the Chamber of Crafts were determined.
Mr. Goldsztajn took part in the conference on behalf of Zagłębie.
In the distribution by trades it turned out that the Będzin and Zawiercie districts (powiaty) will have 2 representatives in the Chamber of Crafts, boot-upper makers, in the persons of Mr. Daniel Kilsztok (Będzin) and Teichner (Sosnowiec).
About the summer colony of Fürstenberg's gymnasium.

As we have already written, this year's summer colony is being organised by the parents' committee of the Sz. Fürstenberg gymnasium in Mszana Dolna. This splendid place lies in the vicinity of Rabka (a 15-minute journey by train). The price for 40 days is 115 złoty (already including the costs of tickets, luggage, etc.).
Registrations are accepted until the 20th of this month at the office, every day from 9 to 2 [p.m.?].
Solemn oath of the young recruits.

On Friday the young recruits of the local regiment took the oath. The oath of the Jewish recruits, which took place in a solemn manner, was administered by Major[?] Steinberg, who came here specially.
Major Steinberg first conducted a prayer and then the oath.
Municipal Budget — Approved
The municipal budget came back this week approved by the voivodeship [provincial authorities], in accordance with the draft of the commissarial council.
A Teacher at the “Yesodei HaTorah” Heder in Dąbrowa — a “Nara” Member

On Friday a young Christian assailed three young Jews in Dąbrowa with antisemitic insults. The young men did not let anyone push them around [literally: blow into their porridge] and answered the antisemite with a “gift of the hand” [a slap]. The epilogue played out at the nearby police station, where it incidentally became clear that the Christian is neither more nor less than the teacher of the “Yesodei HaTorah” heder run by the “Agudah” [Agudath Israel].
The young men went to the kehilla office and demanded an immediate reaction to the teacher's insolence.
It would be interesting to know what the management of the “Yesodei HaTorah” heder has to say about this — it has the honour of counting a “Nara” [ONR, National-Radical Camp] member among its teaching staff — and likewise the Jewish kehilla, which subsidises this teaching staff?
Sosnowiec — Lacking a Few Złoty to Buy a Monthly Ticket, He Hanged Himself

Tragic suicide of a poor Jew.
At 1 Maja Street 12 lived the bagel seller Gronem Neuman with his family, which consists of a wife and 4 small children.
Neuman made his living selling bagels on the trains. At the beginning of the week he would buy a “weekly ticket” and travel with his goods. Lately, however, the “weekly tickets” were abolished; Neuman did not have the few złoty to buy a ticket and so had to stop running his bagel trade.
Last Friday Neuman came to the kehilla board member [dozór] Mr. Moshe Mordechai Weinstock and asked him to help him obtain a loan of at least 25 zł., with which he could go on feeding his hungry family. Mr. Weinstock promised to raise the sum and at the same time gave him a few guilders for Shabbat.
On Shabbat, however, at 8[?] in the afternoon, the tragedy happened: when Neuman found himself alone at home, he hanged himself with a belt on the door, which he had locked beforehand.
The wife, coming home and finding the door locked, raised an alarm; the neighbours came running, broke open the door and found the tragedy.
Neuman, who still showed signs of life, was taken to the Pekin hospital, where he died only on Monday during the day.
The suicide left 3 letters: 1) to his wife, whom he asks to forgive him for the terrible deed — “I could no longer — he writes to her — look on at the suffering of our children”; 2) to his brother-in-law Berliński, whom he asks to watch over the family he leaves behind; and 3) to the gmina [Jewish community], to give him an honourable grave and not to treat him as a suicide.
She Fainted Supposedly, but He, Poor Man, Fainted for Real...

This week a local merchant travelled by train to Łódź. In the same carriage a young lady was travelling too. When the train was approaching Piotrków, the young lady said: “Oh, I don't feel well,” and fell into a “faint”. At first the merchant even wanted to stop the train, but he thought better of it and set about reviving the young lady with his provisions for the journey — a piece of orange, even wine.
When the young lady came to, she would not stop thanking the young man who had revived her; she showered him with compliments, so that afterwards he himself was not feeling well...
When the train stopped at Koluszki, the “rescued” young lady excused herself to her “rescuer”: she had to get off at the station to take care of something.
The young man answered her with a smile and thought to himself: the good Lord knows what a young lady needs to take care of so quickly — but one doesn't question a story!
The train, however, did not wait for the young lady and went on.
— Oh well, the young man shrugged, a real pity; she'll take another “pociąg” [train], so be it.
Arriving in Łódź, the “rescuer” realised that, together with the “rescued” girl, his wallet with 800 złoty and other valuable papers had been stolen from him.
Only then did he understand that this was what the young lady had arranged for him while he was reviving her from a fake faint — and he himself fainted for real.
Not 10 but 9 Jewish Councillors...

As is known, Jewish Sosnowiec obtained 10 mandates in the last city council elections.
This week a change took place. The main electoral commission allotted the 10th mandate to the Sanacja [the ruling camp], thanks to the fact that the Sanacja has 25 councillors out of 48.
Out of One Trial and Into Another...

On Tuesday Mr. Jaskierowicz stood before the district court, charged with beating his competitor, Mr. Forstal of Będzin. The trial was adjourned. On leaving the court, the defendant again attacked Mr. Forstal and beat him. The police drew up a report about it.
—o—
A Jew Forces the Radomsko Rebbe to Take an Oath
The trial between Mr. Welgrin and his father-in-law Mr. S. Grünbaum, who is accused of taking a large sum of money from his son-in-law, has already come up several times before the local district court.
In this curious trial the Radomsko Rebbe is also summoned as a witness; each time he was unable to appear in court because of his poor state of health.
Last Monday the Rebbe came to the court in order to give his statements concerning the trial.
But Mr. Grünbaum and his “woman of valour” insisted throughout that the Rebbe take an oath, whereas Mr. Welgrin released the Rebbe from the oath.
Because of the Rebbe's refusal to take the oath, the hearing has for the time being been adjourned.
The behaviour of the Grünbaum family has aroused bitterness in Hasidic circles.
—o—
Meeting of “Torah va-Avodah”
On Sunday the annual general meeting of the T"vA movement took place at the premises of the Sosnowiec “Torah va-Avodah”, with the participation of central committee member Levi Yitzchak Jungster and member of the Moetza Mr. S. Gothard. A board was elected consisting of: Y. Windman, Blum[?], Zachariasz, Szklarszyk, Rogowski, Welgrin, Shlomo Rogowski, Narcyz, Ziegler.
—o—
Beware of Thefts
In connection with the fact that a large part of the population is now leaving for summer lodgings — and like mushrooms after rain, so thefts multiply at this time — it would be desirable for an ordinance to be issued requiring caretakers [stróże] to pay more attention to the flats left empty by the “letniki” [summer holidaymakers] during the summer season.
—o—
Mr. Liberman Not Confirmed as Chairman of the Kehilla Council
About 15 months ago, when the kehilla council in Dąbrowa was constituted, Mr. Hertzel Liberman was elected chairman.
This week the gmina received a notice from the Ministry of Religious Affairs that the election has not been confirmed.
—o—
Suicide of a Mentally Ill Woman in Dąbrowa
At the station in Dąbrowa a mentally ill Christian woman, 22 years old, threw herself under a passenger train. The suicide was killed on the spot.
—o—
Passenger Train Pelted with Stones beyond Zawiercie
Beyond Zawiercie the train arriving from Kraków was pelted with stones, which shattered several windowpanes. Fortunately none of the passengers was hurt; one stone struck the assistant engine driver on the head.
From Sports Life.

[Sports — Będzin, Sosnowiec.] "Hakoah" — "Sarmacja" 4:0
In the decisive championship match over staying in Class "A", "Hakoah" suffered a heavy defeat.
After this match the fate of "Hakoah" — to drop into Class "B" — has been as good as sealed. The same thing has happened this year to "Hakoah" as happened a year ago to Sosnowiec "Maccabi".
• • •
In accordance with the decision of the Maccabi World Union, the championship matches for the title of Jewish Champion of Poland will begin in the coming days. All Jewish Class "A" clubs of Poland will take part in the contest. An exception has been made for Sosnowiec "Maccabi". Already in the coming days the first championship match between "Hakoah" and "Maccabi" (Sosnowiec) begins.
Besides the title of champion, the winner will also receive a cup donated by the Maccabi World Union.
• • •
The new board of "Hakoah" — despite having been weakened, since several board members resigned their mandates — is working tirelessly to create its own stadium in Będzin.
The negotiations with the "Sosnowiec Company", the owners of the plot on which the stadium is to be built, are progressing quickly and promise to be settled favourably.
A. W-ski.
———
The rowing section of Sosnowiec "Maccabi" is holding, next Sunday the 10th of this month, rowing races for the club championship over 50 km, and 30 km for beginners. Start and finish at Ostrogórka.
———
The still-young sports club "Kadimah" in Będzin is showing, since its general meeting, much activity and promises good development.
A whole series of sections is being organised, for which special instructors have been engaged.

Protests by the P.P.S. against the City Council Elections.
Two protests by the P.P.S. [Polish Socialist Party] have been lodged with the Main Electoral Commission in Będzin. Because of this, the constitution of the new City Council is being held back for the time being.

Memorial Assembly on the Shloshim of M. Winer.

[Będzin — Revisionist movement; Brit HaChayal.] A communiqué sent in by "Brit HaChayal" in Będzin.
The command of "Brit HaChayal" in Będzin held a memorial assembly ("academy") dedicated to the memory of the unforgettable M. Winer.
As the curtain opens the Betar choir recites "Shiviti", and the "Hakoah" orchestra plays the anthems.
Commandant M. Glidman gives the opening address in Hebrew, Polish and Yiddish, and Mr. A. Diament takes the chair.
After the orchestra plays Chopin's Funeral March, telegrams of condolence from various organisations are read out.
Cantor Mr. Baum and the choir sing "El Male Rachamim" and "Ki Malachav" [misprinted "Ki Balachav"]; a deep impression is made by the recitations of Eliezer Eksztajn (Sosnowiec): 1) "Ikh volt geven a ..." [title partly illegible] (Bialik); 2) "Es glust zikh mir veynen" ("I long to weep") (Bialik), etc. In the last part of the assembly the chairman A. Diament gives a speech in which he describes the human greatness of the tragically perished man.
The most important part of the assembly ends with a splendid lecture given by Mgr. Dr. J. Szechter (in Polish).
The speaker illuminates with splendid rhetoric the idea of Kiddush HaShem and self-sacrifice, which are a leitmotif of the Revisionist movement.
The memorial assembly is closed with "Hatikvah".
