Hitlerite associations in Upper Silesia dissolved / Young Christians treat Jewish children to chocolate in Sosnowiec / The first group of children to the summer colonies / A theft in a grocery shop in Sosnowiec / Today — the last day

Yesterday, by an order of the police directorate in Katowice, the associations of the Polish National Socialists in the territory of the Katowice (Silesian) voivodeship were dissolved.
The members are also forbidden to wear the red[?] uniforms.
The reason for the dissolution is that the organisation's activities are in conflict with public security.
The order states that belonging to the organisation will be severely punished.
—o—
Young Christians treat Jewish children to chocolate in Sosnowiec
In recent weeks we were given a series of reports that Christians were handing out sweets to Jewish children. We did not take these reports into consideration, especially after similar reports were also denied in the Warsaw Jewish press.
Last Wednesday, however, Mr. Dimant[?], who lives in Sosnowiec on Mila Street [ul. Miła?], came to us and reported that 2 Christian[?] young men approached several Jewish children who were playing in the courtyard where he lives, and wanted to treat the children to chocolate.
The children, however, refused the gift
—o—
The first group of children to the summer colonies
Yesterday and today the first group of schoolchildren already left for the summer colonies in Sławków, the property of the Będzin municipality (magistrat). About 300 girls went.
The children maintained at the expense of the sickness fund (Kasa Chorych) also left.
As we have already written, this year the sickness fund is sending only Christian children.
We have already touched on this scandalous fact, but we do not hear that any of the Jewish public figures are giving it a thought...
—o—
A theft in a grocery shop in Sosnowiec
During the night from Saturday to Sunday, by breaking open the grilles of Mehin's[?] grocery (colonial goods) shop, various grocery goods were stolen.

The lottery and life

Thousands of people ask themselves daily the question: what does one do in order to win in the lottery?
It goes without saying that those who have won can best answer this. But the one who has won does not like to tell, because he is afraid that all his friends and acquaintances will turn to him for a loan. So he goes on playing with a „greybshtendn“[?] laugh on his lips, as though he had not won, and he explains the improvement of his material situation by the improvement of his business.
What interests people most is the fact that one person does not win even once, and another wins a second, third and more times. How can this chance be explained?
Most players pay no attention to the psychological state of those who win. The one who has won certainly did not become disillusioned with playing the lottery. Surely he did not win the first time he bought a ticket. Surely he also bought a second ticket, which brought him nothing, but he believed that he would win. He went on playing and in the end — won.
With the lottery it is just as in life. Man's greatest enemy is disappointment and losing hope — man's greatest virtue is perseverance. In life one can always notice that things do not go right for a person because, when he begins doing something, he is soon disappointed, throws it away and turns on to something else. Such a person can never have anything. Another, with greater endurance, aims at the trodden path, and the result is a good one.
Playing the lottery is the same!
So those who have not yet won must remember that the drawing of the first class begins on the 19th of this month, and if they have not yet won, they now have every chance of winning.
One just must not be disappointed!
W311

The Dąbrowa Jewish Kehilla Welcomes Bishop Kubina of Częstochowa with a Torah Scroll under a Canopy

[Dąbrowa — kehilla; the bishop's visit.] On Saturday and Sunday Bishop Kubina of Częstochowa stayed in Dąbrowa [Górnicza] in honour of the Christian congress.
When the Dąbrowa heads of the kehilla learned that the bishop was coming to Dąbrowa, they reckoned that the kehilla must welcome the high guest. And indeed a delegation — kehilla president Mr. Najfeld, vice-president Mr. L. Rechnitz and Mr. D. Grynbaum — went to the local priest to inform him that the holy community of Dąbrowa wished to have the honour of taking an official part in the reception in honour of the distinguished guest.
The priest received the delegation very politely, thanked them several times for the honour and spent some time in conversation with the delegation, during which the priest declared that "Poland is not only for us, but also for you."
The priest's polite reception is what really gave courage to the "wise and understanding men", who set about energetically organising things so that the Dąbrowa kehilla's reception would turn out in splendour and glory. For that purpose they invited for the Sabbath the rabbi of Strzemieszyce, and also a row of householders, the town's notables — rich Jews without beards and Jews who have no money but fine silvery-white beards, the elders of the town.
At the appointed hour the delegation, with the heads of the kehilla at its head, went to Żwirki i Wigury Square, where the official reception was to be held.
The organisers of the reception were scrupulous about the fact that it was the Sabbath, and also took along a Torah scroll. True, it had been given to "HaShomer HaDati", but just standing like that with the scroll would not have been fitting, so they brought the canopy, under which the vice-president of the kehilla council, Reb Avraham Leibish Fuks, held the Torah scroll. The poles of the canopy were decorated with white-and-blue and white-and-yellow ribbons.
At about 4 o'clock the bishop arrived and was greeted by the local president [mayor] Kaczkowski; in the name of the reception committee — advocate Margolis and others.
After the greetings the bishop was promptly led under the prepared canopy, and the procession at once moved into the church.
As he walked, the bishop bestowed his attention on all the delegations, among them the Jewish one too, which by then was no longer standing at the place the reception committee had assigned to it, but already somewhat off to the side.
The Jews (with red, flushed faces — perhaps from shame or from distress) then went home in haste; for the honour of the Torah they could no longer stand in the street amid the huge Christian crowd, especially on the Sabbath...
The rabbi, who had come specially from Strzemieszyce, naturally did not deliver his prepared sermon, and so the interpreter, Mr. B. Rechnitz, also had nothing to do.
According to what Christians report, the bishop, in his speech in the church, among other things also thanked the Jewish population for its reception.
The Participation of Jews in the Liberation of Poland

[Katowice — lecture; history.] (From Prof. Bałaban's lecture in Katowice.)
In connection with the 125th anniversary of the death of the Jewish colonel in the Polish army, Berek Joselewicz, the Association of Jewish Fighters for the Liberation of Poland in Katowice organised a lecture by the well-known historian Prof. Dr. Majer Bałaban of Warsaw on the subject: "Jews with Weapons in Hand".
Before a packed hall the chairman of the Katowice federation opened the evening and, greeting him in warm words, gave the floor to the distinguished lecturer.
Prof. Bałaban gives a historical survey of the Jews in Palestine and in the Diaspora, where they bore arms already 800 years before Berek Joselewicz. Also known were Lisowski's Cossacks [the lisowczycy], in which Jews were strongly represented. We also know from writings found with the rabbis in the 17th century that in the time of Władysław IV Jews served in the army, because very many women turned to the local rabbis to establish officially the actual death of their husbands who had perished in various battles. At the court of King Stefan Batory a Jewish soldier was known whom the king, for his merits, made one of the royal secretaries.
At the end of the 18th century, soon after the French Revolution, the two Jews Berek Joselewicz and Józef Aronowicz received permission from Kościuszko to recruit soldiers; Berek Joselewicz at that time, together with other troops, fought a battle with the Russian army and was then severely wounded. Known is the legend of Szmul Zbytkower, who set out two small barrels with gold and silver ducats, and to everyone who brought a living Jew he gave a gold ducat, and for a dead one a silver ducat; he thereby sought to stop the slaughter.
The distinguished speaker reads very interesting letters between General Dąbrowski and Berek Joselewicz.
In 1802 Berek Joselewicz submits his resignation and it is accepted. In 1804 he is again in the "Hantverer"[?] regiment as a captain, and then in 1807 he is in Greater Poland in the 3rd regiment and takes part in the fighting at Tczew and Gdańsk.
In 1808 he receives a golden cross of merit.
Then comes the famous battle at Kock, where he fights a bitter struggle with the Austrian hussars, who on 5 May 1809 surround him on all sides, and on that same day he is killed.
Berek Joselewicz is a symbol of Jewish heroism. Among others the lecturer mentions one Jakub Szpat of B ę d z i n, who was an officer and, at the head of 200 men, led several battles in 1808 and held out to the end; and also the art painter who died not long ago, Leopold Gottlieb, who, being on the battlefield already with Piłsudski's Legions, immortalised the last Polish battles with his brush. His pictures are in the Polish National Museum.
Thus Jews have always fought for Poland and will go on fighting, and the rights we have won we will not let be taken away from us — so Prof. Bałaban ends his lecture.
The numerous audience rewarded the distinguished lecturer and well-known historian with prolonged applause.
S. S.

Polish Jews in Palestine Have Created a New Institution, "Hashgachah"

[Palestine — economy; Polish Jews.] Through the central committee of the Association of Polish Jews a new institution has been created under the name "Hashgachah" ("Supervision"), whose aim is to look after the property of the Polish Jews [in] Palestine and to manage it.
In the course of the last 2 years many tourists came from Poland, who invested their money in houses, building plots and the like.
Before leaving the country they faced the problem: whom can one rely on, and with whom can they leave their property — above all with a public institution. For this reason the new institution "Hashgachah" was created, whose task is to save much of the property of the Polish Jews from ruin.
The institution will strengthen the confidence of the Jewish-Polish capitalists in Palestine and also consolidate the financial investments in the country.

A Jewish Beggar Caused the Untimely Death of a Beit-Midrash Gabbai in Modrzejów

[Modrzejów — crime; beit midrash.] The small town of Modrzejów (near Sosnowiec) is under the impression of the misfortune that occurred there, with the tragic death of the gabbai, 48-year-old Nachman Rebnic.
The story is as follows:
A few weeks ago the tragically deceased Rebnic was woken from sleep by several beggars, who wanted Rebnic to give them the key of the beit midrash, where they wanted to spend the night.
Rebnic got dressed, went with them and unlocked the beit midrash. But one of the beggars wanted to bring his wife too into the beit midrash to spend the night; when Rebnic, naturally, did not permit this and resisted, the beggar dealt him a kick in the stomach, from which he immediately fainted.
The doctors who were called declared that Rebnic's condition was serious and that he must be operated on at once.
R. was immediately taken to the Jewish hospital in Sosnowiec, where the necessary operation was performed on him, and the patient's condition began to improve.
Last week a change suddenly set in, and on Sunday Rebnic died.
The beggar who by his brutal deed caused this loss has been arrested in Königshütte [Królewska Huta, Chorzów].

A Letter to the Editor.
[Letter to the editor — the town synagogue.] Esteemed Editors!
More than once attention has been drawn in the columns of your esteemed paper to the various acts of mischief that occur from time to time in the local town synagogue, but what happened last Sabbath simply smacks of a scandal.
The impudence of the two young men, who seized the bimah by force, held up the Torah reading, did not find it necessary to ask permission from the kehilla or from the gabbaim who were present in the synagogue, but treated the synagogue as no-man's-land with the help of "their own people", and in an unheard-of manner exploited the synagogue for political demonstrations, turning a holy place into a street rally with shouts of "Down with", "Long live", just like in the year 1905, as if it were revolutionism and heroism — aroused great indignation among all the worshippers of the synagogue.
The synagogue committee, not wishing to provoke scandals which might perhaps have led to bloodshed, controlled the agitated mood and did not react at the time to the irresponsible behaviour of the two young men, who supposedly represented a political organization that preaches the "Kingdom of Israel" on both sides of the Jordan, and as such they ought to have shown more tact and not desecrated a holy place. We express our strongest protest against this system of lawlessness, and we warn the public that in future such wild outbursts will no longer be tolerated.
In the name of the synagogue committee
Aron Hercyger

Society and the Course of Our Life

[Editorial — Zagłębie; the economic crisis; a suicide in Sosnowiec; the trade unions.]
The situation is unbearably hard, conditions are enormously strained. Jewish life has become impoverished to the highest degree.

When a person from other places comes here to us, he is amazed[?]. Here — he says — with you in Zagłębie people are still living; here there is movement, here people trade, here people travel and things are moving, while back home everything has died away and life has all but[?] stopped pulsing. So we here, the inhabitants of Zagłębie, are envied for still being alive, at a time when elsewhere there are only shadows of life, signs of a former existence.

But what the "rich" Jewish life in Zagłębie looks like in reality can be characterised by the latest incident, which happened last week in Sosnowiec, that is, in the "best" situated town of Zagłębie.

A Jew who trades in bagels — and according to the Urząd Skarbowy (tax office) he is surely a "merchant". This very Jew travelled every day with the bagels to Upper Silesia. Every week he took out a weekly ticket and somehow made a living with these bagels; but his bitter fate willed that the weekly tickets be abolished, so that he was forced to buy a monthly ticket. Yet since he was no longer so "r i c h", he began to torment himself, and the money for a monthly ticket he could by no means scrape together. Having free travel for a whole month was for him a fantasy that could never come true, and the end was that he saw he had nothing left to go on knocking about the world for, that he was superfluous among us here — and he took his own life.

There is a little flower of the fantastic wealth of Zagłębie. The outward glitter dazzles, and the stranger, the visitor[?], thinks that here people live and earn, while here we have the same shadows as in all of Poland.

Zagłębie in general, and its Jews in particular, is impoverished beyond imagining; only, from outside one does not see[?] it, thanks to the fact that from old times people here were better situated. One still had, after a fashion, something to live on, and as the reserves ran out long ago, people began partly to pawn objects and partly to sell them — and that is how one lives. People wanted to drag things out "as far as the tavern", until the crisis passes, because they persuaded themselves, as at the outbreak of the war, that this was a matter of a few weeks. But as we see, everything has already been exhausted, and it has led to such a sad state that a dealer who formerly made a quite respectable living had at this moment to part with the world, because he did not have a few spare gulden [złoty] to lay out, which his penny trade demanded.

Of course, this incident is not the first in the present crisis period, but the trouble is that people have begun to look on indifferently at all these events, which make our already sad enough life ever more abnormal.

But the question arises: may we look on these catastrophes with the same indifference with which we have grown used to them? May we make of the prevailing abnormality a quite normal phenomenon? True, the troubles, the difficult situation in which the world finds itself and into which it has dragged us Jews even further, have taught us to get used to everything and to be able to bear everything; but that still does not mean that we must regard abnormal phenomena as normal, as healthy, and treat them as such.

We understand that one must be steadfast, that one must know how and understand how to bear on one's own shoulders the hardest of the people's sufferings and troubles. On the other hand, one must not let the sick, the dangerous, become embodied and take root in the healthy body, because it poisons the organism, and then it will already be too late to come with remedies.

We have today, for example, at every step associations and institutions, so that the human being as such, as a free person with independent thoughts, one does not see[?] at all. Whatever one would[?] touch, it is only party and party, and it turns out that the person without the party, without an association, is a complete zero. So one ought surely to ask the question: what does it do for him in time of danger, why does it not rescue him, when he is a part of this very body?

Let us take, for example, the tragically deceased Najman[?]: had his trade union been interested in him, had he been a part of its body, he would have had someone before whom to pour out his bitter heart, someone with whom to share his grief — and the catastrophe would surely not have come about. An association, and a professional one at that, as soon as it exists, as soon as it has members, must first and foremost concern itself with the material situation of the member, and must bring things to the point where it is his ideal, his darling, his personal devoted friend.

The trade union must be either everything to the member, or, if not, it would be better for it to be nothing at all, because, as we see, if it brings no benefit, it is not merely useless, but actually harmful at every step — and this must not be permitted, this must not be tolerated.

Let us cast a glance at the catastrophic events, which bring in so much poison and poison the body that, for the time being, is still healthy. Let us not permit, with a light conscience, the destruction of that which must be healthy. The people as such must see to it that its soul, its spirit, its ideal be sound to the core, and that on these foundations it continue the further course of life.
Dr. Papuri.
Those Who Have Been Placed over Jewishness.

Everywhere and all over, in every institution and in every society, lawlessness (hefkeyres) is gaining the upper hand. And it is characteristic that the more lawlessness prevails, the more courage and audacity people have to come to the masses and demand of them responsibility and commitment for this very problem.
We now pause on Jewishness. Jewishness in the true sense of the word — truly, this is no topic and no problem for the writer of these lines, if only because we have someone to take care of these matters; we pay for it so that those who are called to it, those who are competent in it, should take care of it.
Thus last week an uproar arose: in Będzin a butcher was caught who slaughters calves himself, or hands the work over — as he himself declared — to a Christian. The rabbinate is surely reacting to this. Characteristic, however, is that never before has so much lawlessness prevailed in this field as we hear of today, when there are so many supervisors of kashrut and whatever else, and you are told loudly that more trustees (ne'emanim), more dayanim, more shochtim are needed, more supervisors over these very supervisors.
It is, for instance, no secret that the government is on the side[?] of the clergy (kley-koydesh) and strictly[?] sees to it that they should be the first to receive the money; they thus have the possibility to keep their responsible post[?]. So the question arises: why do they not fulfil their tasks, which are their only mission? To this one must answer that in this field too lawlessness reigns without measure, and it has been brought to the point that the butchers exploit[?] it splendidly at every opportunity, so that they take the accepted rules lightly and do[?] with a calm conscience everything that is convenient and agreeable in their eyes. The rabbinate apparently has no time to watch over all this, because one has to ponder and scheme and think how to smuggle in yet a lot of relatives and "men of our circle" (anshey shlomeynu), who are to ride on the kehilla's shoulders — which, by the way, are already today loaded and burdened enough, so that the Jewish population is no longer able to carry them on its bent, exhausted shoulders.
But, when it comes to it, everything is ownerless in Jewish life, so why should there be an exception here? Why should our clergy not adapt themselves to today's modernised times?
We have nothing against our clergy when they want to go with the times and modernise themselves. But in that case, what use are the masks, and the rolling of the eyes up to heaven at every opportunity, and demonstrating again and again that all this is done in the name of the holy Torah and that it is they who make the world happy and uphold Jewishness?
Try, if it is possible to talk to such a one: he will clearly prove to you that by his merit and their holiness we live; if not for them — such a one will explain to you quite seriously — Jewishness would long since have ceased to exist.
But if you talk with a truly observant Jew, with an honest ben-Torah, he will make a bitter face and lament that Jewishness has fallen so low and has become for everyone a kind of "spade to dig with" (kardom lachpor bo).
The question of the shochtim and the cantorship[?] and the whole kehilla system is in such a sad state that it is nauseating to speak of it; it is simply a desecration of God's name (chilul hashem) to treat it before the public, before the broad strata of the population.
Selekt.
G. Kuper. Bravo, Herr Goebbels! (Instead of a “Welcome” on His Coming to Poland).

We have long known that Dr. Paul Joseph Goebbels, the propaganda minister of Hitler's Germany, knows his trade and is a master of his propaganda profession.
He showed it as soon as he became minister. No sooner had he sat himself down on the soft ministerial chair than he at once set about making the German book market famous and making a name for it all over the world. For years the world had known of German works, German books were popular — but never were they as popular as when Propaganda Minister Goebbels took them in hand and burned them on Berlin's main streets. The whole world was then seething over Germany; everywhere people talked and wrote about Goebbels's brilliant idea, and Germany's name grew.
Having done the first bit of cultural work for the country, Propaganda Minister Goebbels saw to doing something also for propagandising German trade and industry. He very easily let Jewish trade and industry be ruined, for the welfare of the pure, kosher Aryans. In the very shortest time he brought it about through propaganda that all the enemies of the newly arisen Germany throughout the whole world — all Jews, socialists, liberals, intellectuals, apart from others — should have nothing whatever to do with genuine-German, pure-Aryan trade and industry. These enemies of Germany will not live to see German merchants and workers working for them, producing goods for their use; they are not too sick [i.e. not reluctant] to buy other articles, not genuinely German. With genuine German punctuality and diligence the propaganda minister carried out his difficult work.
He brought it so far that Germany now can no longer pay its debts to the foreign creditors, among whom there are many Jews. Serves them right! (a mitsve af zey!) — In a word, since Germany has existed, never has so much been said and written about its trade and industry. And all this thanks to Goebbels's propaganda.
When trade and industry had already been duly propagandised and worked over, Mr. Goebbels did not rest, but set about propagandising the German film, theatre and the press. Here too he displayed his brilliant propaganda talents, as earlier in industry, and made the theatre and the press very famous in the world. Not a day passes without the world writing about German films, theatres and newspapers. True, in the last year and a half hundreds of cinemas have closed, thousands of actors have been left without work, and the newspapers are dying off like flies in autumn — but people ask about them everywhere, write about it, and that makes them very popular and famous abroad. And that, after all, is the task of a propaganda minister: to make his country's achievements famous and popular in the world.
It is impossible to enumerate in a newspaper feuilleton the many important propaganda works that this meritorious, extraordinary[?] man has done in the short time he has sat on the ministerial chair. But what he has lately been doing for German tourism surpasses all comprehension.
As is well known, he had already earlier made German ships very famous in the world. He brought it about that all enemies of Germany no longer dare to set foot on a German ship. The ships sail only with genuine-German sailors, accompanied by the melodious Nazi songs and Hitler's radio speeches. But since he was afraid that German railways and aeroplanes might envy the ships' popularity, he has now set about making them famous in the world too.
Well, since Goebbels, as a brilliant propagandist, knows that for propaganda one must win over the foreign press, he did indeed have his first "job"[?] done through a journalist of an American newspaper. He chose a big newspaper, the "Times"; he had the American correspondent, who wanted to fly in a German aeroplane from Berlin to Paris, very thoroughly stripped naked, as his mother bore him; they searched him for money in his clothes, shoes, toothbrushes and other hiding places for so long that the naked correspondent missed the aeroplane. Afterwards the German searcher shouted "Heil Hitler" and — basta!
As was to be expected, the correspondent, as soon as he had snatched his trousers back on, immediately telegraphed about it all to his newspaper. All the other newspapers reprinted the lovely story, and the propaganda for German tourism keeps growing. The whole world rings with it.
Bravo, brilliant Herr Goebbels! Work, work for your Germany, do not rest, make more such fine things and the country will remember you.
Even we Jews, your enemies, appreciate your great propaganda talents.
Perhaps it would even be only fair to engage Goebbels to lead the anti-Nazi work here among us?
For nobody does it the way he does.
Bravo!
Rabbis Plead and Cardinals Answer

[Essay — Jews and the Church; antisemitism.] S. Rotenberg.
The Middle Ages.
Across the whole of Europe, camps of crusaders march in the most varied costumes. On black, brown, green and amaranth garments a great cross is embroidered — the symbol of love for one's neighbour, of forgiveness and humility. Like fiery lava, hundreds of thousands of people pour forth — men, women and children, knights and mercenaries, princes and guild journeymen, believing fanatics and free adventurers — yet not in order to spread the word of God, but in order to rob and murder weak and defenceless people.
The 3 words of Pope Urban the Second, „Deus le volt“ (God wills it), which were the signal for the Crusades, were enough for the world to be seized by an enormous conflagration, for whole human settlements and cities to be wiped off the face of the earth. Old people, women and children were mercilessly slaughtered, and, as always in history, the first victims were naturally the weakest of the weak, the eternal scapegoat of world history — the Jews.
Without any why or wherefore, whole Jewish communities were murdered and their goods and possessions plundered.
Rabbis sanctified the Name of God [died as martyrs] and went to beg the mighty bishops and cardinals for protection. But there they were answered that the Jews are the devil's children, blasphemers, sorcerers, that they drink Christian blood and poison the wells.
* * *
1934.
The century of radio, television and stratosphere flights.
Again [printed „virer“] the world has been flooded with shirts of various colours. Only the rulers and the symbols have changed. Instead of a cross — which recalls the „pale Jew of Nazareth“ — a swastika. And a new act of violence is being committed against humanity: instead of a crusade we now have a cruel swastika-crusade, which in its cruelty far surpasses all the medieval methods of the Inquisition.
But how is this possible — it is 1934, after all?
I am holding in my hand a newspaper which was set on a Linotype and printed on a rotary press that throws out 100 thousand copies an hour. I read there about the latest achievements in the field of television — that already in the near future one will be able to hear and see at home everything that happens in the whole world. Further on I read about the newest scientific research on the splitting of atoms, in which enormous quantities of energy lie hidden, about successful attempts to revive the dead, etc., etc. One is seized by a deep inner joy at living in such an epoch of so colossal an upsurge of the human spirit.
But this joy vanishes like a „fata morgana“, like a sweet dream, when one sees on the other side of the very same newspaper the daily chronicle: — „Nara“ people [probably members of the ONR, the National-Radical Camp] have again bloodily beaten up Jews; a blood-libel trial in Vienna; a Talmud trial in Katowice; and further — a delegation of rabbis asks the Cardinal for protection, and the Cardinal answers: — the Jews are blasphemers, they spread heresy and pornography, the Jewish youth is communist.
* * *
Barely a thousand years separate us from these 2 epochs; much has changed in that time, only one thing has remained standing at the dead point — rabbis plead and cardinals answer.
But the question arises: in whose name did the rabbis go to plead? After all, one no longer lives today in a ghetto, where the only representatives of the people are the rabbis. Hundreds of thousands of Jews hold today that our rights must be obtained not by bowing and begging for mercy, and that our whole struggle up to now is precisely so as not to return to the epoch of the bear-dance, of „Mah Yafit“ and of „Moshkism“ [?; servile Jewish fawning, from the derogatory „Moszek“].
Every self-respecting person must surely turn red with shame on reading the dispute between the rabbis and the Cardinal: on one side a crawling submissiveness, on the other a clear and open accusation against the Jews.
Why did the rabbis not have the courage to answer that, even if a certain part of the Jewish youth is imbued with the socialist ideal, this is because the conditions in which they live push them into other camps?
But as long as crawling „Moshkes“ exist, the conversations will remain just as they were a thousand years ago.
Rabbis will plead and cardinals will answer...
Who Is to Blame? (A Reply to Mr. Wygodzki)

(A reply to Mr. Wygodzki)
In No. 22 of the "Zaglembier Tsaytung", Mr. Y. Wygodzki turns with a demand to Mrs. Ts. Szajn and Mr. L. Rubinlicht to lay down their mandates in the city council, so as not to sit with the "bench-buyers at the expense of Jewish interests".
As one of those who had an interest in the creation of the general Jewish electoral bloc, having been delegated by the Revisionist groupings, I permit myself to answer Mr. Wygodzki as follows:
The actual culprits in the defeat of the highly respected public emissary Dr. Weigzieher [sic, = Weinzieher] are the delegates of the so-called "General Zionists", who at the first meeting of the bloc proposed the candidacy at the expense of Dr. Weigzieher and later even added the Zionist candidate Mr. Yakov Gutman! This is not the place to recount the irresponsible deeds of these gentlemen in order to make impossible the mandate of the Revisionist candidate, who wanted to be none other than Mr. Montag, and whom the so-called General Zionists could not reject as a person with a "new face".
At the first meeting, which took place on Thursday, the role of these gentlemen became clear: not [?] to advance the candidacies of the Zionist groupings — Revisionists, Mizrachi and Hitachdut — in order to bring in so-called important prominent, representable figures, coloured in the well-known type of "non-...ist" [?]; that kind of personal self-advertisement; and they did not speak of a national front, as befits "fighters", did not mention the Zionist bloc, but agitated for important individualists!
And we ask: what did the Zionist groupings — Revisionists, Mizrachi, Hitachdut — want to do, which are at the very least no worse Zionists than Messrs. Wygodzki and company?
The ballot slips were ordered by the above-mentioned General Zionists, and like that type [printed "sip"] who "eats and wipes her mouth", the gentlemen came at the last minute, "on that night", with the whole lexicon of insults, and just as at the unfortunate 18th Congress dragged the tragic deceased Dr. Arlosoroff of blessed memory out of the grave in order to fall upon us, the bearers of State Zionism, and hastened to issue a proclamation in the well-known language of "Separate yourselves".
The situation was painful to me, since with all means I wanted to avoid the bloodshed of Mr. Rubinlicht! But the situation was: exclude the "murderers"! I have the treacherous [?] slip; obeyed the morality preachers to their faces.. It worked.. and the General Zionist Mr. Yitzchak Wygodzki together with Mr. Leybl Goldsztajn took the "murderers" "pod pachę" [Polish: arm in arm] into a separate room, in order "to save the situation" together.
Then on Sunday morning — "Every man to his tents, O Israel". That is, everyone lived by "Chai" [the list number, 18]! And completely forgot about the candidates, and in particular about Dr. Weigzieher and Yakov Gutman! And did not lift a hand to save the situation, but printed other slips, lived by "Chai"!
And we ask once more: what is this? "Naivety", or some other name? How did you, honourable gentlemen, work for the honourable and respected Dr. Weigzieher? No more than 25 "Chai" votes could have saved the situation, so that you, Mr. Wygodzki, would not have to write your laments. If you yourselves are guilty, then do not throw yourselves upon others! You surely remember the story: when the bear attacked 2 friends — one, the clever one, climbed up the tree, and the 2nd played dead. The bear sniffed at the "dead" one; afterwards the clever one asks his friend: what did the bear whisper to you? And he answers him: "Base is your friend who abandons you in danger" — that is what the bear whispered to me...
Yes, Mr. Wygodzki! Your anger reminds me of the saying: "Jupiter! Your anger is a sign that you are wrong."
Avraham Diamant.
My First Oneg-Dacha!...

[Humorous feuilleton — summer holidays.] By Y. Oberzhanek [J. Oberżanek?].
As told by a "letnik" [summer holidaymaker].

Gentlemen, wish me mazel tov: I am already living, in a lucky hour, at a dacha — that is, my little wife is already living at the dacha.
Where do I live? At which dacha? Never mind where; the main thing is that my little wife is a "letniczka" [summer guest] and I am a "słomiany wdowiec" [a "straw widower"].
A fine thing, I tell you, to be a straw widower. True, you do get worn to shreds, you get blackened with grime, it costs money, you don't eat enough, you don't drink enough and you don't sleep enough — but in return you are a "wolny ptaszek" [a free little bird]. No onlookers, no opinion-givers, no question-askers; you throw off the yoke [chomąto, horse collar], you become a free bird. No more husband — a bachelor again, and what a life!
When was all this said? When did a straw widower live it up? When the coins were jingling in the pocket. Then, in those good times, a straw widower caroused so as to "make use" [użyć] of the world. Then one could "take advantage" [skorzystać] of the "occasion" [okazja]: as soon as the summer wife had kissed the mezuzah on the other side of the door, one said a shehecheyanu and began to "renew" [odnawiać] those couple of years.
First of all one took off the wedding ring, which is a charm for "success" [?, probably powodzenie]; every day freshly shaved, the hair combed with a "perzhal" [?, perhaps a parting]; every day a white collar, ties and suits changed often, trousers worn with a crease. Every evening to a different cinema, and certainly not "solo" — always with "something on the side".
At the restaurant one ate lunches of 5 "courses", and after the meal one had 12 "goings"... After supper one went up to the "Górka" [the hill] to draw some air, and one "drew" [pun: also "did business"] only after midnight; one went home to sleep when one no longer had to pay the watchman [stróż] for the gate, slept until noon — and "the Jews had light"!..
All this was once, in those good times. When it was cosy in the pocket — then one knew the taste of being a straw widower. But now other times have come: in the pocket it is sad [smutno], in the cash box there is a "draught" [przeciąg], everyone has become short-sighted and can't see a single grosz before their eyes.
So this year I really have to adapt myself to the times. I don't go to a restaurant; I have set up my own restaurant. I cook myself and eat myself — well, woe and alas for the cooking and for the eating.
In the morning I run with the little pot to the "shvayger" [?, probably "shvaytser" — the dairyman] for milk; I make a fire — the stove doesn't draw, there's no draught; I strike matches [zapałki], pour paraffin, cut kindling, stuff in old newspapers, I look like a chimney sweep; I put the pot of milk on the stove and run to the shop for rolls, and by the time I come back with the rolls the milk is... on the floor [podłoga].
Later I go to the butcher's stall to buy meat, and the butcher asks me:
— Do you want it for soup, or for a stew?
I stand there embarrassed and don't know what to answer — what is the difference between a soup and a stew?
The butcher sees that I don't know my way around these things and gives me to understand that for soup one takes one kind of meat and for a stew another kind of meat.
— Give me — I say — whatever is lighter.
— Then take veal, or minced meat.
— What's the difference between veal and minced meat? — I go on asking the butcher.
— That a person should be such a shlimazl! — the butcher marvels. — Veal is for soup, and from minced meat you can make cutlets, a meat loaf.
— Well, then let it be for soup, because I have a weak stomach. So I answered the butcher, and he gave me meat for soup.
Well, what does one put into the soup? You can't eat just meat, so I decided to cook a few noodles.
I bought flour, two eggs, and set about making a dough. I poured in flour and poured in water. I added flour — it became hard as a stone; I added water — it ran all over, and everything got full of dough. The suit with dough, the trousers with dough, dough on the floor, dough on the beds, dough on the writing desk; there was plenty of dough everywhere, except... on the noodle board!... The height of it was that the water in the pot boiled away, the meat got "scorched", and after three hours of work — after three hours of lighting, chopping, kneading and rolling — I went down into the street, starving to death, to look for a lunch...
And running the household — is that a trifle? Making the beds yourself, washing the dishes, sweeping the rooms, dusting the walls, beating the rugs [chodniki] — an "important" [ważna] job for a man! Who remembers to put on a clean collar, to wear pressed trousers, to sit in the cinema with "something on the side", to go up the "Górka" after midnight, to come home in the morning — gone are those good times when a straw widower "made use" [użył] of a few dacha weeks; gone are those golden times!
Never mind — running the household is only half the trouble; as you say, one manages: if you have the złoty, you eat; if not, you eat "baldness" [i.e., nothing] with sour milk. But the worst is the "first trip out". The summer wives won't hear of any excuses; they know that the letnik comes for Shabbat, so he has to bring the Shabbat luggage: a piece of chicken, a cooked little fish, challahs, a "mandl" [fifteen] of eggs, a few strawberries [truskawki] and above all — cash!
And the worst really is the "first trip out". On the first trip out one has to keep up "style"; one summer wife "shows off" [stawia się] before the other: one tells that her husband brought a live carp, the second tells that her husband brought a live tench with a young gosling, along comes a third and shows off a new deck chair [leżak], and the fourth brings a hammock with a deck chair.
Now I really am getting ready for the first trip out to the dacha. Go I must, the Shabbat luggage I must bring, and there isn't a grosz to my soul — and worst of all, I don't know where my wife's dacha is: I quite forgot to ask which dacha she went to and what the landlord is called.
Gentlemen, you can wish me mazel tov — me. That is — my wife is already living, in a lucky hour, at the dacha, and I am already a straw widower: I run a restaurant all by myself, cook myself soup with noodles, go to the butcher myself to buy meat, boil milk myself and make the fire in the stove myself, wash the dishes myself, sweep out the house and dust the walls myself — I am a straw widower!
Fellow Jews, have a good Shabbat; I'm off to my wife at the dacha — perhaps you know where my wife's dacha is?
On the Abolition of the “Jewish” Public Elementary Schools

In recent days we learned from the press that the school authorities, in agreement with the Ministry of Education, have set themselves the task of unifying the school system in such a way as may completely change the foundation and character of the education given “until now” to the Jewish child.
Speaking openly and plainly, “unification” means the complete liquidation of the “Jewish” public elementary schools (powszechne), the so-called “szabasówki”. Technically this is to be carried out as follows: the city will be divided into school districts, and the districts will be cut in such a way that in every school the composition of the children will be mixed, and lessons will also have to take place on the Sabbath and not on Sunday. If the Jewish children do not want to lose a day of the week, they will of necessity be forced to go to school on the Sabbath and on Jewish festivals, since on Sundays and [Christian] holidays the schools will of course be closed. And in order to “make kosher” this act of violence, it was also found necessary to hear the opinion of the school superintendents (kuratorzy). The school superintendents indeed discussed this project at a conference of theirs in Warsaw and, as a matter of course, “blessed” it and gave it their full approval.
Now the school authorities have set about realising this project. The beginning was made in Lublin! There the decree struck deep at the whole of national Jewry. When a delegation went to the school superintendent with a suitable memorandum, explaining and pointing out that it is impossible for Jewish children to attend mixed schools if one wants to respect their religious tradition and their attachment to the Jewish milieu — the superintendent revealed the “secret”: although the beginning is being made in Lublin, this is not a local measure. Next “in the fire” — he said — comes Łódź, and afterwards it will be done in all the other cities. If — he went on — the Jews hold that their children must have schools in which the Sabbath is kept as a day of rest, let them build such schools for themselves with their own money.
But for us Jewish parents, for whom the Jewish-national education of our children is the alpha and omega of our life — such an answer is a heavy blow over our heads.
We, the Jewish parents and our children, hold that a great enough injustice is being done to us in any case, in that the “szabasówki” are gradually being housed in inferior school premises, as [is done] for Jewish children; we, the Jewish parents, hold that so long as our rights to a school system with Yiddish [Jewish] as the language of instruction are not realised, then in the special state elementary schools with Polish as the language of instruction for Jewish children the following subjects must occupy an honourable place, and precisely in the mother tongue: Jewish history, Jewish culture and literature, etc., etc. All these are postulates which even the children demand and cry out for — yet they do not figure in the curriculum.
We also hold — and very firmly — that in these schools only Jewish teachers must teach.
In short, our conclusion is: many injustices we pass over in complete silence, [but here] an energetic and widely ramified campaign must be undertaken at once in order to annul this decree, so crushing for us.
All Jewish political, cultural and social organisations in general must speak up — while it is not yet too late. The greatest duty lies on the Jewish kehillot; out of these bodies must be created the organ that will keep its hand on the pulse of the sick, aching organism of the patient called the school for the Jewish child.
L. P.
A Double Livelihood (A Little Feuilleton)

It seems that England has now given a little more thought to the great armament programme that Hitler is carrying out in Germany. As long as it was a matter of armed storm detachments, of an enlarged army and of an armed German people in general, England did not worry much — it let France do the worrying about that. England has nothing to fear from an armed German people as long as Germany has no warships and therefore cannot reach the English shores.
The English statesmen became uneasy, however, when they were told that Hitler is also creating a great air fleet for Germany, that he is building a large number of war aeroplanes, and that very soon Germany will have thousands of aeroplanes which will be the last word in military technology and military science.
Ex-Kaiser Wilhelm once said that Germany's future lies on the water, and he began building a great war fleet, which became a danger to England. Then came a world war and destroyed Kaiser Wilhelm's war fleet, and with it also Germany's future on the water. Now Hitler has come and says that Germany's future lies in the air, and he has begun building a great fleet of war aeroplanes — and with an aeroplane one can reach England just as easily as France — and England has therefore had to think very seriously about Hitler's armament activity.
But what will England do? England, together with France, could have stopped Hitler's armament, but Hitler buys a large part of his aeroplanes in England. That is, he gives a livelihood to the English manufacturers — so how should the English government not let him do it?
The English government therefore has a better remedy. It will enlarge England's own air fleet, so that it need not be very much afraid of Hitler's aeroplanes. Stanley Baldwin, the de facto leader of the English government, made that known long ago. The English manufacturers will therefore have a double livelihood. They will make aeroplanes for Hitler, so that he can attack England, and they will make aeroplanes for England, so that it can repel the attack of Hitler's aeroplanes.
And what does the old peace-chaser Ramsay MacDonald do? He recites Psalms for peace and reads tkhines [supplicatory prayers].
Tsvien.
Sages, Be Careful with Your Words!

Reading the pious and submissive “memorandum” concerning the “ONR riots” in Poland, addressed on behalf of R' Mendel Alter of Pabianice and the delegation in the name of the Agudat HaRabbanim [Union of Rabbis] in Poland, and the reply of Cardinal Kakowski, which was to be expected as an answer — or, more correctly, as a consequence — of such a “prośba” [petition], a shudder passes through every seriously thinking Jew: what our Agudat HaRabbanim is capable of! Granted, in religious matters — that goes without saying, that is after all “their patent”. Again, when one needs something from the “authorities” (that is, when they need something), it is known that they are close to the government — so one might have thought that at least the little bit of Jewish politics they would leave to those who are called to it — but it does not occur to them at all: they are politicians too! And therefore the question arises: in whose name did they address the memorandum, and who authorised them to do so? And what kind of answer — begging their pardon — did they reckon on receiving? Do our rabbis really not understand that such a reply from Cardinal Kakowski worsens the present bitter situation by 100 per cent? — And what do they intend to answer to the reply they received, to which they have not merely failed to react (silence is tantamount to admission) — and which is also, in a refined way, an approval of the riots that took place!
If only... they would understand this — that this disgrace could have been avoided if one did not meddle in matters not one's own; have they also forgotten, in this, the “Sages, be careful with your words”?
A. Yud.
Oneg Shabbat

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Korach
The Portion
a) "And Korah took" (15[sic]:1)
"This portion is finely expounded in Midrash Tanhuma." Rashi.
Usually Rashi picks out one homily from the many homilies expounded on a verse in the Midrashim and quotes the homily that pleases him as an interpretation. Here, however, Rashi refers the reader to Midrash Tanhuma, which is not Rashi's way.
But since on the verse "And Korah took" many homilies are expounded about the intention of the great quarreller, each homily believing that he had a different intention — therefore Rashi does not choose a single homily, because Rashi holds that as regards Korah all the homilies are true: all the evil thoughts one could possibly ascribe to him are true... Siftei Da'at.
b) "Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy" (ibid., 3)
1.
Usually all quarrellers and strongmen like to say to their rabbis: it is a miracle that you came upon such gentle and quiet people as we are... had you come upon strongmen, they would have taught you manners. So too Korah's congregation argued to Moses: it is a miracle that all the congregation are holy and are no quarrellers... So spoke Korah and his congregation... Sha'ar Bat Rabim.
2.
Korah's congregation said these words by antiphrasis (lashon sagi nehor): "Rav lakhem" — enough of your leadership, "for all the congregation are holy" — don't you see? The whole congregation is nothing but saints, so to speak[?]... Therefore "rav lakhem" — enough of you, if you have produced such a congregation... Emek ha-Shedim.
3.
"For all the congregation are holy."
The Bach was rabbi in Kraków. Once he was in a small town near Kraków and, as was the custom, paid a visit to the local rabbi. He saw that this rabbi was a scholar of scant learning who at times could not decide a halakhic question. On taking leave the Bach said to him:
— We should swap places: you should become rabbi of Kraków and I should become rabbi in this town...
The rabbi was astonished: how can that be?
— It is so: with us in Kraków there is a congregation in which all are holy, there are many scholars and halakhic authorities there; so be it, you could well be rabbi there too, although you cannot decide a question... But here, in this town, there is nobody who could decide a question...
c) "I have not taken one ass from them" (ibid., 15)
The Chacham Tzvi, when he was rabbi in Amsterdam, did not want to benefit from any individual at all. He accepted no festival money, no mishloach manot and the like, apart from his salary from the community, so that he would not have to flatter any of the city's wealthy men. This had grave consequences for him. Because of it he made all the wealthy men his enemies, for the wealthy — as his son-in-law R' Aryeh Leib gave to understand — want to have their rabbi in hand so as to be able to bite him now and then... The False Messiah (5)

[Serialized historical tale — David Alroy, the false messiah; installment 5.]
Sh. Berg.

But more than anyone it was the poor and simple folk who went. They went en masse. Only the rich Jews and the old rabbis stood against David al-Ra'i [David Alroy]. They were not sure whether he really was the Messiah, and they feared that if he should later lose, the rulers would take revenge on all the Jews.

His strongest opponent was Rabbi Shmuel Gaon. From the very first minute he was against him, and every new victory of David al-Ra'i brought him new fear and grief. He quarrelled with the young rabbis and said that with their belief in the false messiah, as he called David al-Ra'i, they were helping to bring troubles upon the Jews.

Menuha sided with David al-Ra'i. She was even ready to run away from home and go over to the Messiah, her Messiah. In her father's quarrels with the young rabbis she stood up for David al-Ra'i, and her father flew into a rage and shouted:

"What do you want? Why do you stand up for him? Do you side with him too? It won't help any of you; he is a false messiah, he will perish, and because of him the rulers will slaughter all the Jews."

Menuha did not dare to contradict[?] her father; she kept silent and quietly let her tears flow. It hurt her doubly that her father was so merciless and uttered his prophecies about all the Jews and about David al-Ra'i, about the Messiah, about her David, about her Messiah...

Meanwhile David al-Ra'i made all the preparations to go further. He sent word to the Caliph of Baghdad and to the rulers of all lands that he wanted no war with anyone; he only wanted to go and take the ancient land. He asked the rulers to let his army pass through their lands. He wanted nothing for free. For everything he would pay in gold.

Even before he set out on the road he decided to summon the leaders of the Jews in all lands to a great assembly in his capital city, Shushan. The leaders did not need to be afraid of coming to him, because for many years thousands of Jews from all lands used to come to Shushan, to the tomb of Daniel the Prophet.

The tomb of the prophet Daniel in Shushan was not in the ground but in the air: in the middle of the river, above the bridge, the tomb hung on iron chains. Once the tomb had been in the ground, but the townspeople waged long wars over the tomb, until it was hung up over the middle of the river.

Shushan lies on both sides of the river. On one side lived the men in power, and they were very poor; on the other side was the Jewish quarter, and the Jews were very rich. The tomb of the prophet Daniel was in the Jewish quarter; so the poor men in power said that the Jews were rich by the merit of the prophet. They wanted to have the prophet's tomb on their side, so that his blessing would rest on them too. The rich Jews would not allow the holy tomb to be dug up, and great fights and wars used to break out between the Jews and the men in power.

So the Sultan, after much bloodshed, made the compromise that the tomb should hang in the middle of the river, between both sides of the city, and both sides would have the blessing. And year after year thousands of Jews from many lands used to come to the holy tomb.

And as soon as the Messiah's call reached the Jews, they began to stream from all corners of the world to Shushan, Shushan the capital, where King Ahasuerus once reigned; they were now going to an assembly with the Messiah.

The great assembly.

On Hamishah Asar be-Av (the fifteenth day of Av), the first festive day after the day of mourning of Tisha be-Av, David al-Ra'i appointed the great assembly. The Nasi [Prince] of Babylon also came, and even Rabbi Shmuel Gaon came too. He could not withstand[?] the demand of his community and the yeshiva people, who demanded of him that he go. He also thought that he might perhaps influence David al-Ra'i to give up his dream. Menuha went along.

Menuha was still a maiden. Apart from the fact[?] that her father would not have wanted to marry her off, she herself would not have wanted to marry anyone either, because she was waiting for David al-Ra'i. In all the years she had been waiting for him, her ardent love for him had grown more ardent and stronger still. She loved him not merely as a man, even the best and handsomest of men, but as the Messiah, her Messiah. She was sure that he had not forgotten her, that he still loved her, that he was waiting for her. And as she went[?], every moment was to her like a year.

The camp of thousands of delegates stood assembled facing the palace of the fortress. David al-Ra'i came out and stood on the steps. Behind him stood the sixty heroes, one hand on the great curved sword of Damascus, and in the other hand a long sharp spear.

The camp stood silent and gazed. David al-Ra'i began to speak; his voice was so beautiful and mighty, like a wondrous song.

"Jerusalem is dear and holy; to all peoples and nations Jerusalem is dear," he began. "Over Jerusalem the Christians and men in power have waged many wars and shed much blood. Only we, Jerusalem's true children, do nothing for our holy city. There, where our kings reigned, where our prophets prophesied and our Tannaim taught, where our Temple stood — strangers rule, and we are in exile, slaves of wicked rulers; we endure the greatest torments and do not stir from our place. Once Jews were heroes; we had the Hasmoneans, the Zealots, the heroes of Betar; today we are slaves. In love with our slavery, we have fallen so low and been so degraded that we have already lost the will to be a people as before. Does the chosen people no longer want its chosen land?"

Then a storm rose in the camp; many wept for joy and all cried out:

"You are our Messiah! Lead us! Lead us!"

The Nasi of Babylon with Rabbi Shmuel Gaon went up onto the steps, and the Nasi spoke up:

"You are right[?], Messiah; would that the redemption might come. But how can we make an uprising against the Caliph — he will surely exterminate all the Jews?"

[Sosnowiec — Zionism and Keren Hayesod; clashes with the Revisionists.]
Last Sunday an academy [formal gathering] took place here in connection with the proclamation of the "Keren Hayesod" campaign.
The "Keren Hayesod" campaign was actually supposed to have been started several weeks earlier, but the matter was delayed because of "certain reasons", and the instructor of "Keren Hayesod", who stayed several weeks in Sosnowiec on account of the campaign, could not fulfil his mission.
After many incidents and stormy meetings, an agreement was reached in the fighting camp, and they set about carrying out the campaign for "Keren Hayesod". In honour of this, Dr. Hindes, Eng. Levitas and others came here to take part in the academy.
As the devil would have it, on the eve of the academy the death sentence was passed on Stavsky; this naturally provoked dejection and strong bitterness among the Revisionists, who wanted to vent their anger and wrath by disrupting the academy.
The approach to the hall looked like a war position. Foot and mounted police had to intervene several times and put an end to the mutual [?] brawls between the Revisionist youth and the opposing groups. Nor was the honour of Dr. Hindes and of other "Keren Hayesod" representatives spared; thus, for example, when the instructor Bram went to the railway station to wait for Dr. Hindes, he was badly beaten; Dr. Hindes too was received with abuse.
After the academy Dr. Hindes, Levitas and others were escorted by police to the flat of the advocate Kowalski. Hardly had the police guard gone away when the guests were pelted with rotten eggs and potatoes. The other side too, the opponents of the Revisionists, did not stand with folded arms, as a result of which a brawl broke out in the street.
The wild scenes gave satisfaction to the non-Jewish passers-by, who were delighted at "how the little Jews are fighting" [in Polish] over the fact that Palestine, the Jewish home, is to "be built"...
The police intervened again, and about 15 men, the "active ones", were taken off to the commissariat, where some were released at once and some only the next morning.

From Sporting Life.

[Sport — Zagłębie.]
The Zagłębie Football Association has resigned.
On Wednesday a stormy meeting of the board of the Zagłębie Football Association took place over the cancellation of the autumn round of the championships. After a very heated discussion the entire board (except "Unia" Sosnowiec), headed by its chairman Mr. Walski, tendered its resignation, and in connection with this an extraordinary meeting has been convened in Częstochowa for the 30th of this month.
Cycle race of "Maccabi" Sosnowiec.
On Sunday "Maccabi" organised a cycle race on the route Sosnowiec–Tychy–Sosnowiec via Murcki: 50 km for seniors and 30 km for juniors. In the 50 km race first place was taken by M. Kac, who covered the distance in 1:31:40; 2) H. Lejtner 1:32:40. In the junior race N. Kotek came first, in a time of 58 minutes. At the finish a crowd of about a thousand people awaited the cyclists.
Championships of the Zagłębie "A" class.
On Sunday a further 4 championship matches of the "A" class were played, because the "Solvay"–"Sarmacja" match was postponed. The individual results were as follows;
Unia — Zagłębianka 3:5 (2:2).
"Zagłębie" — "Hakoach" 2:7 (1:1)
To the supporters who came from "Hakoach" in Dąbrowa, "Hakoach" gave much pleasure. The team, which for the first time in the whole season appeared at full strength, played well, but the referee, Mr. Brila, evidently did not like that "Hakoach" was already leading 2:1, so he came up with a pretext and sent off Hampel. Afterwards, with his subjective decisions, he drove the "Hakoach" men out of all patience. The players, unable to play under such conditions, yet unwilling to leave the field, because in that case they were threatened with a money fine, stood on the field, and the "Zagłębie" forwards carried the ball into and out of the goal. Instead of a football match the public got a football comedy and laughed heartily. The referee, seeing that the crowd was laughing at him, left the field. The blame for such things lies with the Referees' Association, which delegates to such matches people who are absolutely unversed in the rules of football.
"CKS" — "Brygica" 1:4 (1:1).
The local "derby" of the two Częstochowa clubs ended with a deserved victory for CKS. The goals were scored for CKS by Bogucki 3 and Puszybilek 1, for Brynica by Kropiński. The match was refereed by Mr. Grajcer of Częstochowa — rather weakly.
Championship of the "B" class.
In the "B" class championships the results were as follows.
Shimshon — Szwis[?] 1:5.
Kinneret — Maccabi 0:1.
Dąbrowa — Gwiazda 2:2
Czarni — Płomień 0:2.
———
The board of the Będzin "Hakoach", despite all difficulties, has set about very energetically building a stadium of its own. It is organising a whole series of sporting events of all its sections. "First in the fire" is the football section, which is organising a tournament of four teams on the 23rd and 24th of this month. The winner of the tournament receives a cup.
The tennis section, too, intends to hold a few tennis matches in the coming days, but first the club's internal championships will take place, for which all members of the tennis section are preparing very intensively.
The cycling section is not asleep either, and will very soon organise a cycle race for the Jewish championship of Będzin. Besides the title the winner will also receive a cup.
"Hakoach" hopes that Jewish sports lovers will help the very fine initiative of "Hakoach" to build the one and only Jewish stadium in Zagłębie.

The behind-the-scenes connections of the „home-grown“ Hitlerites

Sensational trial before the Katowice district court.
This week the already well-known sensational trial again took place before the Katowice district court; it gives a clear picture of the dirty deeds going on behind the scenes of the so-called „People's Socialists“ [Polish National Socialists].
The subject of the trial is the suit of the lawyer Kozielski of Sosnowiec, organiser of the „People's Socialists“ in Zagłębie and in Upper Silesia.
As is known, the lawyer Kozielski, who founded the „Jedna Karta“[?], conducted a lawsuit against his comrades, whom he accused of slander. His comrades had publicly reproached him that he, Kozielski that is, had secretly negotiated with a certain Baumann[?], who had promised him 20.000 zł. for a certain „concession“.
Several trials have already taken place in this matter: on 31 January [Yiddish „styczeń“] a verdict was handed down by which one of the gang was sentenced to three months' arrest and to pay 300 zł.
Both sides lodged an appeal against the verdict, and this week the sensational trial began again before the Katowice court of appeal. At this sensational trial, which will last several days, the party's dirt will be washed in public. Because Kozielski's lawyer reproached the judge with being one-sided — the trial was broken off.
Why she poisoned her husband and children

A sensational trial has taken place in the Katowice district court. The heroine of the trial is a certain Gertruda Hibner[?], who is accused of wanting to poison her husband, a railway official.
The matter is as follows:
Mrs. Hibner gave her husband bread smeared with phosphorus, intending to kill him with it[?]. She wanted to get rid of her husband because of her affair with her lodger.
The accused had married her husband in 1923. At first their life together was happy, but when in 1926 she met her permanent lodger Lazar, the harmony of their family life was spoiled; husband and wife began to quarrel, and scenes of jealousy became a daily occurrence.
Finally, when Lazar moved into the Hibners' flat as a lodger, Mrs. Hibner decided to poison her husband so as to be able to carry on her love affair with the lodger undisturbed.
Hibner, however, realised in time that the bread his wife had given him was smeared with poison, and he threw it away right after the first bites. He ran at once to a doctor and was saved from certain death.
The husband handed the whole affair over to the court. Meanwhile the investigation has led to a discovery: Mrs. Hibner is namely accused of poisoning her two small children, who died two years ago in a mysterious manner.
For this reason an exhumation of the dead little bodies was carried out; they were sent to the dissecting room (prosectorium) for expert examination.
73-year-old Jew of Sosnowiec does not hold with the ban of Rabbenu Gershom

In Sosnowiec old Reuvele is well known, already 73 years old but [—?], because he „[—?]“ the ban (cherem) of Rabbenu Gershom [against polygamy], which — in his opinion — is a heavy „burden“[?] on [—?] humanity.
He has [—?] put the idea into practice. Disregarding the fact that he has a wife in Sosnowiec, he went off to Będzin and married a second one.
And when good friends and acquaintances ask him: How can it be? A Jew over seventy, a Torah reader (baal kore)?!
— Mine — he says — is a „dried-up [old thing]“[?], so I went to Będzin and got married.
Warsaw appeal court frees 2 young Jews from a heavy sentence

The young men had been accused of committing an act of violence (rape) against a young Christian woman from Upper Silesia.
The defence lawyers lodged an appeal with the Warsaw appeal court, which this week annulled the above-mentioned sentence.
The young men were released from the Będzin prison immediately after the verdict.

Instead of medicine — poison.
Last Monday a terrible incident took place in Mysłowice.
A local Christian woman who suffered from a stomach ailment bought a remedy for stomach pains from a hawker. When the woman used the remedy she was seized by tremendous pains and died that very same day[?].
As it turned out, the woman had been poisoned. The police are searching[?] for the hawker who sells "remedies" for stomach pains.

Appeals against turnover tax may be filed until 30 June

We draw the attention of all craftsmen and small industrialists who have received an assessment for 1934 of lump-sum (ryczałt) turnover tax that appeals regarding the amount of the tax may be filed until the 30th of this month.
Appeals may be filed only by the following: 1) those whose turnover has actually decreased in 1934 relative to the average turnover on which the lump-sum tax was calculated; 2) when the assessed lump sum is much higher than the assessed turnover for 1933 (for those who until now had no lump sum); or 3) if the present lump sum is much higher than the previous lump sum (for the years 1932/33).
There are a great many such cases, because the average turnover tax for the years 1928, 1929 and 1930 was much smaller than the average turnover of the years 1930, 1931, and therefore the matter must not be neglected and an appeal should be filed at once.
The appeals will be considered by the tax offices, and if it is recognised that the tax should be reduced, the tax office will annul[?] the reduced sum at the end of December this year.
Hitlerite organisations dissolved in the Będzin, Zawiercie and Olkusz districts

In the previous number of our paper we reported that in Upper Silesia the Hitlerite organisations had been dissolved.
The authorities of the Będzin, Zawiercie and Olkusz districts (powiats) too, recognising that the activity of the organisation is against the law and threatens security and public order, have dissolved the National Socialist party and stopped its activity.
At the same time the starosta issued an order under which it is forbidden to belong to the organisation and to wear its uniforms.
As we are informed, the Hitlerite party has also been dissolved in Kraków.
Through a second murder the killer of the baker Jakubowicz in Łódź was caught

In Wysokie[?] the policeman Kowalski was murdered last Thursday.
The police, who organised a manhunt (obława) around the Wysokie forest, succeeded in catching the murderer. As it turns out, the same man had also murdered the baker Jakubowicz in Łódź several months ago.

The colony is located in the „Three Roses“ boarding house. The fee from today until 15 August is 73 zł 50 gr.; from 16 August to 15 September — 66 zł 50 gr.
