Let the Honour of the People Be Raised (On the Lawless Doings in the Houses of Study)

[Synagogues and houses of study — opinion.] Last week's chronicle tells us of two facts from which we might well draw a moral: 1) On the Sabbath, Revisionists entered the Będzin synagogue, seized the bimah and, before the Torah reading, announced to the congregation that Stavsky had been sentenced to death in Jerusalem.
2) In Modrzejów, beggars came at night and woke the local gabbai from his sleep because they wanted to stay the night in the beit midrash. The gabbai granted their request, but did not agree that one of them should take his wife in with him. For this the beggar kicked the gabbai in the stomach so hard that the unfortunate man paid for it with his life.
Two separate events, two separate conceptions — and yet one must dwell on them, because neither brings us any honour; both debase the prestige of religious Jewry. Unfortunately and regrettably, as soon as anything happens, as soon as something occurs, the first place is the synagogue, the first place is the beit midrash: if one has to come to blows, if one has to quarrel and curse, the first and best place is a holy place.
On the Arlosoroff–Stavsky affair as such we do not wish to say a single word at the present moment; but we cannot understand why, at the very first moment, this news had to be announced precisely to the synagogue worshippers, who perhaps have no idea what it is all about. From anyone else, perhaps — but from the youth, who claim to know what they want, we could surely have demanded a little reverence. If they had indeed decided to speak in the synagogue, they should nonetheless have asked permission, and not burst in like storm troopers and seize the bimah, which was bound to arouse bitterness among the congregation. Besides, this gives the impression of complete lawlessness, for which there is absolutely no place in a holy place.
For one must not forget that every holy place is, and must be, a neutral place, where there may be no room for partisanship, and where one must avoid bringing in the mundane and polemical discussions, which root envy, hatred and strife to the highest degree. And must [printed: 'radf'] a holy place, however one looks at it, be a place where people test their strength?
And the second fact, the Modrzejów incident that cost a human life. Is this tragic story to teach us nothing? Must one really not dwell on this tragic event?
More than once we are outraged, we get agitated, we protest, we adopt various resolutions with which we want to prove that we are human beings equal to other people; yet we forget one thing: that if we first of all want to be valued, why then do we not value ourselves? Why do we debase ourselves by our own integrity, by our own reason, by our own understanding? Why does this not bother us? Why does it not hurt us, when it is all the more painful because we ourselves root the degradation, and we ourselves place ourselves a step lower, thereby stamping it that we need not stand at the same height as all other people?
Why should we not understand that if we first of all want to be valued and respected, we must, after all, first show respect for ourselves, reverence for our own interests and problems?
Never mind that we are already used to the sad state of our houses of study and think it must be so — that not only can it not be otherwise, but it even seems to us that it may soon not be otherwise; that filth has become holiness among us goes without saying.
But it happens more than once that our houses of study are visited by strangers and by non-Jews, and disgust seizes us when we observe what impression our 'holiness' leaves on non-Jews. At such a moment we are covered with shame, and this is not forgotten so quickly; it is deeply engraved in the people's memory.
Let us just cast a glance over the houses of study of 'rich' Jewish Zagłębie — are we not then drenched in shame? Instead of houses of study we have scaffolding grown into place ['rustovanyes', Polish rusztowania], and when it comes to taking down what will surely be taken down in our great-grandchildren's times, the great-grandchildren will think the synagogue is being dismantled... And where there is no scaffolding there is filth and darkness, which by the way has been turned into holiness. And who does not remember by what miracles Będzin got a decent synagogue? Did not the hypocrites raise a hue and cry back then that the style there must not be touched because it is sanctified? Did they not then shout that Jewish blood flows from the little birds being painted there, although it did not cost them their money? Do we not owe this memorial to Dr. Weinzieher and Szymon Fürstenberg, who paid no heed to anything but carried out the necessary work while they represented the Jewish kehilla?
We simply say that there is no understanding and no will for cleanliness and order. Yet one must remember that a holy place is not a public domain where everyone may be allowed to carry on all kinds of orgies, with no authority to stand up and remind them that there is a limit here — this is permitted, and this is not under any circumstances.
For example, it must under no circumstances whatsoever be allowed that the street be dragged into the houses of study and the synagogues. For discussions and lectures there are other places.
Now about begging in the houses of study. In former times, as we know, there was a hekdesh [poorhouse] for beggars; today the hekdesh is in the beit midrash, where a beggar lodges for the night in this very holy place, and it turns out that it is their property. Because of this, in fact, the misfortune in Modrzejów happened; otherwise the 'guests' would not have had so much chutzpah as to drag the gabbai out of bed.
This is what our houses of study look like, this is the level to which they have been brought — and this is tolerated, and it is looked upon with indifference.
It is surely high time that, if we do not want or are unable to adorn and smarten up our houses of study, we should at least protect them from filth, dissoluteness and partisanship. We must not allow them to be defiled through us, for after all it is a holy place.
It goes without saying that if we had kehilla representatives who were not changed like fresh laundry every week, the affairs of the houses of study would have had to be within their competence; and since this is not so, and our rabbinate is not interested in it either, because 'it yields nothing' — that is precisely why our synagogues and houses of study find themselves in such a dismal condition.
No people in the world will [allow] temples to be turned into lawlessness, and we too must not allow it; even though our houses of study are already in such a low state, they must be rescued. Every possibility must be used so that their prestige be raised.
R. Let.
On Guard Against a New Law

[Economy — taxes and the small traders.] In just a few days, on the 1st of July [lipiec], the regulation comes into force under which merchants holding licences of the 3rd and 4th category will have to keep official books for the tax, so that every tax office [urząd skarbowy] can check them.
It goes without saying that a merchant of this category, who looks out for a customer as if with a candle, and when none shows up — for a little interest-free loan [gmiles-khesed]; such a merchant will certainly be unable to undertake keeping official books.
These merchants will therefore be forced to engage bookkeepers, who are to be the masters over the books. It is self-evident that people of this category will not be able to get used to this, if only because they will not have the means to pay a bookkeeper, however cheap he may be; moreover one must bear in mind that one must [?] have responsible people, otherwise the owner is responsible for everything.
Many merchants would be content to earn what they will need to pay for the bookkeeper. How then can the matter be carried out?
Usually our merchants know that they will not be able to manage this, and so they concern themselves little with the question. But that is not healthy [?]; one must not treat it with indifference, for afterwards one can have trouble from it, because a law — once it comes into force and one does not comply with it — one certainly gets no joy from it. Moreover great weight is given to what the association of which he is a member tells him, and since the association tells him nothing, it means nothing has come of it.
We do not know — it is possible that the law will not yet be carried out; still, one must treat the question seriously and indeed see to it that it is not carried out, otherwise it is very, very bad, because people of this category cannot engage bookkeepers of their own, whom they are not even able to hire with the necessary material.
Our professional-economic institutions must take up the question seriously. The central bodies must intervene at the ministry already now. If this has not happened so far, then the situation is catastrophic.
By waiting until the last minute one can lose a great deal, and that must not happen. Everything possible must be applied already now, so that the new law does not come into force; otherwise the middle strata of the Jewish masses face ruin.
Selekt.
Optimistic.

[Opinion — fascism and democracy.] By the reckoning, the world is done for. All the facts and figures show that we are heading for fascism, darkness, destruction. But let us not be slaves of mathematics.
After religion, the figure, the reckoning, has become mankind's idol, and statistics too can be idolatry.
I remember a doctor's reckoning:
A doctor sat with a fountain pen ["wieczne" pen] in his hand and proved that the man must die. He is already very old, his heart has long been no heart at all, it could stop any minute. Of his lungs not an olive's bulk of lung is left, the liver is affected, the kidneys show pus, the arteries are hardened [?], the stomach has entirely stopped taking in food, and now he has double pneumonia with a high [?] fever — well? Can this man get well?
By the reckoning the man indeed could not get well, but he did get well. And he outlived his doctor by a good [?] number of years.
For besides heart, lung and stomach, there is still something in a person called life, and this little bit of "life" cannot be calculated with a fountain pen.
And just as there is an unconscious element in a person's existence, so there is also something hidden from the eye in the life of nations and civilisation.
Things do not always go according to the reckoning and the actual situation.
Karl Marx was a sociological watchmaker; he assembled wheels upon wheels that are supposed to show how time goes and when it strikes midnight.
And indeed his clock goes, and the hour comes, and it strikes midnight — but the rooster does not crow according to his clock. The rooster does not know at all that it is his time to crow.
———
It is easy to see the darkness of the night, but it is not so easy to notice the first ray of dawn.
And it seems to me that I see the day beginning to break. I do not mean my day, the day we all hope for — things have not got that far yet [?].
But compared with the year 1933, every return to liberalism is a ray of light. A hope that the sun will rise one day.
For it is by no means proven that fascism is a step towards communism. Fascism may well be a thing in itself, to which mankind might have had to adapt for a good several generations.
And even on a step one can stand for quite long enough.
And it seems to me that fascism has already reached its peak and that it must now turn back.
Above all, the one who has laid fascism into the ground is — Hitler.
Mussolini gave fascism a bit of prestige: he strangled and stabbed in the turbulent days after the war, when human victims were reckoned as sheer nothing and civil war as an everyday matter.
And he took over Italy when she lay in a faint, and the nature [?] of one who has fainted is that he comes round and recovers.
The trains in Italy would not have stood still for ever; whoever had become master would soon have set them running. But Mussolini set himself up like a Napoleon before the world:
"You see? Before me the trains in Italy did not run, and I — I made them run!"
And because of the rivalry between France and England, and on top of that because Germany kept digging against France, Italy had to play a role, to become more important in the field of world politics, even if some good-for-nothing had held power in Rome.
So Mussolini said: "You see how great I am? See how I made Italy great!"
And since he has a strong censorship with an iron machine, one hears only how people shout hurrah in Italy, not how the people groan.
Hitler, however, did everything the other way round: he came out with [—] ["leydastva", unclear word], in broad daylight, when all the windows were open, and he himself kept drumming for ten years — come to me, soon I open my circus!
And he picked a quarrel with a people that knows how to cry out. And although the world does not always hear its cry, this time it did want to hear its cry about Hitler — for its own reasons.
And he promised happiness, great happiness abroad and at home, on which he has already had to go bankrupt. Hitler has shown how fascism works — it doesn't!
He swore off the Corridor and lost Vienna, and still stands at the door of Paris, hat in hand.
The German worker grows poorer, thinner, hungrier, more downcast, and great Germany is collapsing from day [to day].
Hitler's example will not allow any fascism in England and France — however much noise the little fascists make — and it will also keep America from it.
And so times are improving little by little everywhere; the course is going back to democracy, to humaneness.
D. T.
Under the Wings of the Swastika

By Sz. Rotenberg.
It is a fact that the Nazi leaders no longer regard Hitlerism as a purely German matter. They have presumed to be the missionaries of a new „religion“ and „philosophy“, and to exchange the cross — which reminds them too much of the accursed Semites — for a purely Aryan swastika.
Their propaganda minister Goebbels, the apostle of Hitlerism, roams the world wishing to bless the nations with the discovery that Jews and Marxists are the source of all the evil and wickedness that befalls mankind, and that the moment they are rooted out and removed from public life, redemption will come. But one must be politically naive to believe the liquorice-sweet speeches of the Nazi prophets, who are so strongly reminiscent of the prophets of Baal, who preached that for people to be happy a certain part of them must be brought as sacrifices to the idol „Moloch“. The Hitlerites, too, preach a return to the god of thunder and lightning „Wotan“, to whom the ancient Germans offered human sacrifices. They openly come out against the Christian religion as a Semitic contrivance that is unfit for so „lofty“ and „pure“ an Aryan race as the German one.
In the programme for their „world redemption“ the Nazis have not forgotten woman either, whom they want to turn exclusively into an apparatus for producing as many children as possible, in order to enlarge the bloodthirsty and war-provoking Hitlerite gangs. For a long time woman has waged a hard struggle for her rights; she has succeeded in breaking through the „male wall“, in penetrating, at least partly, into public life and in exercising a certain influence there. It is surely the wish of every cultured and logically thinking person to see woman as an equal member of society and to benefit from her help in the struggle for social liberation. And now come the Nazi „philosophers“ and declare woman an inferior creature, fit for nothing more than the three „K“s: Kirche, Küche, Kinder [church, kitchen, children].
Therefore the news that Prof. Zieliński, in the name of the Polish „Intellectual League“, invited Goebbels to give a lecture sounded like bitter mockery, like the prank of a jester sticking out a long tongue at the duped public. And it had to be Prof. Zieliński who did it — a man imbued with democratic ideals and with the refined, universal-spiritual aesthetics of ancient Greece. And it had to happen precisely in the name of the intellectual elite of Poland, which ought to be the „pillar of fire“ for everything that is progressive, better and more beautiful in life. How did the members of the League not blush with shame when they adopted the resolution to invite to a lecture the Grand Inquisitor, the fire-master of the spiritual auto-da-fé in Hitler's Germany? Their guest will surely figure in the pages of cultural history as the wildest vandal of all times; his name will surely remain for eternal generations the synonym of barbaric cruelty and human degeneration. That historic night, when the tongues of fire consumed the creations of the finest human minds, will surely remain forever like a witches' night, like a loathsome dance of demons on the ruins of European culture and civilisation.
In reality it is not merely a matter of Jews and Marxists, who serve only as a convenient point of attack; in fact the Hitlerites want to wage a bloody swastika crusade against the whole of European civilisation. Exactly like the pre-war Junker militarism, the Nazis now want to enslave Europe and turn it into a Prussian colony under the wings of the swastika.
A further sad sign of the times is the appeal of the „Human Rights League“ against the „Nara“ [ONR] movement in Poland. At first glance it might have seemed that this was truly a humanitarian deed. Although no practical deeds could have been expected from such an appeal, it could nevertheless have exerted a certain moral pressure. But on becoming better acquainted with the text one falls into still greater despair, because it becomes clear that the League for „Human Rights“ does not regard the Jew as a human being with equal rights, but as a second-rank creature. It is enough to quote from the appeal for the matter to become entirely clear. We read there:
„The first victims have already fallen in the struggle with Jews on the streets of Warsaw, and a Jew has been killed. But that is a second-rank matter; tomorrow a Christian may fall“.
One need not be a specialist in reading between the lines here; it is written plainly and clearly that the fact that a Jew was murdered is a second-rank matter. The only fear is that tomorrow a Christian may be killed. It is simply a comedy. A league for human rights, which ought first and foremost to defend the h-u-m-a-n being without distinction of nation and race, is itself under the influence of racism.
Will mankind let itself be infected with the poisonous Hitler microbe? Will it be permitted that the swastika spread its wings over the world and plunge it into the wildest chaos and idolatrous barbarism?
Let us hope that this will not happen, that in the end the „night of the long knives“ will vanish like an evil nightmare and a new morning will rise, cleansed of cannibalistic Hitlerism — a morning that will bring with it freedom and equality for all who work and build, without distinction of race and skin colour.
"Stop Thief!"

[Będzin — municipal politics; polemic on the city-council elections.] An old, tried-and-tested Jesuit device for covering up the truth and masking what is base and ugly: one helps oneself by shouting and crying "Stop thief!"

This is the impression that every honest and logically thinking person must come away with on reading the articles by Messrs. Lewin and Diamant in the "Zagl. Tsayt." Nos. 23 and 24.

But if Mr. Lewin's article is at least written with tact, with logic, with composure — although its arguments do not stand up to any criticism — Mr. Diamant's article, on the other hand, is full of lies, hypocrisy, flattery and demagogy. Mr. Diamant has simply "lost his temper", fallen into sheer hysteria and galloped so far that he went as far as profaning the sacred memory of the great tragic Jewish victim, Dr. Arlosoroff of blessed memory.

It is really not worth answering all those "salvurtn" [?] and "arguments", because public opinion has long since pronounced its verdict, and the healthy instinct of the masses has already duly branded the irresponsible "benkl-bapers" [?]: "Go out and see what the people say!" That, for us, is the best proof that all these hair-splittings and the whole scholasticism are nothing more than throwing sand in people's eyes. Only so as not to leave anyone with the slightest doubt about this unheard-of public scandal, I permit myself to repeat the following:

Immediately after the publication of the electoral ordinance for the last city-council elections, we Zionists were the first to take stock of the seriousness of the moment, and we were the first to adopt as a categorical and sacred principle that for the city-council elections we must put up as candidates the finest and best that Jewish Będzin possesses; and although there were suitable candidates in our own ranks, politically mature and nationally conscious people, we were nevertheless the first to step down, ceding the place to more qualified and more suitable candidates. We did this in the awareness that this is a time of distress, that we are living through a terribly critical and tragic period, that we are surrounded by a world of enemies who would drown all the Jews together in a spoonful of water, and that we must therefore strain all our common forces to obtain a representation that would be capable — through its influence, its authority, its spiritual and intellectual baggage and experience, and its proud national consciousness — of defending our honour and our bleeding interests and of fighting the waves of the roaring sea of antisemitism, of hatred and envy against us. And precisely for this purpose we turned to the meritorious Będzin communal worker and influential personality Dr. Weinzieher, asking him to accept the mandate to the city council, because he alone is called to it and he alone possesses the moral right to represent the Jewish population of Będzin. Dr. Weinzieher, taking into consideration all the arguments enumerated, agreed to accept the mandate.

I do not wish to repeat once again the whole course of events and the scandalous conduct, known everywhere, of "Torah ve-Avodah" and the Revisionist party, who by their conduct "passed an exam" in political immaturity and in having no understanding whatever of the tragic problems of the Jews at the present time and of the great troubles we are now living through. Instead I want to recall once more and establish that they abused the trust we placed in them: at the very same time as we sent out more than 4 thousand ballot papers on which their candidates also figured, they stuck a knife in our back, distributed their own ballots and campaigned only for their own "candidates", and brought about such an absurdity that, instead of so famous a personality as Dr. Weinzieher, people without a name and without the slightest influence were elected, people whom nobody will reckon with at all. Thereby, on the one hand, they desecrated the honour of the esteemed Dr. Weinzieher, who answered the call of his brethren like a loyal soldier in a hard and responsible hour, and on the other hand they caused the Jewish population of Będzin to lose so proud and influential a defender as Dr. Weinzieher.

Finally I would also like to thank Mr. Diamant for reminding me of the story of the bear and the two friends, and I will remind him in turn of the story of the fly that perched on the head of an ox. While the ox was ploughing the earth, the fly proudly called out and sang:

"My pakhali!" [Russian: "We ploughed!"]...

I consider the polemic closed.

Y. Wygodzki.
I'm Riding on the Line...

[Humorous feuilleton — summer holidays; monologue, part one.] (Monologue of a Jew who went to rent a "letnie mieszkanie" [summer lodging])
Rendered by Ben Amotz.
— Why do I look so bad? Why do I walk bent double? — you ask. — I rode on the line, that's what I did.
— Which line? Speak clearly — are you, God forbid, crazy or out of your mind?
— I am, thank God, in my right mind and know what I'm saying, and I want the same from you: that you too should understand me — that my bad looks and my brokenness have to do with the line.
— With the dacha line...
The "pleasure" began right after Havdalah. As you know, I take great delight in a glass of something warm [?]; as a Jew says, "From Psalms and tea your head doesn't ache" — and all the more so when Saturday night comes: then the tea matter takes an important place with me, and as always, coming home from the "shtibl", I made Havdalah, cracked out the "Hamavdil", and cast a longing look at the stove.
— What are you looking at the stove for? — asks my missus, a little under her nose.
— What kind of question is that? — Tea? Let there be tea! — I answer like a man of authority.
— Tea, shmee... Why are you getting so angry? Maybe we should start [?] roasting [?] ourselves by the stove for your tea? Not enough heat in the house? Sweat is pouring off the children, and he still wants tea?
— What did I do? — you ask. — I kept quiet and dropped the matter, because I am already "trained" and know that as soon as the first summer day appears, my wife becomes "weakly": it's hard for her to breathe, to walk; even the gossip about the neighbours she cuts short...
Never mind — I thought to myself — if you find it "duszno" [stuffy], shall I load such a heavy burden on you as well? In a pinch, "pompkowa" [?] [pump] water is fine too.
———
What time it was — I don't remember. It happened like this: I had barely dozed off when suddenly I heard a groaning, a sighing mixed with sobbing... At first I thought my neighbour was treating me to these "lyrical" tones — a "członek [?] of the club" [club member], who holds "midnight lament" every night at the "club". But when the groaning, sighing and sobbing grew stronger, I jumped out of my sleep and — what? [?] What has happened here? Around my bed my wife is hopping with her head bowed, and my little company are flailing about like stamping machines.
— Hush! What's the matter with you? My children, why are you trembling so? Woe to my enemies — maybe run for a doctor?
— No, Daddy — we don't need a doctor; Mummy dragged us out of our beds so that you should...
— So that I should what? — I say, faster now.
— You should go and rent a "letni mieszkanie" in the Beskids...
— Hm... a "letnie mieszkanie". How do you say it? A "letnie mieszkanie w Beskidach"...
Enough — I'm a lost man; my fate is the same as Abraham Stavsky's. I said: agreed — I'm going on the line.
———
Arriving at the station at 4 o'clock, I had the impression I had fallen into a concentration camp: tumult, din, the squealing of children who hadn't slept enough; men already "escorting" their "living inventory" run about sweating, panting, with the tickets and luggage slips, and when the "ticket man" calls out "strona Katowice" [Katowice direction] — we all pour, with bag and baggage [?], onto the platform to welcome the Warsaw [?] "Pi-Per" [?], the "bezpośredni pociąg" [through train] Warsaw–Zwardoń...
On the platform the crowd stands loaded; the hands of the living creatures are full, the only difference being this: among the fair sex, the "weakly" little wives hold in their hands the travelling bags stuffed with.. powder, rouge and other articles of "pierwszej potrzeby" [?] [first necessity], while the men — the horses in human form — several travelling bags and various other "zabawki" [toys]...
The noise here is like Thursday evening at the Będzin market halls. Several men without "peronówki" [platform tickets] clamber up the wire "fence" on the other side of the station and from there send "latest news" over to their departing wives and families.
— Feigl Leah! — shouts a bass voice — "Mother is better."
— Praised be the Almighty — answers the squeaky little voice of a little woman — write, do you hear, Aaron Yaakov — write, I'll write to you too.
— Jews, women, who here is Kante's daughter? [printed "tater"] — bursts out another Jewess — I have a parcel for her. Don't you know who Kante's daughter is?
— Fresh butter biscuits, well baked, brown "rivkeles" [?] baked — buy!
The "weak" little wives swallow the saliva of an appetite whetted by the butter biscuits, but they keep to their "fast"; they don't touch the biscuits.
— "Nie mam żadnego [?] apetytu" [I have no appetite at all] — says a young wife — "do niczego nie mam apetytu" [I have no appetite for anything]. — Appetite, so to speak [?] — responds another — the whole Sabbath meal I didn't put in my mouth.
Who knows how long the talk about appetite would have gone on had it not been for the sudden tidings:
— The train is here!
— "Proszę wsiadać" [All aboard] — the conductor gets angry, but who is able to squeeze into the train so quickly? What a rush, what a shoving — merciful Father in Heaven! How great are Your mercies upon Your people Israel: from all sides they aim to destroy us, we are "a scorn and a derision", a disgrace and a mockery to the lowest house-painter — and here such self-sacrifice, just to be able to enjoy the great and beautiful world You created...
— Praised be the Lord, blessed be He, that we are already inside, in the carriage, you know — says to me a fine acquaintance who is escorting his "weakly one" as far as Katowice.
— Yes, yes — I agree with him — the first act is played out; now one must prepare fresh strength for Katowice, where one has to buy the "wycieczkowy" [?] [excursion] ticket.
But about that — in the next issue.
Demoralization among Nations. — The Individual Learns from the Collective.

One need not be a great philosopher, sociologist or politician to grasp the organic connection between the collective and the individual, to understand that the present brutalization of certain individuals towards other individuals (for example the Nazis and the "Nara" [the Polish ONR] towards the Jews) stands in a certain connection with the enormous difficulties of finding the way to peace among the nations.
There is simply a material connection here: if mankind had been able to make peace among the nations, Germany too would as a matter of course have been satisfied and calmed down; her national ambitions would not have poured out [?] into such a disgraceful, inhuman anti-Jewish campaign. In the Polish youth, too, extreme chauvinism would not have flared up.
Worse, however, is the psychological connection between the collective and the individual. Right after the war, when mankind realized that the former international relations had caused the terrible bloodbath with its tens of millions of dead and cripples and ruined homes, the democratic leaders of the nations, seeking new forms for the relations between peoples, said to themselves: why should the collective be any different from the individual?
If for the individual there is the commandment "Thou shalt not kill", why should it not be valid for the collective too? If the life of individuals among themselves is codified and regulated by various bodies, why should the same not be possible for the collective? Why should a regulator not be created among the nations, a kind of higher power, that could compel them to discipline, to justice, to lawfulness?
On the basis of this elementary theory — to compare the collective to the individual — the International Tribunal at The Hague was created even before the war, and after the war the League of Nations was founded in Geneva, which sat down to find the peaceful way to judge "between nation and nation", just as from time immemorial one has judged "between man and man".
The outcome of these efforts is well known to us — for the time being we are still at the very beginning [at "aleph"]. The greatest sages of the world, however excellent their pacifist intentions may be, are by no means able to find the means of avoiding brutal physical force in international relations. All acknowledge the terrible misfortune, the enormous ruin that lies in constant arming, the poverty it brings upon states, and the ever-hovering danger of a new war. Nevertheless no one has the power to avert these ruins and dangers and the rule of brutal force.
Now, if life has shown that the collective cannot learn from the individual, is it any wonder that things have been turned upside down and the individual has begun to learn from the collective?
People said to themselves: since the world is founded not on morality and justice, not on lawfulness and discipline, not on mutual understanding and tolerance, not on regulations and codifications, but on the inhuman principle of "might makes right" [kol de-alim gvar] — why should the same principle not be valid for relations between individuals too?
Where is it written that only a geographic, physical border permits one to regard the people on both sides of the cordon as mutual enemies and to persecute one another to destruction — why should the same not apply to the spiritual, national border between group and group, so that one, the stronger, may strangle and oppress, persecute and trample the weaker, and take from the other his property together with his very life?
In essence one could carry this theory right down to the most particular of particulars, to the single human being, and make the rule of the fist valid: the stronger shall hurt the weaker, rob him and take his inheritance, as the German Nietzsche taught with his doctrine of the Superman.
But before one arrives at such cynical barbarism, at plain savage cannibalism, one can for the time being still wrap the impurity in piety, the bestiality in ideals of racism, "Aryanism", neo-nationalism, which people even try to preach among the nations like a new Torah from Sinai.
This, however, is in a certain sense the result of human disarray, of the bankruptcy of the idea of peace among nations.
The collective did not want to learn from the individual — so the individual learned from the collective.
Thus one can see with the naked eye how demoralization among nations gradually leads to demoralization among citizens too, and it may yet be that, in the course of further development, man will throw off the yoke of discipline and be transformed into a plain wild beast.
That will be the zenith of civilization: the wild beast will be the Nietzschean-Nazi Superman!
P. K.
Radio Bulletin.

What do you need to know when taking a radio to a summer residence?
Summer is beginning and the public is already getting ready to go off to the dacha.
Many people take their radio sets along so as to have the opportunity there, too, to enjoy themselves with the radio broadcasts. We therefore find it necessary to give our readers a few instructions on what must be done with the radio when moving it to a summer residence, so as to be in order with regard to the postal authorities.
Normally the radio listener is obliged to notify the post office every time he changes his place of residence; an exception is made only for those who go away to a summer residence, but for no longer than 4 months. In this way the radio listener can go on paying the normal monthly radio fee at the same post office as all year round. One need only notify the post office in writing of the temporary change of address. The radio installation that stays in town, however — for example the aerial and the earthing — must be secured in such a way that no one can use it during the summer months. It is best to lead the earth wire out to the other side of the window and there join it to the aerial and solder it [?]. In this way the radio inspector, should he come to the radio listener's permanent residence, will have the assurance that no one can use the aerial.

Before the Storm

[Poetry.]
Not calm on the lake...
Ploughed through is the water,
mountainous, with white peaks.
It storms, tears itself from the shores,
wants to flood all the roads —
Not calm is the lake...

Not calm is the little forest...
Slender pines, tall oaks,
white birches, grey willows
secretively rock their branches,
cannot keep something silent —
Not calm is the little forest...

Not calm are the little swallows...
Rocking, wavering,
they hover, fly in fright
under the thatch, to their nests,
to escape the wind from the west —
Not calm are the little swallows...

Not calm is the stork, too...
Majestic, stretched out,
he cuts the air like an arrow from bows,
over fields, over forest tops,
flies home to protect his nest —
Not calm is the stork, too...

Not calm is the little shepherd...
Thunders crash, lightnings flame,
he drives the sheep and cattle together
down the mountain, to shelter himself
from the fiery lightnings —
Not calm is the little shepherd..
Ben Zecharyahu.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Chukat)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Chukat
The Portion
—o—
a) "This is the statute of the Torah" (Num. 19:2)
The halakha rules that all of us have the status of those impure through contact with the dead, because nowadays we have no ashes of the red heifer — and who, after all, takes care not to touch a corpse or someone impure through a corpse?
The question arises: other sacrifices, too, we do not offer nowadays, and yet it is said: "Whoever engages in the law of the burnt offering is as though he offered a burnt offering", and so with other sacrifices as well. So why should it not be "Whoever engages in the portion of the red heifer is as though he offered the heifer", and the study purify those impure through the dead?
But precisely for that reason the heifer is indeed a statute that is not according to reason and understanding...
And therefore it is said: "This is the statute of the Torah which the Lord commanded, saying" — even the "saying" (the fact that we read the portion of the heifer twice a year and yet remain impure through the dead) — even that is also a statute...
R' Akiva Kranitzer (Rabbi of Kraków).
—o—
b) "Nor of figs, or of vines, or of pomegranates; neither is there any water to drink" (Num. 20:5)
They complained that there was no water — "And there was no water for the congregation"; so why did they speak of figs, vines and pomegranates? Did they then at least have bread? Was nothing more than vines and pomegranates lacking to them?
But, complaining about water, which the manna did not replace, they said: if we at least had figs, vines and pomegranates, the fruit would quench our thirst; but apart from the manna we have nothing, so we shall surely die of thirst.
Tekhelet Mordekhai.
—o—
c) "We will not pass through the field" (ibid. 17)
The verse acquires its proper sense according to the explanation of R' Yosef ibn Kaspi in his book "Mishnat Kesef":
The desert tribes, as is well known, dug wells in the fields for the sheep and for the shepherds (as the Pentateuch relates of Abraham and Isaac. These pits were small and could not hold much water; they were the most important treasure of an oasis.
This is what the Jews declared (lit. "commanded") to Edom: we will not go through the fields, we will not even approach in order to drink water (which for the desert wanderer is a matter of life), we will go by the King's Highway, where there are no wells; we will not damage your fields and will not drink up your water. —
—o—
d) "And Moses did as the Lord commanded; and they went up into Mount Hor in the sight of all the congregation" (ibid. 27)
"And Moses did as the Lord commanded" — is this "as the Lord commanded"? God had commanded that only Moses with Eliezer [sic; in the verse: Elazar] should go up the mountain (see verse 25), and Moses went "in the sight of all the congregation", about which God had told him nothing.
But the Gemara (Ketubot 17) says that six hundred thousand are required to escort a dead person, and God commanded that only Moses be present at Aaron's death, because "Moses is equal to six hundred thousand"... But Moses did not think much of himself — "Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth" — so he went up "in the sight of all the congregation", before the eyes of all six hundred thousand Jews..
Pri Ya'akov.
• • •
R' Eizel had disputes with the Netziv. When the Netziv published his commentary on the "She'iltot of Rav Ahai Gaon", R' Eizel made a sharp quip:
In Ketubot 17 the Gemara says that the funeral of the dead must be attended by six hundred thousand. On this the Gemara says: "This applies to one who read Scripture and studied Mishnah; but for one who taught others there is no limit"; Rashi remarks: "And consequently we learn that for one who neither read nor studied, [Torah study] is not interrupted. I found this in the She'iltot of Rav Ahai"... I can say with Rashi: "I found this in the She'iltot of Rav Ahai" — that there exists a person who neither read nor studied: in the Netziv's commentary on the She'iltot I see that he is one who neither read nor studied...
Zikaron la-Aharonim.
—o—
e) "And the Canaanite, the king of Arad, who dwelt in the Negev, heard" (Num. 21:1)
"This is Amalek... and he changed his language to speak in the language of Canaan." Rashi.
Amalek likes to change his language so that people should not recognise him, and so does "Amalek's partner" ("the kosher one among butchers — Amalek's partner" [sic; the Talmudic saying reads "the best among butchers"], and in the Gemara "butcher" means a shochet [ritual slaughterer], because in Talmudic times the butchers were also slaughterers).
The slaughterers like to change their language; sometimes they put on a pious act...
Nahalat Devash in the name of the Maharam.
• • •
The Sanzer Rebbe once said of the young men, the slaughterers, that before they get their posts they put on a show of God-fearing men, and afterwards, once they are already slaughterers, they show their face.
"Anyone may slaughter in the first instance, and their slaughtering is valid after the fact" (Hullin, folio 2)
In the first instance all are good slaughterers — in the first instance, before they take up their craft. After the fact, however, when they have been slaughterers for a long time, there remains only "and their slaughtering is valid" — their slaughtering is kosher only after the fact...
• • •
In a little town near Posen there was a slaughterer who was a complete ignoramus. Dr. Feilchenfeld, the Rabbi of Posen, found out about it. So he sent for the slaughterer, examined him on the laws of slaughtering and saw that in matters of slaughtering he did not know his hands from his feet. He said to him:
— Young man, you must take up another trade.
— What trade can I take up? — asks the young man — I am no craftsman. I excel only in my piety; so what can I take up?
— Become a baker... A baker, too, must be pious. He must separate the challah portion... he must pour water over his fingernails before beginning to knead the dough... And since you are indeed a Hasid and a God-fearing man, I will issue you a permit allowing you to be a baker throughout all the dispersions of Israel...
—o—
f) "We have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord and against thee" (ibid. 7)
Because "we have spoken against the Lord and against thee", because we spoke slander — "we have sinned": it led us to other sins as well... Such is the way of slander..
Binah la-Ittim.

The “Polonia” on the Rabbis’ Audience

[Press — from the Polish press; Jews, the Church and antisemitism.] (From the Polish press).
In one of the latest issues of the Chadecja [Christian Democrat] organ “Polonia” an article appeared about the sadly famous audience of the rabbis with Cardinal Kakowski.
Discussing in detail the course of the audience (according to the version of “K.A.P.” [the Catholic Press Agency], of course), the paper gives the Jews a portion of moral lecturing:
“The Cardinal’s standpoint must have made a strong impression on Polish as well as on Jewish society. We doubt whether the Jews will be satisfied. Of Cardinal Kakowski’s answer — and the rabbis’ memorial will certainly not calm the antisemitic wave [?] in Poland; on the contrary, it may intensify [?] it even more. Certain arguments the Jews should not use in their struggle with their opponents. Among them, for example, is the argument that the Germans are Poland’s eternal enemy. Only a born Pole can argue that way, but not a Jew, because it is, after all, a generally known fact that the Jews have always distinguished themselves not only by sympathy for Germany, but in the critical moments of our history they were the intermediaries, and one-sidedly in favour of the Germans, waiting for our downfall (!!) The Germans became ‘barbarians’ for them only when Hitler and his followers came to power and began persecuting the Jews.
The Polish Jews may, in the struggle against Hitlerism, invoke universal humanitarian principles, as they like to do, but they must not make use of national Polish criteria.”
In a further part of the article the author reproaches the rabbis for having committed a great want of tact in invoking Catholic principles, because — he repeats — where the Catholic Church is trampled and persecuted, the mighty Jewish press has never taken up its cause; on the contrary, it has always taken the side of the enemies of Catholicism.
“The Catholic — we read further — has always suppressed physical force in social life (that is the theory; the ‘Nara’ [ONR] people prove it in practice. Sh.) That does not mean, however, that he need not defend himself against harmful influences from non-Catholic spheres. The German Jews had so much self-criticism that they publicly admitted (!!) that before Hitler’s coming their co-religionists had pursued a policy that harmed German cultural and moral life, which was bound to provoke a reaction of German nationalism. Our Jews have a very small measure of self-criticism. With us the greater part of the Jewish intelligentsia are leaders of anti-Christian culture, spreading it among Christian society. In this way the Jews themselves create antisemitic moods and thereby strengthen them in Poland — as if the economic factors were not enough for that.”
Needless to say: heavenly prospects for the near future.
Sh. Shakh.
And It Shall Come to Pass in the End of Days

[Satirical feuilleton — emigration to Palestine.] Or: “Do Palestyny!” [Polish: “To Palestine!”]
My grandfather, may you live long, was a wise man. A Jew, he used to say, must live with trust in God; a Jew must have faith; a Jew without trust and without faith is no Jew at all.
And I tell you he was right, my grandfather, may he rest in peace: where, I always cried, will I take such a fortune [“majątek”] for a middle-class certificate?
What does God do? He gives an order: “Little Jews, do Palestyny!” Well, as long as the saint Lutosławski of blessed memory (“zikhroyne le-kezekukhn” — may his memory be for a cheesecake) shouted “do Palestyny”, people listened to him the way a cat listens! Now, you see, it is something quite different. When every janitor [“stróż”] already shouts “do Palestyny”, those are different words! Still — a “Biardainer” [?] head-trick: our brethren really do his will and — travel “do Palestyny”.
It goes on on every table and bench, everyone is going — “there is not a house where there is not one dead.” There is not a single house where you would not find a Jew with a — passport. If he has no passport, people talk about a passport (when there is no brandy, people talk about brandy). Especially as we now have, after all, “free emigration” to Palestine. One, two, and you have a passport. You have barely settled the income tax [“dochodowe”], the property tax [“majątkowe”] and the “spozniczowe” [?], and if you are an upright citizen [“rzetelny obywatel”], that is, if you have never yet been punished for going crooked [?], if you have never yet had a police report for conversations on the “Mandushever” [?] street —
then you already have all the rights in your pocket; you travel to your native town for an extract from the permanent population register [“wyciąg z księgi stałej ludności”], have your portrait taken, put all the paraphernalia together and lay down 500 złotys with a [?] — and you get without any difficulty a passport “do Palestyny”.
Now you take the merchant — the passport, I mean — and travel to Warsaw, and after you stand some three days in the queue at the Romanian consul, three days at the Czech consul, three days at the Italian consul, three days at the Austrian consul, and spend nights for a month at the — Palestine Office, you get on the train and travel home with a finished, kosher, visa-stamped passport.
What did my grandfather say? — Trust! Little Jews travel, little Jews push in the queue, little Jews pay the złotys — heaven and earth and Palestine. Gradually, gradually it will get sparser here. Every month a few hundred little Jews fewer, in half a year several thousand little Jews fewer, in a year several hundred thousand little Jews fewer, etc., etc., so long and so wide, until there will remain no more than: Dr. Thon, Dr. Gottlieb, Dr. Rosenblatt — and done [?]! Then I, Yudl Hartsveytog [“Yudl Heartache”], will raise my bowed head and breathe more freely.
I imagine what a man of standing Yudl Hartsveytog will be here! They will caress me, they will pamper me [“pieścić”] like an only son: when there are elections to the Sejm, the Endeks together with the PPS people will put me up on their candidate lists. With the Endeks I will eat from the same bowls — “the Jews had [light]…”

The False Messiah (6)

[Serialized historical tale — David Alroy, the false messiah; installment 6.]
Sh. Berg.

David Alroy calmed him and said that he did not want an uprising, he wanted peace; only the Land of Israel did he want to redeem for the Jews, and to bring the Jews to the Land of Israel.
Late at night, after the assembly, two young women went down to the river — Menucha and her friend, the Nasi's daughter; soon David Alroy came too, for here he was to meet Menucha.
Menucha stood as if in a dream, and as in a dream David Alroy approached.
— Menucha!
— David, my Messiah!
These were the only words they spoke, and afterwards they stood a good while in silence.
— I am waiting for you, Menucha, fairest of all daughters, my bride — David Alroy began — but I shall have to wait longer still; in redeemed Jerusalem, on the holy mount, cleansed of the foreign defilement, we shall set up our wedding canopy. Then your stern father will agree too.
— And I shall love you — said David Alroy — as Rabbi Akiva loved his Rachel, my bride; I shall redeem my people, you and myself...
They parted warmly, celebrating [?], after so many years, their love, firm in their hope that the redemption would soon come and that their wedding canopy would stand on the holy mount in Jerusalem.
Rabbi Shmuel Gaon, however, remained obstinate in his disbelief in David Alroy. At the very time that David Alroy was speaking with so many hopes to Menucha, the old Gaon sat with the representatives of Baghdad and poured cold water on their fiery faith — he is a false messiah! — the old Gaon argued — he will bring nothing but misfortune.
The next evening the great assembly came to an end; with a blessing David Alroy took leave of the representatives and closed with the call
— Next year in Jerusalem!
And the camp answered with a loud cry — Next year in Jerusalem!

The Ban (Herem)

The representatives returned to their towns and lands and brought with them the tidings of redemption; the joy among the people grew greater and stronger. David Alroy waited for an answer from the Caliph and the other rulers; the number of his soldiers grew from day to day.
After Sukkot the Caliph sent for the Nasi. The Nasi put on his rich garments, mounted [?] the white horse and, with his horsemen ahead, rode off to the Caliph.
In the Caliph's palace the Nasi of the Jews stood dejected and broken. The Caliph was angry: the Jews are rebelling, he shouted, they have already taken all of Persia, now they want Baghdad. They want to conquer the whole world, they forget that they are lowly servants. He would exterminate all the Jews if the rebellion did not stop. He would give them a heavy punishment in any case, even if they stopped rebelling. But he would let them live if they brought him David Alroy's head.
The Nasi begged the Caliph to calm himself. This was no rebellion. He, David Alroy, only wanted to take the Holy Land from the Christians. But the Caliph remained adamant that it was a rebellion against the Mohammedans as well. The Sultan of Persia had been driven out and was asking him for help.
Sad, with bowed head, the Nasi returned home. The assembled Jews saw his contorted face, and a heavy groan broke from their hearts. He was bringing no good news.
Rabbi Shmuel Gaon, hearing this, jumped up and said triumphantly:
— Now you see that I am right. The vengeance is already beginning; the Caliph, who was always good to the Jews, is in a rage, he will destroy us all and pour out all his wrath on the heads of the Jews. I always said that he is a false messiah, that he is leading the people astray. He has led even the Nasi astray! An end must be put to all this falsehood — he shouted — a ban! Put the deceiver under a ban!
The Nasi turned pale when he heard the word herem; it was a terrible, a dangerous means, sharp as a sword, and whoever is under the ban has no more hope. The Nasi still believed that his kinsman David Alroy was the Messiah and would conquer the Land of Israel. He also hoped that he could prevail upon the Caliph not to hinder the Messiah, and so he asked the Gaon to wait with the ban; but the Gaon would not hear another word. The rabbis and the notables sided with the Gaon, and right then and there Rabbi Shmuel Gaon placed David Alroy under the ban.
He wrote out the ban on parchment and signed it. The rabbis signed too, and they compelled the Nasi to confirm the ban with his signature and to affix the seal. With pain in his heart the Nasi did it; he knew that by this he was signing David Alroy's death sentence.
The Gaon took two courageous beadles of the rabbinical court and sent them to David Alroy, instructing them thus:
— Deliver to him, the false messiah, the deceiver, the ban, and let there be an end to him!
A wild terror fell upon the Jews of Baghdad when they heard that the Gaon, the rabbis and the Nasi had placed the Messiah under the ban. Now they were afraid to side with him and to believe in him. Before, they had been ready to go through fire and water for him; but the ban cast such dread upon them that they were afraid even to think of him.
All of Baghdad turned away from the Messiah — all but Menucha. She alone remained faithful to him. She ran to the Nasi, tore the hair from her head and lamented:
— What have you done! — she cried — he is the Messiah! He would have brought the redemption! You have killed him! With your own hands you have shed his blood! You have killed the Messiah! Why did you let my father talk you into it! I cannot stand up against my father! But you, you the Nasi, why are you afraid of my father? You do believe in the Messiah, so why did you put him under the ban? Why have you destroyed him?
The Nasi excused himself, saying he could not help it; the Gaon is the highest representative of the Torah, and he, the Nasi, had to obey.
— The Messiah lives! He will live, you cannot kill him — Menucha cried wildly — the ban is nothing. The Messiah is stronger than the ban — he will triumph!
Menucha saw that the Nasi could not help her; he could not lift the ban without the Gaon, her father... Her father was determined to destroy David Alroy. The rabbis and the rich side with her father, and the poor tremble before the ban as before fire. They fear they will die if they side with the Messiah, who is now under the ban. What was she to do? How could he be saved from certain death?
And she resolved that she must save him. She went in to the Nasi's daughter, her faithful friend, wept before her and begged her to help her save David Alroy.
— I must not tell a single word to anyone! — Menucha wept — they would only stop me. Help me save him! If you do not want to save the Messiah, save my bridegroom!... Come with me, let us run to him and warn him of the danger.

Zagłębie Under the Heavy Impression of the Assassination of Interior Minister Pieracki

[Zagłębie — Mourning for Interior Minister Pieracki; Będzin; Sosnowiec; Dąbrowa.]
The Będzin magistrate resolves to name a street after Pieracki.
The news of the shameful assassination attempt on the person of Interior Minister Pieracki, and the further news that the minister had died, made a very heavy impression in Zagłębie.
People gathered in the streets, commenting in various ways, but with enormous indignation, on the news of the shameful murder.
Mourning flags were hung out on the state buildings and on private houses.
Throughout the streets of Zagłębie notices of the Ministry of the Interior were posted about the reward fixed at one hundred thousand zł. for whoever delivers the murderer up to the authorities.
Representatives of social organizations in Zagłębie submitted condolences into the hands of Starosta A. Baksa.
In the name of the Jewish Merchants' and Industrialists' Association in Sosnowiec, Messrs. Safer and [—]kabak expressed condolences.
In Będzin
On Monday at midday, under the chairmanship of the (city) President Mr. Rzeczkowski [?], a mourning session was held, at which the memory of the murdered minister was honoured by 1 minute of silence.
It was then decided to send a delegation to Ząbkowice to lay a wreath on the coffin of the tragically fallen minister.
The delegation consisted of President Rzeczkowski and the aldermen G. Rechnik and Salski.
At the session it was resolved to name a street after Pieracki.
———
On the initiative of the kehilla board a solemn memorial service was held in the town synagogue.
In special leaflets the kehilla board called on the whole Jewish population to take part in the solemn divine service.
The synagogue was packed full. Various strata of the Jewish population came. On the bimah the members of the rabbinate, R' Yehoshuele, R' Dan and R' Hanoch Dor [?], recited the appropriate chapters of Psalms. Each recited a separate chapter.
After the singing of El Male Rachamim by Mr. Piotrkowski, Rabbi R' Hanoch Dor [?] spoke on matters of the day, about the great loss of Interior Minister Pieracki, over whom, together with the Polish people, Polish Jewry also mourns. Rabbi Friedberg prayed that the Blessed Name, Who avenges innocent blood, may help that he who murdered the noble, honest, energetic minister should receive the punishment he deserves.
A short but matter-of-fact speech was given by Dr. Weinzieher (in Polish). Already for the second time, he says, we are mourning the loss of great men of the Polish Republic. The first victim was the first President of the State, who was murdered by those who could not bear that the President had been elected also with Jewish votes — by those who do not recognize us as citizens with equal rights of the Polish Republic.
From the same camp [?] ("lavozeria"), says the speaker, fell the present victim, the one who openly declared from the Sejm tribune that there is no difference of race or nation, but all citizens must enjoy equal rights.
The director of Fürstenberg's gymnasium gives a survey of the merits which the tragically fallen minister had earned for the good of his people and fatherland, and of his liberal attitude to all citizens of the Polish Republic. With the call "Honour to his memory" the memorial service is concluded.
On Tuesday, the day of the funeral, all shops were closed from 12 to 1 at the call of the magistrate.
In Sosnowiec
The Chamber of Commerce sent a telegram of condolence to the Kielce voivode.
———
On Sunday afternoon a mourning academy took place. After the playing of the anthem and Chopin's funeral march, speeches were given by: Starosta Baksa, Deputy Gaszewski [?], the Dąbrowa President Kaczkowski and Director Mazur. A telegram of sympathy was also sent into the hands of Premier Kozłowski.
———
A solemn memorial service took place on Tuesday morning in the local town synagogue. The Jewish population, called by the kehilla board, took part en masse, so that by the appointed hour the synagogue was packed, and, wishing to avoid a catastrophe, the stewards of "Brit HaChayal" let no more people in.
The memorial service, to the credit of the local kehilla, was properly organized. The members of the board and of the council came as one man in gala dress.
Also present were the rabbis Frommer, Hager, Glickman, Halberstam, a delegate of the local starostwo, and a delegation of "Maccabi" with its splendid banner at its head.
After the cantor Mr. Leichter with the choir sang "Shiviti Hashem", Councillor Mr. Józef Safer gave a speech (in Polish), in which he showed how great the loss is for the Polish people and also for us Jews — the tragic victim, Minister Pieracki.
Wrapped in a tallit, Rabbi Hager takes his place before the Holy Ark, from where he gives an inspiring speech. In this week's portion, says Rabbi Hager, we find the verse "And Aaron died there on the top of the mount." Minister Pieracki too, he cries out, the great man, the liberator of the people, has fallen as a sacrifice on the altar of Poland's honour and glory.
We Jews too feel the deep pain of the Polish people, for we are not merely a trading people, but always ready, at the call of Poland's statesmen, to defend with blood, with heavy sacrifices, every span of earth which the enemies wish to tear away from our fatherland.
At the end of his speech Rabbi Hager calls on the Jewish population to accept the proclaimed month of mourning and to refrain from the usual entertainments.
The cantor with the choir then sang very beautifully "Adam lahevel dama", El Male Rachamim and Av HaRachamim.
With the singing of the Polish and the Jewish anthems the solemn memorial service is concluded.
———
To pay their last respects, representatives of Jewish organizations travelled to Ząbkowice. The "Brit HaChayal" of the local command was represented in larger numbers, with their banner at its head.
In Dąbrowa
Last Saturday evening a session of the town council was held, at which President Kaczkowski spoke about the great loss. The speech was heard by those present standing. To honour his memory the session was interrupted for 5 minutes and a telegram of sympathy was sent to the Council of Ministers.
A Bandit Attack on 2 Young Men from Będzin in Upper Silesia

[Upper Silesia — Crime; Będzin.]
On Tuesday night 2 young Jewish men, sons of the furniture merchant and carpenter K. Preger, were driving back on a cart from Szarlej.
When they were already several kilometres from Szarlej they were attacked by 2 bandits; one of them managed to jump up onto the cart, where he demanded money, and in doing so he struck the 17-year-old Wolf Preger on the head with a blunt object and wounded him.
The bandit, seeing that he had found no money, wanted to rob the horse and cart. The struggle over this lasted a certain time, until they came upon police. Then the bandit ran away.

The new Industrial Law comes into force on 15 sierpień [August] 1934. After that date no one will be able to open a craft workshop unless he has first obtained a craftsman's card.
The Centre demands that all craftsmen who have no craftsman's cards should be registered.

On the basis of Article 94 of the Industrial Tax Law the tax offices are entitled temporarily to limit the collection of the lump-sum (ryczałt) tax for the year 1934 if it is established that turnover for 1934 has fallen considerably. All interested parties must report at once to the office of the Craftsmen's Association, where they will receive the necessary information.

Committed a Theft in Łódź and Fled to Katowice.

[Łódź / Katowice — crime.] On 16 February this year the notary [rejent] Rzechowski [?] in Łódź noticed, when he entered his office in the morning, that a theft had been committed at his premises, and he at once established that 5,300 zł had been taken out of his armoured safe. Rzechowski reported the theft to the police, who established that the caretaker [woźny] had disappeared together with his wife. This gave rise to the suspicion that the caretaker had committed the theft.
On the 18th of February the police in Katowice detained a man in the company of a woman, and the police recognised [?] the two of them as the wanted persons from the photographs in the wanted notices. They were detained at once, although they had documents in other people's names. The Katowice police communicated about this arrest with the Łódź police, and the investigation established that the detainees were indeed the runaway caretaker and his wife, and both were transferred to Łódź.
The arrested caretaker confessed to the theft and also confessed that he had forged his documents.
These days husband and wife sat in the dock. The accused confessed to the theft in court and defended himself by saying that he had suffered want: he earned 70 zł a month at the office, but he also had a little business selling cigarettes in a kiosk.
His wife also confessed, explaining that she had helped with the theft because her husband had talked her into it.
The court passed a sentence according to which the accused caretaker was sentenced to two years' imprisonment and his wife to one year's imprisonment.

On the Thirtieth Yahrzeit of Theodor Herzl.

[Zionism — Jewish National Fund.] (Communiqué sent in by the JNF [KKL] headquarters for Poland)
The 20th of Tammuz this year marks the thirtieth yahrzeit of our leader Theodor Herzl.
Recent events have fully confirmed the predictions of the creator of the Jewish renaissance movement. As never before in recent years, antisemitism has begun to rage in every corner of the world. Jewry is now threatened not only by final economic ruin, but by plain physical destruction.
Eretz Israel has therefore become the only hope of the people, a rescue and a rebirth.
The land of our liberation is now being built at an extraordinary pace.
We already have there a Yishuv of more than a quarter of a million Jews, who in village and town are creating our own national home.
The urge to immigrate grows incessantly, and despite all the difficulties that the English administration in Eretz Israel creates for our work of construction, our achievements grow from day to day.
Now it is clearer than ever that Herzl's prophecies are being confirmed by the terrible life of exile and by the pioneering deed of the people in its Old-New Land.
This year on the 20th of Tammuz the Jewish masses will express their reverence for the founder of Zionism by embellishing his eternal monument, and will plant thousands of trees in the Herzl Forest on the soil of the Keren Kayemet.
The Keren Kayemet headquarters in Poland is already making all the necessary preparations for this year's great 20th-of-Tammuz campaign.
Specially issued stickers (nalepki) will be distributed at various prices [?], which will surely be bought up by the entire Jewish population.
Everywhere memorial services, mourning academies, etc., will take place.
The 20th of Tammuz is the day of „afforesting the Land“, the day of intensified work for the upbuilding of the country.

He attacked his tenant's children with a knife

The residents of the Old Market (Stary Rynek) in Będzin witnessed on Wednesday evening a terrible scene, which took place in Merin's house on Bóżniczna Street.
In this house the tenant Meir Żabner [?] has been living for many years; he is in a dispute with his landlord — not a money dispute, but over toilets, which the landlord wants to put up precisely next to Mr Żabner's flat, which consists of no more than one room.
The finale of the dispute took place the day before yesterday, when the landlord, Mr Merin, came into the courtyard accompanied by his brother Shlomo; they were reacting to the fact that Żabner's son had, without their permission, opened a small gate (door) from the courtyard they had closed off. Because of this a sharp exchange of words broke out between them, which led to Żabner's 2 sons being attacked and wounded with a knife several times on their bodies.
At the terrible screams of the wounded a crowd of hundreds of people came running, who condemned the shameful deed.
Żabner's sons, covered in blood, went to the municipal hospital, where they received the necessary help.

The story of a lottery ticket

The number of the ticket is 137215. For 2 years an army sergeant of the „KOP“ [Border Protection Corps], Mr P., has held a quarter of this ticket. The second quarter — the clergyman Mr B.; a half ticket was held by Mr N. of Lwów. In the present lottery the two above-mentioned gentlemen stayed loyal to their previous number, but Mr N., although the collector (lottery agent) sent him the same ticket, sent it back. „This number is not a lucky one — he said — so far I have won nothing on it“. During the summer I will take a break and not play.
Fate played a joke.
This Friday the big prize of 100.000 zł. fell on number 137215. The military man and the clergyman were made happy for their steadfastness. The two quarters discarded by Mr N. were bought by: Mr E., a bookkeeper from Kostopol, and Mrs S. from Gdynia.
And Mr N.? One can imagine... He surely bought at once, although it was already past the time, a half ticket. In the first class he lost his chances, but in return he can win 200.000 in the second class, and possibly later even a million zł.
It is characteristic that the quarters of this ticket have such a wonderful story and are to be found in various parts of Poland. On this lucky ticket four people won who do not know one another, have never seen one another, and it is possible that they will never see one another.

The Danger Facing the Jewish Craftsman in the Future

[Będzin — craftsmen.]
As is known, the amendment (nowela) to the Industrial Law comes into force on 15 August (sierpień) of this year. The law provides (despite the introduction of compulsory organizations) that craftsman's cards will be issued to those who have the so-called acquired rights ("prawa nabyte") only until 15 December (grudzień) 1934, and until 15 August 1934 one can apply for craftsman's cards on the basis of the law in force until now.
In this connection the Central Craftsmen's Union calls upon the Będzin branch to register, according to a set form, all Jewish craft workshops in Będzin and to inform all craftsmen and craftswomen who have no craftsman's card that, if they do not comply with the law, they face the danger that their workshops will be closed.
The Craftsmen's Union in Będzin therefore called a second meeting on Sunday, with the aim of informing those concerned.
At the meeting a resolution was adopted that all craftsmen and craftswomen, and especially the seamstresses — dressmakers — who have no craftsman's card, should come to the association to register; otherwise they face the danger that their workshops will be closed.
How important the question is, is shown [?] clearly by the fact that the largest public organizations take an interest in it and have decided together with the committee of the Central Craftsmen's Union, which strives to legalize the existing craft workshops.
Sad, however, is the fact that those concerned themselves do not care about it at all, as if it were not they who are meant here. The Jewish population is worried by the danger that tens of thousands of Jewish workshops are threatened with closure — and those concerned themselves do not care at all.
The Craftsmen's Union therefore appeals to all craftsmen and craftswomen: do not neglect your vital, bloody interests; legalize your workshops, so that you do not lose your bread.
The New Bankruptcy Law

[Sosnowiec — economy and law.]
At the meeting of the legal committee of the Chamber of Commerce in Sosnowiec.
(Sh.Sh.) This week, in the Sosnowiec Chamber of Commerce, under the chairmanship of councillor Żukowski, a meeting of the Chamber's legal committee took place.
The new law on bankruptcies was discussed, which has already been adopted in first reading by the Codification Commission.
The draft of the new law breaks with the hitherto binding [?] regulations on 3 phases of bankruptcy (curator, temporary syndic, permanent syndic) and introduces a single-phase regulation. According to the draft, a merchant who has stopped paying his debts can be declared bankrupt. At the same time, short-term suspensions of payment because of passing difficulties are not yet grounds for declaring bankruptcy.
The declaration of bankruptcy is decided by the District Court (commercial division); the further proceedings are then conducted by the civil division of the same court, and supervision over them is exercised by one of the district judges of the District Court. A creditors' council with sufficiently wide powers can be appointed; all time limits are set so that the proceedings [?] should last as short a time as possible.
Taking part in the meeting were the president of the District Court, Zborowski; vice-president Kubarski [?]; the chairman of the commercial division of the District Court, Tura; a group of commercial judges, as well as the councillors of the Izba.
After the report of the Izba's legal adviser, Adv. Braun, and after the ensuing discussion, the opinion was established that in general the new draft is clearer and more transparent than the old law; nevertheless several proposals on the question were adopted, and the Chamber of Commerce will [?] submit them through the Union of Chambers of Commerce.
A lively discussion was also provoked by the question whether the fact of stopping payments already suffices to declare bankruptcy, or also a business that still pays its obligations but is in fact below its balance (insolvent). The committee took the position that the deciding factor must be the fact of ceasing to pay.
A whole series of amendments to the individual articles of the draft was also adopted.

What's New in Upper Silesia?

[Upper Silesia — short news items.]
Verdict in the Trial of the „Homegrown“ Hitlerites.
As we have already written, the trial against the leader of the „People's Socialists“ in Katowice, who had been sued by the lawyer Kozielski of Sosnowiec for slander, took place for the second time before the Katowice court of appeal.
At first instance the defendant was sentenced to 3 months' arrest and a 300 zł. fine.
At the trial the dirty laundry of the „People's Socialists“ was washed once again; the summoned witnesses declared that Kozielski had not been out to do „business“ as leader of the party — the proof being that on his organ „Jedna Karpa“ [?] he, poor fellow, lost a lot of money.
The court of appeal upheld the verdict of the first instance.
—o—
Warsaw Police Uncover a Gang of Communists.
The political police in Warsaw have succeeded these days in uncovering a gang („szajka“) of 17 persons, founders of communist cells in Upper Silesia.
—o—
Zionist Org. Seeks to Have the World Conference Held in Katowice.
The Zionist Org. in Katowice is making efforts to have the forthcoming world conference, which is to take place in October of this year, held in Katowice, because in the autumn it will be 50 years since the Hovevei Zion conference that was held in Katowice.
—o—
„Hasło Podwawelskie“ Spreads Its Incitement to Upper Silesia.
Together with the closing of the Hitlerite org. in the territory of the Silesian voivodeship, „Błyskawica“ and similar inflammatory sheets were also stopped.
In connection with this, the antisemitic sheet named „Hasło Pod Wawelska“ [sic] of Kraków has spread its dirty wings to Upper Silesia as well, where the sheet is conducting a strong antisemitic incitement.
It is to be hoped that the security authorities will recognise the harmfulness of the racial agitation and will also stop this sheet, this organ of incitement.
—o—
Telegraphic Protest to the Government over the Wage Reduction for White-Collar Workers.
In connection with the arbitration commission having fixed a wage reduction of 8 per cent for the white-collar (“intellectual”) workers of Upper Silesian industry, the workers sent a telegram to the government, protesting against the decision of the arbitration commission.
—o—
Government Orders Worth Half a Million Zł.
The Ministry of Communications has ordered various screws worth half a million zł. from the screw factory „Fitzner“ in Siemianowice.
—o—
Put to Sleep and Robbed of 1,950 Zł.
A certain Józef Satar, travelling on Saturday in the daytime on the Katowice–Pszczyna train, got acquainted in the carriage with a person who, after a long conversation, treated Satar to a cigarette. After smoking the cigarette Satar fell asleep; the person then took from his pocket a wallet containing 1,950 zł.
—o—
Telephone Call Charges Reduced.
In accordance with the order of the Ministry of Posts and Telegraphs, the charge for telephone calls from Katowice to Ligota [?] („Ligatai“) has been reduced. A 6-minute call now costs only 10 groszy instead of 20.
—o—
Memorial for Dr. Herzl.
The Zionist Org. in Katowice is holding next Tuesday, in honour of the 30th yahrzeit of Dr. Herzl, a memorial service of mourning in the synagogue. All Zionist groupings are taking part in the memorial except „Poale Zion“, who have refused to take part.
—o—
Tragic Death of a Small Child.
In Niedobczyce, Rybnik county, a tragic accident happened in the flat of a railway conductor. On a table in the flat stood a pot of boiling milk. At a certain moment their child, one year old, overturned the pot, and the child, who was badly scalded, died a few hours later.
—o—
A Funeral Procession in Bielsko.
The tragic death of Minister Pieracki found a strong echo among the Jewish population of Bielsko, where several mourning meetings and a mourning procession through the streets of Bielsko-Biała took place. Almost the entire Jewish population took part in the procession.
—o—
General Meeting of the Co-op. Bank.
In the premises of the Jewish community last Monday the annual general meeting of the Co-operative Bank in Królewska Huta (Königshütte) took place. The reports show that despite the severe crisis the bank conducted wide activity in its field.
After the discussion the board was granted discharge (absolutorium). The existing board was then re-elected.
—o—
Protest against the Aliyah Decrees.
Under the chairmanship of Mr. Rater [?] a meeting of the community council took place in Rybnik, which adopted a protest resolution against the aliyah decrees of the English government.
—o—
A Year in Prison for Pouring Hydrochloric Acid over Her Husband.
Before the district court in Królewska Huta last Tuesday the trial took place of a young Christian woman who, during a quarrel with her husband, had doused him with hydrochloric acid.
The heroic „woman of valour“ was sentenced to one year in prison.
