The Problem of Work

The question is truly a very hard one.
On the one hand there is talk of restructuring the Jews, of moving the Jewish masses into productive branches of livelihood, and on the other hand we cannot even preserve[?] the earlier structure, the productive livelihoods that already exist.
Now we are asked to help rescue the 50,000 Jewish artisans' workshops in Poland which are on the verge of going under because they have not yet registered. And the help required is material: to support them, through the kehillas or other institutions, with the sums needed to pay for the examinations.
Well then, if we cannot bring even so small an action to a good end[?] — to preserve these livelihoods — how can we think of expanding the artisan class and creating new productive livelihoods?
And the matter of productivisation itself is also elastic[?] enough.
What comes into consideration here first of all is the passing on of a craft from generation to generation, concretely: the question of apprentices, which is very acute among us. As long as this question is not solved, it is right [to say] that in a few decades there will be no Jewish artisans at all.
But by regulating this matter the craft is preserved among us only within its former framework; the productivisation of the Jewish masses, the restructuring, is still very far off. What is meant by it, after all, is that Jews should penetrate new fields of physical work, that fresh Jewish forces should take up labour, that craft should in a certain sense take the place of trade and of "air-livelihoods". It also means the agrarianisation of the Jewish masses — moving Jews from town to village, from the scales and the measure to the scythe[?] and the sickle. How can all this be achieved if we cannot even preserve the small "something"[?] we have had until now?
The main thing is that this requires a revolution in our psyche and in our tactics; to carry out this revolution, entirely different elements of Jewish society must be taken into account. And it is therefore very possible that it will be quicker to build new ones than to rescue the old ones.
It is not at all pleasant to tell the truth, but many signs show that all the stifled cries about helping and rescuing may remain a voice in the wilderness. For it is truly astonishing: the artisans themselves must surely be interested in rescuing their livelihoods; if they lack awareness and understanding, there are artisans' associations, guilds, chambers of crafts, there is the ORT society, there are other various institutions that strive to help the artisan in his struggle for existence — why then, after 5 years of toil[?] and threats, has the danger of ruin still not been removed? Is[?] the whole obstacle merely the few dozen złoty of examination fees? Why do the artisans manage to pay taxes, buy trade licences and the like? Perhaps they really cannot manage and must turn to a kehilla, or to a people's bank and other public expedients — yet they do not stop trying to save themselves. And precisely here, where the whole future existence is at stake, people remain dependent[?], helpless and apathetic, and let it run almost straight into the abyss!
The same question applies to apprentices. Since time immemorial artisans have made use of apprentices, who served as cheap hands and brought in profits, and there also lay in this a certain instinct for the survival of the species — for preserving the trade in which they themselves had already become rooted. The necessary element of pupils was always found, too. And suddenly — a complete reversal: neither do the artisans want to keep children, nor do pupils want to learn! The reasons for this are well known, but that is exactly where the trouble lies, for we see how weak society is at resisting the smallest obstacles.
Without a revolution in minds the goal will not be reached; if we want to bring about a fermentation[?], the dough must be kneaded differently.
The matter of productivisation is not a problem for the artisans and their institutions; it is a broad and deep political problem for the whole Jewish community. And this problem cannot be solved through financial aid, but only through political struggle on both fronts, the internal and the external.
The whole political and social apparatus must be specially mobilised for this: to arouse enthusiasm for this struggle among the youth and the older leaders. We are, after all, ready to arouse even artificial enthusiasm — especially when the issue here is not remaking life, but adapting to the newly created surrounding conditions, and the enthusiasm can here be genuine, resting on reality. If only we are able to watch and understand reality and master it.
We must certainly rescue the 50,000 workshops; we must also help ORT to go on planting Jewish craft in the coming generation. We must respond with the fullest readiness to every appeal of the artisans' communal leaders.
But we should know that all this is small and almost negligible compared with the great goals that stand before us, and we can reach them in no other way than through a great revolutionary effort.
P. K.
The Grandfather and the Grandchild.

The New Type of Person and Jew.
THE GRANDFATHER (with a worried and sad expression): So, dear child, you are sticking to your latest decision to study aviation!
THE GRANDCHILD (merry and mischievous): It is my firm decision. If you, Grandpa dear, believe that flying is just a whim of mine, or some odd fancy, then you are greatly mistaken.
THE GRANDFATHER: If it really is as you say, then I cease to understand you. I must doubt your clear judgment.
THE GRANDCHILD (with a serious expression on her fresh face): But I, Grandpa, can understand you. You belong to the generations of old. Your wisdom is from yesterday. But I am a child of today, I belong to the new type of person, which is still quite foreign to you, and it is hard for you to penetrate my particular psychology and to feel the spiritual-moral atmosphere in which I live.
THE GRANDFATHER: I believe, my dear child, that you know more or less of my hard struggle, which I waged against the old way of life of my surroundings, and how much effort I put into living according to the spirit of the present. Yet it is impossible for me to understand how such a young child as you can so frivolously want aviation, which is closely bound up with mortal danger. In my eyes it is voluntary suicide. From you, dear Yehudit, I hoped for something else.
THE GRANDCHILD (in a mischievous, laughing tone): I understand, dear Grandpa, you hoped to see me in the "Habtsaliya[?]" movement. You expected Zionist sermons from me, and that a day would come when a rich young man would declare his love to me, and you, Grandpa, would yet live to dance a hopke at my wedding... Have I guessed what you are thinking?
THE GRANDFATHER: No, you do not understand me. I am worried about your life, which is much dearer to me than my own. Tell me, my dear child, have you really thought about the mortal dangers that will lie in wait for you as an aviatrix?...
THE GRANDCHILD: Yes, Grandpa, of course I have thought about all the possibilities of death that are bound up with flying. But precisely these constant dangers to life attract me.
THE GRANDFATHER (with an expression of fright and despair): What do you mean by that, my child? Do you only want to frighten your old grandfather?
THE GRANDCHILD: You, Grandpa dear, must know once and for all that I, your grandchild, have no ulterior[?] motives and no hidden intentions, that I say what I mean and I mean what I say.
THE GRANDFATHER: What did you actually mean[?] by that[?]
THE GRANDCHILD: The new type of person, to whom my generation belongs, can feel the true taste of life only where death threatens. We do not strive to live well and comfortably, but heroically. We are always ready to put our young lives in danger. Calmly and cold-bloodedly we look death in the eye. Obstacles do not frighten us. We do not know feelings of fear at all. Not everyone can become a flier over the seas, a flier around the world. An aviator who deserves this name must be born. The born aviator, the highest type of the new person, must possess delicate, finely developed nerves, yet calm and firm as steel. The born child of the air must possess a body and mind disciplined through and through. His way of thinking, of acting, of measuring and weighing the dangers he meets must be cool and matter-of-fact — scientific. Besides that he must be endowed by nature with an intuitive power that makes him able to face any danger and not lose himself by a hair's breadth...
THE GRANDFATHER: My head is spinning as I listen to your description of the new type of person to whom you belong.
THE GRANDCHILD: Grandpa, I know well how to value your hard-won, human[?] courage, but — no offence — you are not fit to be an aviator. A real aviator must not get dizzy. Not even[?] at the moment when he is lost in a thick fog over stormy seas. Your grandchild, however, is a born aviatrix — be proud of me...
THE GRANDFATHER: How can I be proud of you, dear child, when you think only of yourself and you have not a crumb of feeling for your unfortunate brothers and sisters, who are persecuted, oppressed and even murdered in various countries!...
THE GRANDCHILD: With a sigh, with a groan, one cannot help our unfortunate brothers and sisters. In order to help others, one must first become something oneself. Let me become what I am capable of becoming, then I and my comrades, of the new type of fearless people, will perhaps be able to do something useful for our people too. I expect very much from my brother, your grandson, whom you know very little. He too, Max, belongs to the new type of Jew...
THE GRANDFATHER: Maxie? What can he do and what is he?
THE GRANDCHILD: He is a great master[?] of the fist. Soon he will appear as a boxer and he will astonish the sporting world with his agility, with his enormous strength and his valour in patiently taking blows, and, much more, in giving blows.
THE GRANDFATHER (with a sarcastic smile): Is that so! And I never knew that I had such a fine grandson, who has not "the voice of Jacob" but instead "the hands of Esau" [Genesis 27:22] — what luck has befallen me! No small thing, to live in my old age to see a grandson who is shaping up to be a fist-hero.
THE GRANDCHILD: Oh, Grandpa dear, I see that despite your broad and deep knowledge in various abstract fields, I must after all begin to drill you in the "ABC" of the new type of Jew. You believe that to be a boxer one need only be a coarse fellow with two iron fists. No, it takes an iron moral will; the training of a boxer demands moral purity of him. He must not be a glutton and a drunkard, he must avoid women, he must go to sleep on time and practise the great and difficult art of taking fiery blows from the opponent without so much as grimacing. The boxer needs, like the aviator, plenty of light, fresh air and a regular life. One cannot become an outstanding flier or a successful boxer if one has not disciplined body and mind. A person with a torn soul, or with a wounded spirit, can never become a good flier or a brave boxer.
THE GRANDFATHER: I see that I — I will remain, children[?], an ignoramus regarding your new type of Jew, from whom you expect so much.
THE GRANDCHILD: Grandpa, all your life you fought against the stagnant and the backward. Now you must wage a struggle with yourself, so as not to stagnate and fall behind your grandchildren...
R. G.

Moshe Feinkind: Herzl's Prophecy (On the Thirtieth Anniversary of His Death)

[Zionism — Article in memory of Herzl; 30th anniversary of his death.] In a thoroughly depressed mood, in a mood of despair and hopelessness, in an atmosphere of medieval persecutions of Jews and of disenfranchisement, it falls to us to mark the thirtieth yahrzeit of the unforgettable, great and radiant Jew, Ze'ev Dr. Herzl [Theodor Herzl].
Before our eyes there still stands today his majestic figure as we saw him. There still ring in our ears [printed: "in our eyes"] his inspired, prophetic speeches with which this warm, sincere Jew opened the Congresses, which were a balm for the wounds [?] of this so grievously suffering people.
Herzl suddenly parted from his assimilated surroundings and came back to his forsaken people. With the greatest fervour and enthusiasm, as his great-grandfather, the Spanish marrano Reb Leibl, had once [?] done — who had lived a long time as a marrano and only when fleeing to Turkey threw off his mask and became an ardent, devoted Jew.
And Herzl too [?], before he returned to Judaism and before he arrived at the idea of a "Jews' land" [Judenland], went by various roundabout ways, but he arrived at the right time.
Recognising with his deeply penetrating eyes that the Jewish people, whose child he too was, has no remedy anywhere in the whole world, that the drama of persecutions repeats itself from time to time with short pauses but always in the same forms against this landless [?] people, he appeared then like an apostle with his "Judenstaat" to answer the political "Judennot" [Jewish distress; ?]. And what he prophetically foresaw — that a time would come when the Jews, willingly or unwillingly, would have to leave their homes and concentrate in their own land — all that has indeed come true.
Which one of us could have foreseen that in the very heart of Europe, which the Jews helped to build with so much sweat and blood, those same Jews would have to take the wanderer's staff in hand and, like the fabled "Ahasver" [the Wandering Jew], set out into the world to seek themselves a new home in the twentieth century!...
What we could not foresee, Herzl foresaw in his "Judenstaat" — and it has come.
Before our eyes, unfortunately, this sad picture is being played out, which reminds us of the expulsion from Spain, of Richard the Lionheart's massacres in England, of the murders of a Bohdan Chmielnicki, of a Gonta, etc., etc.
Only with this difference: then Jews could ransom their lives through disguised apostasy, through idol worship; today, with modern technology, civilisation and new inventions, "there is one law for them, to kill and destroy all the Jews" [after Esther 4:11 and 3:13], and not even the spiteful apostates are excluded.
"The Lord visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, upon the third and upon the fourth generation" [Exodus 34:7].
This verse has now been fulfilled in the dark Hitler-land in its full extent.
Herzl did indeed foresee the bankruptcy of filthy assimilation and of renouncing Judaism as a means of rescue, showing them the way through Zionism back to the Judaism from which one stems.
At every step Herzl's far-sightedness and his prophecy now reveal themselves before our eyes. We see it, if one does not want to close one's eyes to what is plain to sense and sight; we see our so long dreamed-of and prayed-for land being built with the blood and sweat of our children, with the Jewish penny earned by such hard toil.
We see how the people fights, strives and settles on its historic soil, paying no heed to all the difficulties and obstacles laid in our way, from whatever side they may come; we leave our old homes without a single groan and without a single pain and move into the national home. We see how the German "Protest Rabbis" and the other assimilators, who had long since erased from their prayer books every trace of Zion and Jerusalem, claiming that Berlin and Paris are supposedly their Jerusalem and Germany and France their Zion, are now seeking Zion and Jerusalem. We also see the rabbis, who so strongly hated and persecuted Zionism — which preached self-emancipation, the revival of the people and the revival of the land — now praying for a Jewish Land of Israel.
Yes, what we have been privileged to see and live through, Herzl — who staked his whole life, his fortune and his whole career and sacrificed himself for the attainment of the national home — was not privileged to live to see. Bitter death tore him away prematurely; he was barely 44 years old when he breathed out his precious Jewish soul with the words: "Greet Palestine for me"...
But he is and remains immortal among us, just as the essence of his life is and will be immortal.
May his memory be a blessing!
The Purpose... (A Humoresque)

[Feuilleton — Humoresque; Jewish youth, the matriculation exam and unemployment.] Already from his early years, almost eight whole years, the young Jewish pupil M. thought and dreamed only of her... He could not at all imagine his future without her... He always envied his older friends who managed to reach their goal before him, reminding himself, though, that he too would soon be their equal. These very thoughts always consoled him against despair and hopelessness...
In the last year, when his hope began to draw near, to come true, he became an entirely different person — rarely did one notice him running across the street with a book under his arm; now is not the time for him to stroll, he is preparing... And indeed, not a single night did he get enough sleep because of "her" — but it is all worth it... He constantly fantasised about how his first encounter with "her" would be, the joy he would bring his parents and the congratulations he would then receive from his friends and acquaintances.
Time runs, and at last the decisive day came for him — he was placed face to face with his destined one. And he succeeded. Thanks to his abilities he managed to win her... He then fainted for joy; one cannot imagine the happiness among his parents and family. On the Sabbath the student was given maftir in the synagogue, and his father also held a big kiddush. At night a celebration was arranged for invited guests, where they amused themselves at laid tables until broad daylight.
Some months passed; the student came back from a dacha [summer cottage] where he had rested after his last hard days... He came to himself and began thinking about what next... Then it turned out that the whole effort had not paid off at all... He wants to go with "her" to Warsaw, to Kraków — he does not succeed; his abilities do not help, because... because his nose and his name betray him.. He thinks of emigrating abroad — that does not work out either, for other reasons... — — — —
And so for several years now the student M. has been loitering as an idler on Małachowski Street [Małachowskiego, Będzin] (together with many more of his colleagues..). And that is the purpose of the able Jewish pupil together with "her".. with his beloved matura [matriculation certificate]..
Itsele.
An Important Ruling of the Supreme Court

[Poland — law and taxes; kehilla and shechita.] Kehillas need not pay turnover tax on slaughterhouses.
The Supreme Court has handed down an important ruling which is of fundamental significance for all Jewish kehillas (communities).
At the time a number of kehillas were called upon to buy trade patents (licences), and some of them were even prosecuted and fined for not holding any patents. Buying a patent would of course later have led to turnover tax, etc.
The Jewish kehilla of Busko, which had been prosecuted by the tax authorities, carried the case all the way to the Supreme Court, and in this way the question has received a final solution.
The Supreme Court considered the complaint of this kehilla and recognised it as entirely justified; the court proceeded from the following premise:
In order to tax an enterprise it is necessary that the enterprise be run with the aim of giving the entrepreneur a net income, and that the existence of the enterprise depend on achieving this livelihood for the entrepreneur. Net income, however, cannot include earnings which are used to cover the expenses of the enterprise, such as maintaining functionaries, covering administrative expenses, etc.
The Jewish kehilla is an institution of public law whose task is, among other things, to supply the Jewish population with its religious needs, and to these belongs also supplying the Jewish population with kosher meat. For this purpose slaughterhouses have been set up and shochtim (ritual slaughterers) are maintained, who are religious functionaries of the Jewish kehilla. At the same time special ministerial regulations have fixed the fee (taxa) for ritual slaughter, and both the fee and the salaries of the shochtim, as well as all other expenses incurred in connection with the slaughter, are budgeted in advance in the kehilla budgets approved by the supervisory authority.
From all this it follows that the maintenance of ritual slaughter is incumbent on the kehilla on the basis of the binding regulations, and that the kehilla thereby fulfils one of its most important tasks, and not for the purpose of drawing special income from this item; the proof being that the income is regulated according to budgetary principles and must be planned so as to cover all the expenses connected with the slaughter.
The character of such an enterprise therefore differs in principle from all other enterprises, which are designed in advance to yield income and which are subject to turnover tax under the binding tax regulations. Ritual slaughter is therefore exempt from tax.
This ruling of the Supreme Court bears the number 2 K 564–33.
Mgr. J. Warszawski.
I'm Travelling on the Line...

[Feuilleton — humorous monologue; summer holidays, Będzin and surroundings.] (Monologue of a Jew who went to rent a "letnie mieszkanie" [summer flat].)
Related by Ben Amotz.
2.
Well, where did we stop? — At the "wycieczkowiec" [cheap excursion ticket], I think — yes, Fania, upon your life [?]! A convoluted [?] name, upon my life; whoever thought up this name is surely a very great man, because it is not so easy to get hold of this "wycieczkowy" ticket: first of all you have to buy it at the ticket office [?], and besides that one has to go through hard "wyścigi" [?] [races / ordeals] until you get it, the "wycieczkowiec" — I mean.
Arriving in Katowice I started running; where to, I was not sure; it was a miracle that I got my bearings and ran the way other men ran; I understood that the runners too have some "business" to transact, like me...
I ran from one platform to the other, down [?] and up, until my guts nearly turned over; at last I find myself in the right place, behind a long "ogonek" [?] [queue], just like once upon a time for a loaf of black bread from the magistrate.
— Proszę wycieczkowy! [An excursion ticket, please!] — I shout to the ticket cashier.
— Dokąd? [Where to?] — he asks me.
— "Co znaczy dokąd? [What do you mean, where to?] There, where all the Jews go to rent 'letnie mieszkania' [summer flats] for their 'sick' wives.
— "Dobrze" [Fine], but to which uzdrowisko [spa] [?]?
Hearing such refined [?] words from the ticket man [?], that he too is interested in my wife having an "uzdrowisko" — I turn soft as butter and answer him in a half-weeping voice:
— "Do Bystrej" [To Bystra]...
With the "wycieczkowiec" in my hand I set out onto the platform. I don't run, I positively fly [?] for joy; in my great hurry I nearly jumped into the train that carries poultry from Romania to Hitler-land. A fine face I'd have had, upon my life, had the Będzin Anti-Hitler Committee found out about it: I'd surely have met the same "defeat" as all those who get rich on the altar of the Jewish catastrophe in Hitler-land...
— It seems we're already moving — I say to my neighbour in the carriage — because my eyes are blocked by a "leżak" [deck chair] which a "sick" woman took with her into the carriage; above my head — a dozen suitcases, bundles of bedding, and around me — little baskets of "sok" [fruit juice], which is produced for the "summer stay" [?].
The matter of "sok" is indeed the main topic in the carriage; every woman tells of her housewifely skill: I — she says — squeezed fruit a whole summer, and it cost me not all that much.
— "Somehow I have no luck with squeezing — a second one chimes in — last year I fancied squeezing, so I gave it to my husband to take along, and he — the shlimazl — spilled the whole squeezing.
— "Ptui, ptui, may it not happen," an elderly woman takes the floor, yes, yes, when one squeezes one must take care that it should pass off in peace"...
— True, true — I silently agree with the pious Jewess — one must take care that it pass off in peace. Enough catastrophes have already happened when people did not take care while squeezing...
— — — — — — — — —
The "conversation" stops for a while; a stillness has entered "our" carriage. From time to time one hears only the snoring of the sleeping children, for whom their fathers provided in good time, right after Passover, a "letnie mieszkanie"; they are going, the little children, to inaugurate the exile-dacha already; meanwhile they are dozing — "Sleep then, little children, have a sweet sleep," the train is taking you into the region of high mountains and deep valleys".
— Water! Water! — a shout is suddenly heard, perhaps one of you has a little water, a young man has fainted!
It was a miracle that a woman, a "seriously ill" one no doubt, had "up above" a little bottle of "woda kolońska" [eau de Cologne], with which the young man was revived. Later it turned out that the young man is a Sosnowiec man who had not slept the whole night for fear of his good wife, lest he miss the train, and [so] he collapsed from weakness.
In Bielitz [Bielsko] the "atmosphere" became cleaner. The barricades of deck chairs, travel bags, bedding etc. were removed, and one already had the possibility of taking a look at God's beautiful world.
Looking around the carriage I only then saw that I would not get lost here, God forbid: nothing but familiar faces.
— Where are you going, Reb Kalman Yona? — I ask.
— On business, and you? — Kalman Yona asks me.
— Also on business...
— And you, where are you going? — we ask Aron Alurs [?].
— Also on business.
The end of it was that when the conductor shouted
— Wilkowice-Bystra! — we all got out...
— Is that so? Then all three of us have the same "trouble", so let's go together...

The Election Regulations for the Town Administrations

[Poland — local government; electoral law.] In the latest number of the „Dz. Ustaw“ [Dziennik Ustaw, the official Journal of Laws] (52) there appeared, in the form of a decree of the Minister of the Interior (Pieracki), the regulations for the elections to the town administrations, i.e. of mayors [presidents], deputy mayors and ławniks [ławnicy — members of the town executive board].
All town councillors have the right to vote. The elections are valid if more than half of the statutory number of councillors were present at the session.
If the necessary number of councillors was not present at the first session, the head of the town must call a second session within 7 days. If the second session does not take place either, the head of the town (mayor or commissioner) declares that the elections did not take place and reports this[?] to the supervisory authority, which has the right to appoint its own candidates.
The elections are ordered by the starosta [district head] in smaller towns and by the voivode [provincial governor] in larger ones; they also fix the dates of the election sessions.
The head of the town must notify every councillor of the sessions in writing at least 3 days before the date.
The election session is conducted by a chairman, who is elected by the councillors by an ordinary majority of votes. The chairman himself chooses 2 assistants (assessors).
The elections are secret: by name when electing the mayor or deputy, and by lists when electing the ławniks.
The validity of the ballot papers is decided finally by the presidium, i.e. the chairman and the 2 assessors, against whose decisions there is no appeal.
The election of the mayor or deputy.
Candidacies for mayor or deputy must be submitted in writing and be supported by a quarter of the statutory number of councillors.
The list may be signed only by the councillors present, and each councillor may sign only 1 list. The chairman then orders the vote, which is held on ballot papers on each of which there is only 1 candidate.
The voting technique is the same as in the elections to the town councils.
The candidate recognised as elected is the one who has received 1 vote more than half of the statutory number of councillors.
If none of the candidates for mayor or deputy has received the necessary number of votes, the chairman orders an elimination ballot: each voter may cast his vote for one of the 2 candidates who received the largest number of votes in the first ballot.
In the event of an equal number of votes, lot decides.
Only if the further[?] ballots give no result does the matter pass to the supervisory authority.
The election of ławniks.
Any Polish citizen may be elected ławnik who has completed 30 years of age on the day the elections are ordered, has command[?] of the Polish language in speech and writing and has the active right to vote in the town concerned, regardless of whether he is a councillor or not.
The number of ławniks amounts to 10 per cent of the statutory number of councillors, fractions being counted as 1 mandate; for example, 46 councillors elect 5 ławniks.
The lists of candidates must be submitted in writing and signed: 1) in towns of up to 25 thousand inhabitants — by a quarter of the statutory number of councillors, 2) in towns of up to 120 thousand inhabitants — by a sixth of the number of councillors, 3) in towns of over 120 thousand — by a tenth of the councillors.
Each list may be signed by a councillor who is present at the session. Each councillor may give his signature only once.
Combinations of lists are not permitted.
The distribution of mandates.
The mandates are allotted in proportion to the number of votes each list has received.
First of all the divisor (quota) is calculated: all the votes cast are divided by the number of mandates.
The following example clearly illustrates the whole system: Będzin has 40 councillors and 4 ławniks; 4 lists were submitted. List no. 1 received 18 votes, list 2 — 7 votes, list 3 — 9 votes, list 4 — 6 votes. The electoral quota is 40 divided by 4, i.e. 10 votes.
List 1 receives (18:10) 1 mandate.
List 2 receives (7:10) 0 mandates.
List 3 receives (9:10) 0 mandates.
List 4 receives (6:10) 0 mandates.
To distribute the remaining mandates, the number of votes received is now divided by the number of mandates plus 1.
18 : (1 plus 1) = 9
7 : (0 plus 1) = 7
9 : (0 plus 1) = 9
6 : (0 plus 1) = 6
The 2nd and third mandates go to lists 1 and 3.
To distribute the 4th mandate, the number of votes is again divided by the number of mandates obtained so far plus 1.
18 : (2 plus 1) = 6
7 : (0 plus 1) = 7
9 : (1 plus 1) = 4½
6 : (0 plus 1) = 6
The last mandate goes to list 2.
Supplementary elections.
In the event of the resignation of any candidate, or of the annulment of his election, supplementary elections are held within 14 days according to the same system.
After the elections the result is published and the minutes are signed by the presidium.
Protests against the elections may be lodged within 3 days after the elections. The right to lodge protests belongs to the same number of councillors as had the right to submit a list of candidates.
The head of the town is obliged to forward the election protest to the supervisory authority within 3 days.
In the event of the annulment of any elections, whether of a mayor, deputy or ławniks, the supervisory authority must order new elections within 14 days of the day of annulment.
The decree came into force on the day of its publication, i.e. on the 22nd of this month.
Dr. R. R.
The Commercial Schools and the Broad Public.

[Będzin — education and trade; article.]
The school year has now ended, and once again the schools are casting out thousands of children who have finished the elementary school course, and once again every father or mother faces the question: in what direction does one turn the child, so that it may become a useful citizen and human being and have an assured livelihood?
This question, which is eternally topical, mirrors the whole helplessness of every people and the psychology of its insecurity about tomorrow.
Decades ago this question did not exist. A boy went to cheder, later to yeshiva, still later studied his daily lesson, got married, ate kest [board at his in-laws'], became a merchant or... a melamed. Another class gave its child to a craftsman, and after long years of hard toil he independently earned his living.
Of education for girls there was no talk at all, because such a thing simply did not exist then.
In the last decades the situation has changed completely. Boys no longer want to be candidates for melamdim or for "air merchants" who draw their livelihood from a straw off a peasant's cart on a market day. The parents, too, do not want to leave their children barefoot in the street on the hard road of life — and indeed, since the war, a chase after education has begun, but not just any education: higher education. Parents who did not even have the material means for it put themselves into poverty, dressed their children in student uniforms and gave them an academic education, full of the hope that as soon as their children received the diploma of engineer, doctor or lawyer, they would have fulfilled their duty towards the children.
Since there was no system or calculation here, and what dominated was the fact of getting the diploma, and in the worst case the matura, the "market" was suddenly flooded with diploma-holding intelligentsia; the number of academics grew like mushrooms after rain, and the abundance of intellectual forces brought it about that the great majority found no possibility of obtaining practical employment; their future was put under a question mark; the economic crisis smashed a whole series of huge enterprises that could have employed a larger number of intellectuals, and the great army of qualified intellectuals had to throw itself on other occupations, in which all their work to attain the diploma went to waste.
It is therefore worth thinking over what profession to give the child in order to reach a goal and secure its future. Especially must one think it over when providing for the future of a girl. Until now a girl has been regarded as a person of second rank, who must marry, keep house, raise children and wait until the husband, in the best case, brings home the livelihood. That a woman is not a slave or a doll in a shop window, but a fully-fledged human being with a normal mind, who also has a duty to care for the livelihood and can occupy an important place in the structure of society — nobody thought of that. Now, however, it has become topical, because in a time of economic crisis it is impossible for one person to be able to earn for a whole family. The woman must therefore work too. The woman must therefore receive the proper education in order to be able to fulfil her duty.
Recently, indeed, a whole series of vocational schools especially for girls have been founded for this purpose.
Special attention is deserved by the commercial schools, because a large part of the Jews are engaged in trade. That Jewish trade is abnormal we must unfortunately admit, but the conditions of exile bring this about. Recently the government has issued a series of decrees under which the running of certain enterprises will be subject to restriction; it is especially worth drawing attention to the amendment (nowela) to the Industrial Law, which provides that even merchants must hold certificates of qualification in order to be able to conduct a business.
It is therefore advisable that parents who want to train their children for trade should send them to the commercial schools, because in the near future only persons who have completed a commercial school will be able to conduct a business.
As we learn, it is indeed for these reasons that the Będzin Small Traders' Association has decided to create a commercial school for the coming school year, about which the parents ought to know, because one of the greatest tasks of a merchants' organisation is to train the merchant of the future, and the initiative deserves to be welcomed.
Emem.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Balak)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Balak
The Portion
—o—
a) "Perhaps I shall prevail, that we may smite them" (Num. 22:6)
"Like one who removes one twenty-fourth of a se'ah." Midrash Rabbah, 20:4.
Why one twenty-fourth of a se'ah, of all things?
Rabbi Baruch of Leipnik (Lipník), author of "Baruch Ta'am", made a sharp-witted remark on this.
The Midrash says that if even one of the 600,000 (shishim ribo) Jews had been missing, they could not have conquered the Land of Israel; and that is what Balak wanted — "perhaps I shall prevail [to smite them]": perhaps I can diminish them, so that they will not number 600,000, and consequently will not be able to conquer the Land of Israel, found a kingdom there, become a strong nation and destroy their enemies.
The number of the Jews is counted in the Book of Numbers as 625,730; so, had Balak succeeded in reducing them by a twenty-fourth part, one twenty-fourth, which amounts to 26,072, there would have remained 599,658 Jews — that is, already fewer than 600,000; whereas, for example, had Balak succeeded in reducing the Jews by a twenty-fifth, which amounts to 25002, there would still have remained more than 600,000... Therefore the Midrash says: like one who removes one twenty-fourth...
—o—
b) "Neither curse them at all, nor bless them at all" (Num. 23:25)
The Gemara in Sanhedrin 105 says that an angel twisted Balaam's curses, and blessings came out of his mouth.
That is why Balak said to him: "Neither curse them at all, nor bless them at all" — do not curse them, for out of your curses only blessings come... Kotnot Or.
—o—
c) "Who sees the vision of the Almighty, fallen" (Num. 24:4)
"Fallen": when Balaam had his prophecy he would fall down [?]; and so with other prophets too. That is why it is said of Moses: "And there arose not again a prophet like Moses" — no prophet like Moses stood (kam) during prophecy; only Moses spoke with God while standing... Kohelet Moshe.
—o—
d) "How goodly are your tents, O Jacob" (ibid.)
These are the synagogues and study houses. Sanhedrin 105.
1.
Synagogues and study houses are, for Jews, tents — homes. They have no special name in the Bible. "Not like Abraham, of whom 'mountain' is written, nor like Isaac, of whom 'field' is written, but like Jacob, who called it 'house'" (Pesachim 88a) — the synagogue is for the Jew a house, a home... Imrei Chen.
• • •
"Not like Abraham, of whom 'mountain' is written, nor like Isaac, of whom 'field' is written, but like Jacob, who called it 'house'."
For certain Jews the synagogue is a mountain, a hill, which one climbs now and then, sometimes for the sake of a stroll. So one takes a stroll on the Sabbath in the synagogue. For others the synagogue is a field, which for the Sages is a symbol of a place of consultation. "And when they go out, they go out only into the field" (Berakhot 8b) — the synagogue serves only for communal meetings, to consult and decide on communal business. But the synagogue ought to be a house, a home... Kol Omer Kra.
2.
Jacob is a lower level than Israel. "Tent" symbolises outwardness and "dwelling" (mishkan) — inwardness. "Your tents" — your outwardness — Jacob, should be at a small level, "and your dwellings" — your inwardness — Israel, should be at a higher level. Your inwardness must always stand higher than your outwardness... Margalita Tava.
3.
In Mauszer [?] there lived a famous maggid (preacher), R' Rafael. When Rabbi Rafael came home for a holiday from his "tours" around the country, he prayed in the synagogue of the "mit'askim" — the Chevra Kadisha (burial society). He was invited by other synagogues, but R' Rafael would not pray anywhere but with the Chevra Kadisha. He used to say:
— In any case I'll end up in their hands; let me get used to them while I'm alive...
—o—
e) "And the people began to commit harlotry with the daughters of Moab" (Num. 25:1)
It was forbidden to drink wine at the homes of gentiles, because through drinking together and eating together one comes to intermingling. Here, however, it was "and the people began to commit harlotry" — the people began straight away with the worst... Sha'arei Efraim.
—o—
Haftarah.
f) "O my people, what have I done unto you, and wherein have I wearied you? Testify against me" (Micah 6)
The Master of the Universe complains to the Jews: what have I done to you, that you sin so much against me?..
Tzavarei Shalal,
The False Messiah (7)

[Serialized historical tale — David Alroy, the false messiah; installment 7, conclusion.]
Sh. Berg.

Her friend agreed. They stole out of the house, put on men's clothes, hired a couple of swift horses with a rider and flew off to Shushan [Susa] to David Alroy [printed "Al-Rai"].

Far was the road. Menucha urged the rider on and he drove the horses hard. She was racing against death. Her father's beadles had set out a day earlier — who knows whether she would overtake them, the messengers of death for David Alroy!

The horses swallowed the road; they seemed not to touch the ground at all, they floated through the air wrapped in clouds of dust. But to Menucha the road was so long, so far — if only she had wings!

And her father's beadles, with the ban, the death sentence, in their bosoms, ran on ahead.

The end of a messiah.

Menucha did not overtake the beadles. However swiftly her horses ran, the beadles ran swifter still. At night, when the whole camp was asleep, the beadles arrived. The guard met them; they took out the ban and showed it. In terror not a word was uttered; the sentries threw down their weapons and fled.

The beadles went to the elders of the army and showed them the ban; these did not wait a minute and scattered. Soon the evil tidings of the ban spread like a wild fire through the whole camp, and in the middle of the night they all scattered.

The heroic soldiers with their elders, who had not feared poisoned arrows, took fright at the poison of the ban. From the battlefield, where death lurked for them on every side, they had not fled — and before the curse of the ban they trembled; they threw everything away and scattered.

Even the bodyguard, the sixty chosen heroes who had guarded David Alroy day and night and were ready at every moment to give their lives for him, for the Messiah. Even they deserted him and fled.

In the tumult and shouting of the flight the "goyim", the non-Jewish soldiers, woke up. They took fright, thought that an enemy army had fallen upon them, and seized their weapons; they wanted to resist, they wanted to remain loyal to the redeemer of the Jews.

But when they heard the word "ban", they were badly frightened. They were not Jews, nor Christians or Mohammedans, but idolaters. They worshipped the wind. But they too were afraid of a ban. In those times the ban was sharper than a sword and more dangerous than the poisonous venom. People feared an evil plague less than a ban.

And the "goyim" too deserted David Alroy. They took out their [?], struck their tents, so that no trace of them should remain and the punishment of the ban should not pursue them. And with weapons in hand they went back home.

All alone remained David Alroy. All alone remained the Messiah. Empty was the camp where just now the army of the redeemer had stood, preparing with enthusiasm to go and conquer the Land of Israel. Not a living soul remained.

The evil beadles too were gone. They had fled; they had done their part and left.

All alone David Alroy lay in the palace. He was not awakened by the shouting and tumult of the fleeing army, nor by the deep stillness of the empty camp.

And Menucha's rider had driven the horses so hard that they could not make it. A stretch of road before Shushan the horses fell, and Menucha and her friend ran on foot with their last strength.

On the way they met fleeing soldiers. Menucha tried to stop them; terrified, they ran on, and only flung one word at her:
— Ban!

Menucha saw that the disaster had happened. She was too late. She ran breathless, no longer saw her friend, only ran; and her faithful friend drove out the last of her strength and ran after her.

Shushan was empty. Silent it was in the fortress, silent and frightened stood the palace; from room to room they ran with outstretched hands, and Menucha called and cried out:
— David Alroy! Messiah! David Alroy!

David Alroy lay on the bed dead, with a short sharp spear in his heart. On him lay a piece of parchment written all over, with a seal of a lion and a human hand above the lion.

That was the ban and the seal of the Nasi.

David Alroy, who had wanted to be the Messiah and whom the hand of a gentile could not reach to do him harm, was killed by a Jewish hand.

Menucha could not weep, could not scream. She fell like a stone beside the deathbed of her bridegroom, her Messiah.

Over her stood her faithful friend, quietly weeping.

Forsaken by all, betrayed by a brother's hand — a brother whom he had wanted to redeem from bondage — David Alroy lay with a pierced heart; only the two girls remained with him. One of them was his bride, with whom he had wanted to stand under the wedding canopy on the day of redemption on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

When Menucha came to herself, her eyes were dry. She could not weep. Mute, she went out with her friend into the courtyard; they dug a deep grave, and with her own hands Menucha buried her bridegroom, her Messiah.

When Menucha came home, she was no longer in her right mind. She stared with a fixed gaze somewhere into the distance. She saw no one, recognised no one. She kept talking to herself in broken words: Messiah... bridegroom... wedding canopy... holy mountain... She also repeated bits of Torah that did not hang together.

The Sultan of Persia returned to his capital and at once arrested all the leaders of the Jewish communities. They were forged in chains and thrown into prison. He wanted to hang them, but after great effort and much pleading he released them and contented himself with a large fine, which he imposed on the Persian Jews: one hundred hundredweight of gold they had to carry into the Sultan's treasuries.

The news of the ban and of David Alroy's death spread among the Jews of all lands. Most of them, even those who had believed in him, soon said that he was a false messiah. They were glad that he had perished; now they could be at peace again. But a great number of Jews mourned and lamented him in secret. They believed that, had it not been for the ban, he would have been the Messiah and would have redeemed the Jews from exile.

The flaming longing for the Land of Israel that David Alroy had kindled did not die with his death in many Jewish hearts. For a long time it still glowed [?] and drew them. They could not withstand the great yearning for the Holy Land, and in their thousands they cast off exile and emigrated to the Land of Israel.

(The End).
Saving — not hard!

[Advertorial — soap.]
Let us think about this a little: the selling price of every commodity consists of: 1) the value of "the raw materials, and 2) wages and profit. These expenses are always the same, both for a cheap commodity and for a first-class one, because the expenses for labour, pensions, taxes, packing, freight, commission etc. do not change — especially when it comes to a commodity such as, for example, soap. In that case a few groszy are saved only on the raw materials or on the quality of the soap. Therefore it pays, instead of a "cheap" unknown soap, to buy the best and most famous soap, "Kollontay with the washboard", which is lighter, lathers better and is more economical in use.
A Little Letter to Goebbels*)

Mr. Goebbels!
We have the honour of greeting you. We understand, Pan Goebbels, that you are already forced to go out to the "country" with your pack of goods — you have become a village peddler, and you are stuck not a little deep in the mud!
We, the Jews of Zagłębie, eagerly awaited your coming here, and even more eagerly we awaited your going away... We would surely have set you up on the holiday shelf — had we known that the shelf would break off...
Pan Goebbels, I have heard that you have a Jewish look, so I would like to invite you a little to Będzin, so that you could take a little stroll on Sabbath along the "Wszymna D..."[?]... I swear to you by beard and sidelocks that, although the boycott is in full swing, you would still sell not at all badly...
Believe me, when you come to Będzin, they will arrange[?] for you a real welcome (if your Torah has any face at all...).
Pan Goebbels, you want to hear my opinion on your race theory?
— If you please, hear my opinion:
As far as I have studied race theory, I have come to the conviction that race theory is a very heavy thing — that is why it is driven by horse-power.
Although I am a Jew, I must admit that Hitler is a treasure for the world, and by way of advice I tell you that such a precious treasure must be well guarded! How should you guard him? What do you mean, how? The way the whole world does it — a treasure is walled up inside the wall, or else it is buried...
On the occasion of your visit we wish you, Pan Goebbels, that you and your rebbe Hitler rise ever higher and higher — right up into heaven.
Yehuda Fridman.

The Little Jewish Girl

By Kazimiera Iłłakowiczówna. (A little story).
In the class there are many girlfriends; there are poor ones and rich ones. They study, or they don't. More than anything they love to play. There are all sorts of games. Only one little girl is always[?] the last in the games. Everyone catches her, she always pays forfeits, and she has never yet caught anyone.
"What is your name?" — everyone asks.
"My name is Klara" — says the little girl, quickly catching her breath.
"Why do you always let yourself be caught?" — everyone asks.
"Because I don't like playing — says Klara — I don't like running."
— "But it's so nice — everyone says — how can one not like playing!"
"I don't like it — says Klara — the children push me, beat me, because I am a Jewish child."
[—] in everyone [—] out of pity [—] [—] [little sleeve?].
"How dare they!" — she says — "Don't be afraid any more. I love you. I will protect you."

Today's Girls...

(A young man's confession) — recorded by Yosef Marszelik.
Going out walking with girls today costs exactly as much as the Będzin mikveh cost. If it costs health, so let it cost. Yes, walking out with girls becomes every year more and more of a costly business.
A perfectly ordinary girl from a middle-class home, with second- or third-class gauze [stockings?] above and below — if you offer her a light supper or a lunch in a café, she feels deeply insulted. True, the crisis has forced many girls to make compromises, and more than one of them who before the crisis demanded a portion of caviar as a starter is today ready to eat a piece of "marinated" herring. But most of them still stand by their positions, and should you mention the word "café", they get the [—][?].
Try going out with a girl nowadays and you will understand why so many young men become, poor things, criminals against their will. The girls have taken up a fashion: take them to the opera! To the cinema — they say — they will have time to go when, God willing, they get married. Have you ever heard such talk?!
In the old days, I remember, when you took a girl out for a "stroll", you led her up the "Górka", sat with her a couple of hours, told her your life story, taught her to sing "Di Shvue" [the Oath]. And on the way home you bought her a glass of soda water in the street for two groszy, and — that was that! Who even speaks[?] of buying her an ice cream — then you were a real spendthrift.
What's more: I still remember the time when treating a girl to ice cream with soda water was a real danger. In those years, if you went walking with a girl and bought her an ice cream, it was exactly as if today, say, you bought her a motor car.
— Are your intentions honourable? — the girl would ask when you invited her into an ice-cream shop.
And if the young man's "intentions" really were "honourable", only then did his troubles begin.
— Listen to me — the girl's mother would say to her daughter — don't go out with him any more; first find out what such a fellow lives on. He seems to me somehow too much of a spendthrift. Who knows where he gets his money from...
The girls of old, you should know, if a young man bought them some present, it was a big [occasion][?] for them, and they were so flustered that they did not know what to do with themselves. Whatever they gave a young man to hold, they forgot with him out of sheer enthusiasm.
There was hardly a young man who, the day after a stroll with a girl, did not have something to sell — a little shawl or a powder compact, or even a good bunch of keys that the girl had given him to hold for her and, in her great confusion, forgot to take back.
In those years, if you remember, girls used to carry in their hands little purses [sakiewki] with barely room for a handkerchief and a powder compact, and many a young man, if he was lucky, had every few days something of her things to sell. And may I, do you hear, have the good years for Jews, [—][?] what a young man used to find in those little purses.
But today's girls, besides costing you such torment, are such cold robbers that they are never impressed by anything and are never flustered. And if it ever happens that one of them forgets something with a young man she goes out with, it is the young man's watch, or his ring, or something else that she had occasion to ask him for.
That a girl of today should give the young man who goes out with her something to hold until he sees her home — that has not happened yet so far. Take a look at the purses that today's girls carry in their hands and you will understand why. Every such purse is a whole suitcase!
That is why going out walking with a girl nowadays is a [—] risk.
Well — what do you think? — it really is not good.
What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: The Majority of the Kehilla Board Favours Starting a Fight against Secret Slaughter

[Head of the local page; Będzin — Kehilla, ritual slaughter.]
What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday[?], 16 / 16 Tammuz 5694 — piątek 29 czerwca 1934 [Friday, 29 June 1934].)
Będzin
The majority of the kehilla board favours starting a fight against secret slaughter
The bewitched wheel. — A din torah or a fight. — A conference between the kehilla president and R' Itche Meir Levin. — The chances of the "dollar shochtimlekh".
The shechita affair in our town is the bewitched wheel around which the whole kehilla economy turns. It is the main question, which has not been solved to this very day, and thanks to which unheard-of scandalous deeds take place in this field.
At the last board meeting, too, the first item on the agenda was the shochtim question. More precisely: how to put an end to the secret slaughter which is being carried on on a wide scale by the "dollar shochtimlekh" as revenge for not having been included in the new budget.
At the meeting the so-called national "Progres" submitted a motion in which the kehilla presidium is called upon to start a fight against the shochtim Radoszycki and Gerlic and even to turn to the supervisory authority about it.
A second motion was submitted by the Agudah faction, which proposes that the matter of the secret slaughter of Gerlic and Radoszycki be settled by a neutral beth din, which — so it is said — the shochtimlekh are to choose themselves. If they do not abide by the ruling that the "neutral" beth din hands down, the rabbinate is to forbid their slaughter.
During the discussion of the motions submitted, the Agudah side put forward the concept of a compromise, in the sense that one of the "shochtimlekh", Mr. Radoszycki, should be taken on as a shochet. This concept meets with great difficulties: quite apart from the fact that the majority of the kehilla board and also public opinion are in favour of removing both shochtimlekh, there also exists a strict prohibition, bound up with the strictest bans (cherem), between the shochtimlekh Radoszycki and Gerlic, that they go together hand in hand and neither may "betray" the other.
———
This week a "political meeting" took place between the kehilla president Mr. Rubinlicht (printed "Rubiglicht") and R' Itche Meir Levin; at the "political conference" the question was discussed of how the tangled shechita affair in our town should be solved.
As we are informed, Mr. Rubinlicht wanted to prevail upon Mr. Levin to use his influence with his father, the Rabbi of Będzin, so that he would agree that the shochtim dispute be settled by an arbitration of both sides.
———
On Tuesday evening the so-called national bloc, members of the board and of the council, held a meeting at which the forms of the fight to be undertaken by the kehilla were discussed.
Board member (dozor) Tenenberg and parnas Kisner were in favour of announcing a competition for shochtim, and the shochet who is taken on should compete with the "dollar shochtimlekh"...
The chairman of the kehilla council Mr. Landner and board member (dozor) Najmark made a "far-reaching proposal", namely that a competition should also be announced for a rabbi. The proposal is justified by the fact that the rabbi cannot fulfil his functions, because almost the whole year he is at a summer residence or at spas.
The motions were postponed to another meeting.
When You Buy a Loaf of Bread, Give Another Grosz for the "Talmud Torah".

[Będzin — education and relief; Talmud Torah.]
When you buy a loaf of bread,
give another grosz for the "Talmud Torah".
The financial situation of the local Talmud Torah is simply catastrophic, and there is a threat that the institution where hundreds of poor Jewish children study will be closed.
In this connection the board of the Talmud Torah has adopted a resolution which is to be the last attempt to keep the institution in existence.
The last attempt consists in this: on every loaf of bread that is bought, whether in the bakeries or in the grocery shops, a stamp of one grosz will be stuck for the benefit of the Talmud Torah.
It is to be hoped that no one will refuse such a minimal payment, which can stave off the threatening liquidation of the Talmud Torah.
Now This Is Truly Called "Torah va-Avodah"...

[Będzin — movements; Torah va-Avodah; brawl.]
Now this is truly called "Torah va-Avodah"...
The young man Mr. G. came to the editorial office and related that on Sunday evening, in the premises of "Torah va-Avodah", he was attacked by "two brothers", who put out the light and began to beat him.
At the cries of Mr. G. the neighbours came running and put an end to the fight.
As we are informed, the board of the "Torah va-Avodah" society has decided to react to what took place. The attackers have meanwhile been expelled from the society and will stand before a party court.
25,000 zł. to Complete the Elementary School in Gzichów.

[Będzin — municipality; education.]
At the last session of the commissarial council [rada komisaryczna — the appointed town council] it was decided, among other things, to take a loan of 25 thousand zł. in order to complete the elementary school in... Gzichów [a district of Będzin].
At the session the president [mayor] proposed that the council permit him to transfer the sum in the budget from one item to another.
Mr. Rechnic voted against, Mr. Gutensztajn abstained, while Mr. Szwajcer voted for the proposal...
General Meeting of the Discount Bank.

[Będzin — economy; Jewish bank.]
Next Sunday the annual general meeting of the Discount Bank [Bank Dyskontowy] will take place; it is at present the only Jewish bank on a cooperative basis.
As people are saying, two sides have formed, which are holding meetings regarding the bank's future.
It is to be hoped, however, that neither of the sides will lend its hand to causing the bank any harm whatsoever, but on the contrary will make every effort that the institution should at the present moment continue to fulfil its task so far with regard to the broad Jewish masses.
General Meeting of “Torah va-Avodah”.

[Będzin — religious Zionism; kehilla; railways; education.]
On Sunday the annual general meeting of the “Torah va-Avodah” movement took place; it comprises “Tze'irei Mizrachi”, “Bruria”, “Yavneh”[?] and “Ha-Shomer ha-Dati”.
The delegate of “Ha-Po'el ha-Mizrachi”, Mr. Kalman Goldrajch (Jerusalem), took part in the meeting.
On various current Zionist and “Torah va-Avodah” problems, Messrs. Moshe Lewin, Kalman Goldrajch and others gave addresses.
After hearing the report of the secretary, Miss Sh. Rozenblum, various political and other resolutions were adopted.
Elected to the new general committee (va'ad klali) were: M. Lewin (chairman), Ch. M. Zylberberg (vice-chairman), Sh. Rozenblum (secretary), Y. Elboim (treasurer), Moshe Manela, Y. Hampel, Sh. Himelfarb, P. Gothart, Ch. Ornsztajn, Y. Frajberg, Sh. Tajtelbojm, Y. Rozyner, Y. Rozyner.
—o—
Session of the Kehilla Council.
On Tuesday afternoon a session of the kehilla council took place, which dealt with a series of formal matters.
—o—
“Podmiejski” Tickets — on “Podmiejski” Trains...
As is known, from 15 May the “podmiejski” [suburban] fare was introduced on all trains, except those running Katowice—Warsaw and back.
There are, however, Jews who love to split hairs and conclude that if the cashier sells “podmiejski” tickets, one may travel with them on any train.
Such “sages”, travelling from Sosnowiec to Sławków, were taken off at the local station, where reports were drawn up against them.

From the “Friends of France” Society.

[Będzin — societies and culture.]
At the general meeting of the “Friends of France” society, held on the 18th of this month at the premises of Dr. Stattler's commercial courses in Będzin, a temporary committee for the holiday period was elected, composed as follows: Dr. K. Stattler (chairman), Ch. Bauszykowski[?] (vice-chairman), Eng. Flauner (secretary), N. Goldberg (treasurer), Y. Wolf, Perl, L. Majtlis and A. Gutman (board members).
The task of the above society is to acquaint Poland spiritually[?] with France by means of lectures, conferences, articles in the press, excursions, etc.
Besides that, the society's aim is to organise popular courses in the French language, literature, geography and French history, and also to found a library and a reading room for the members.
After the holidays the committee will take energetic steps to realise all the tasks provided for in the statute, which has been approved by the Kielce voivode.
Sosnowiec — “I Thank You, Rabbi, for Your Attention, but in My House There Is No Jewish Kitchen”...

[Sosnowiec section heading; Sosnowiec — kashrut, rabbinate.]
A Jew is walking across the courtyard of the “szklarnia” [glassworks] when he sees a Christian servant chopping off the heads of young fowl with an axe.
The Jew takes an interest in this and indeed learns that the servant's employer is a Jew — a “modern” Jew, true, but a Jew all the same.
The Jew runs to Rabbi Szwarc and tells him about the act of nevelah [carrion — non-kosher slaughter] he has seen. Rabbi Szwarc sits down and writes a little letter to So-and-so son of So-and-so: how can this be?[?]
So-and-so son of So-and-so is not frightened and writes back a letter — a Yiddish letter at that — in these words:
“Rabbi, I thank you for the attention to your request; I am indeed a Jew, but in my house no Jewish kitchen is kept.”
“Keren Kayemet” Celebration in Sosnowiec.

[Sosnowiec — Zionism; Jewish National Fund.]
At the premises of “Ha-Shomer ha-Tza'ir” a large youth meeting took place with the participation of Goldrajch (Eretz Israel), Eng. Lewitas and the local “Kfar Ussishkin” committee.
The meeting is opened by the chairman A. Fromer, who honours the anniversary of the death of Dr. Arlosoroff by a standing tribute and explains the significance of the meeting.
The floor is given to the guest from Eretz Israel, Goldrajch, who speaks on the principles and importance of the Keren Kayemet — land as a political-strategic factor and as a means against speculation, which is a misfortune for Eretz Israel.
Then comes the distribution of diplomas. The honorary chairman Mr. Abramowicz presents the document, from which it can be seen that comrades Adler, Lewkowicz (Akiva), Buch (Ha-Shomer ha-Tza'ir), Fuks (Ha-No'ar ha-Tziyoni) and Meserman (He-Halutz) have during the last half-year fulfilled their quota with a surplus.
Mr. Fromer characterises the role of the Keren Kayemet as an educational institution for the youth.
In conclusion Mr. Eng. Lewitas takes the floor. — Besides land — the speaker exclaims — the youth must also be imbued with consciousness, with spirit, for earth without a soul is a golem (quoting in splendid language from the Maharal's “Golem”, which was likewise nothing but earth without a soul); the youth must be disciplined, filled with strength[?].
The large meeting was closed with “Ha-Tikvah” and “Teḥezaknah”.
Dr. Herzl Academy in Sosnowiec.

[Sosnowiec — Revisionist Zionism; memorial.]
On Sunday a memorial academy marking the thirtieth anniversary of the death of Dr. Theodor Herzl, organised by the “Keren Tel-Ḥai” committee in Sosnowiec, will take place at the “Palace”.
Taking part in the academy will be the member of the Revisionist Central Committee in Kraków, Dr. Yaakov Szechter, and the member of the Central Committee in Warsaw, Adv.[?] Elchanan Lewin, as well as Adv. Gross.
In the artistic-musical part Mrs. E. Perin (piano), M. Warszawski (violin), A. Ekstein (recitation) and also the Betar choir will take part.
On Tuesday, 20 Tammuz, a memorial service with the participation of Rabbi Hager will take place in the town synagogue.
Delegates to the Congress of the House-Owners.

[Sosnowiec — house-owners; road accident.]
Next Sunday a congress of delegates of all the house-owners' associations in the country will take place in Warsaw.
The local house-owners' association will be represented by Messrs. S. Lejzerowicz, B. Fejerpszyk[?] and D. Rozenfeld.
—o—
12-Year-Old Boy Killed by a Car.
On Ludwika Street in Sosnowiec a car accident occurred which cost the life of 12-year-old Avraham Stróż.
Stróż, who wanted to run across the street, was run over by a car, which seriously injured the boy. On the way to the hospital the victim died.
From Sporting Life.

[Sport — Będzin and Zagłębie.] The football tournament of "Hakoach".
On Saturday and Sunday a football tournament was held on the sports ground of "Hakoach" in Będzin, the proceeds of which were designated for building the sports grounds of "Hakoach" and "Zagłębianka". Taking part in the tournament were "Unia", "Diana" Katowice, "Zagłębianka" and "Hakoach" Będzin. Already the semi-final contests, held on Saturday, began with sensations. The course of Saturday's matches was as follows:
"Hakoach" — "Zagłębianka" 0:1 (0:1) [i.e. 1:0 to Hakoach; the paper's scores read right-to-left].
The first sensation of the tournament was the victory of "Hakoach" over "Zagłębianka", which was fully deserved. The only goal was scored by Gutman with a splendid header. Distinguishing themselves for "Zagłębianka": Karch and Stabierai[?], and for "Hakoach": Nunberg[?], Rozen 2 and Gutman. Worth stressing is the strong ambition of the "Hakoach" men despite the weak line-up. Referee Mr. Wiewióra — good.
"Diana" Katowice — "Unia" Sosnowiec 1:2 (1:1) [i.e. 2:1 to Diana].
The second sensation was the win of "Diana" over "Unia". The Katowice men played very sharply and already in the first half Hammer shoots the first goal, but Saboerars[?] equalises. After half-time "Unia" has a very strong superiority, but the forward line indulges in over-combination and spoils the best positions. Meanwhile Hammer breaks through and shoots the second goal. Although "Unia" was the better team, it leaves the field beaten. The "Diana" goalkeeper Urbańczyk distinguished himself. Referee Mr. Ehrgreich — good.
"Hakoach" — "Diana" 1:4 (1:2) [i.e. 4:1 to Hakoach, 2:1 at half-time].
The Katowice side came out in a better line-up with Machinek at the head, but "Hakoach" had its best match of the season and, although it played without Rozen 1, showed splendid technical play on all lines. The goals for "Hakoach" were scored by Hammel and Helberg, 1 each, and Szywek[?] 2. The goal for "Diana" was shot by Nowak. Referee Mr. Wiewióra — good.
"Zagłębianka" — "Unia" 4:5 (2:5) [i.e. 5:4 to Zagłębianka, 5:2 at half-time].
Both teams came out with reserve line-ups. The very fast and agile forward line of "Zagłębianka" scored 5 goals. In the second half the situation changes, as Unia takes over the initiative, but even so it must leave the field defeated. The goals for "Zagłębianka" were scored by: Karch 4 and Sabieras 1. Referee Mr. Grabiński — very good.
———
In the evening, in an elevated mood, a banquet was held in the hall on the "Góra Zamkowa", attended by all the teams, representatives of the clubs and representatives of the Zagłębie football and referees' associations. Also present was Mr. Malach, who gave a very fine speech and presented the representatives of "Hakoach" with the very valuable cup. The public enjoyed itself until late at night.
The cycling race of "Hakoach".
On Sunday "Hakoach" organised a bicycle race for the club championship for 1934. The race took place on the route: Będzin—Czeladź—Grodziec as far as the bridge in Szarlej and back. The length of the route is 30 kilometres. The championship for 1934 was taken by Fiszel in a time of 1:15:17. Second place was taken by Cerner, who because of a defect reached the finish with the bicycle in his hand. Third [printed "טריטער"] came Wizen[?] in a time of 1:22:02. The judges were Professor Stanek, Genborski[?], Rozencwajg; the leader of the race was Mr. Winer.
Championships of the "B" class.
"Kraft" — "Gwiazda" 1:2.
A sensational victory of "Kraft" to the tune of 2:1.
"Kinneret" — "Świt"[?] 0:3 (0:1).
The Sosnowiec "Kinneret" scored an easy victory over the very weak "Świt"[?] to the tune of 3:0.
"Płomień" — "Makkabi" 0:4 (0:0).
"Makkabi" is in very weak form and stands at the edge of the "C" class. In the club as a whole there reigns a lack of discipline, and even other sections give no signs of life. It is a great loss for Jewish sport in Sosnowiec that "Makkabi" should be allowed to go under.
Championships of the "C" class.
"Jalanag"[?] — "Brygada" 1:1 (:1).
Championships of the "Makkabi" World Union.
Today, Friday the 29th, the Będzin "Hakoach" begins to play the championships of the "Makkabi" World Union. The first match takes place in Będzin, and on Sunday — the return match in Sosnowiec.
Debe.
—o—
A banquet of the pupils of the Mizrachi school
On completing the school year, this week the graduating pupils of the "Mizrachi" school in Będzin, who finished the school this year, organised a banquet for the teachers.
A greeting speech was delivered by the pupil Pfeifkopf[?] (Dąbrowa) (in Hebrew) in the name of all the comrades — "We will — he says — be in the ranks of the halutzim, who build our land in the spirit of Israel the Elder and in the spirit of justice and the labour of one's hands."
Speeches were also given by the principal and the teachers.
At a beautifully served table the pupils sang Land-of-Israel songs and gave gifts to the educators. With the singing of "Hatikvah" the banquet is closed.
—o—
The books of the Sosnowiec Chevra Kadisha returned.
The books of the Chevra Kadisha in Sosnowiec, which had been taken away a few weeks ago by the investigating authority, were returned on Wednesday.

"Luna Park" in Będzin.
For 2 weeks now a "Luna Park" with various entertainment numbers has been in Będzin. The "Luna Park" is staying a few more days.

Friday, 23 Tammuz 5694 — „What's new in Zagłębie?“ — piątek 6 lipca 1934 [Friday, 6 July 1934].
Knifings and split skulls — the newest means of getting rid of tenants

[Będzin — violence; landlords and tenants.] In the previous issue of our paper we reported on the attack on the Żabner[?] brothers, who were wounded with knives during a sharp dispute with their landlord, Mr. Merin.
The incident happened barely 8 days ago, and already we are informed of a second brutal assault, by Mr. Feldman, son of a house-owner on Wazhrushe[?] Street in Będzin, who with an iron bar split the head of his tenant Anszel Skoczylas[?] as he was going out into the courtyard with a bucket of water.
Skoczylas was left lying unconscious in a pool of blood. The feldsher who was called, Mr. Szer, gave Skoczylas first aid and ordered him taken to hospital at once.
Alerted, the police came and drew up a report against the „heroic“ young man.
Solemn memorial services in Zagłębie — for the 30th anniversary of Dr. Herzl's death

[Będzin, Sosnowiec — Zionism; Herzl anniversary; followed by a short item: Grodziec.] On Tuesday at the time of the afternoon prayer the Zionist organisations in Będzin held a memorial service in the town synagogue. The service passed off solemnly. Cantor Mr. Bejm[?] with the choir sings the appropriate chapters of Psalms and „El male rachamim“, and Messrs. Winadzki[?] and Manela speak.
Mr. Winadzki speaks of Herzl's prophecy, which is being fulfilled before our eyes. Mr. Manela points out that today's fratricidal hatred is far from pure Herzlism.
After the Jewish and Polish anthems are played by the „Hakoach“[?] orchestra, the memorial ends.
———
At the same hour a memorial service took place in the Sosnowiec synagogue. Taking part were the organisations „Mizrachi“, the Revisionists, Ts.S.[?], „Maccabi“ and „HaShomer HaDati“, each organisation with its banner.
Speeches were made by Mr. G. Stawski[?], who related personal memories of Dr. Herzl, Mr. B. Jasny, M. Windman, and finally Rabbi Hager, whose speech left a strong impression.
The appropriate prayers were performed successfully by Cantor Mr. Lichter with the choir.
At the end the Jewish and Polish anthems are sung.
—o—
A street named after Pieracki
The gmina in Grojce→Grodziec[?] resolved at its last session that the present Czeladzka Street shall be named after the tragically killed Minister Pieracki.
From craftsmen's life in Sosnowiec

[Sosnowiec — craftsmen; followed by three short items: Będzin, Katowice, Będzin.] On Sunday a general meeting of the craftsmen of Sosnowiec took place, at which a board was elected consisting of Shlomo Nachum Langer (president), Yosef Grinberg (vice-president), Sh. Rozencwajg (secretary), Avraham Yaakov Wiślicki (treasurer), Yoel Diament, Shmuel Praga, Itzik Kłaszner, Peretz Rozenberg, Yosef Brumer.
The new board has embarked on broad activity.
—o—
Recruitment drive of „Tseirei Mishmerei Cholim“
There exists in Będzin a youth society called „Tseirei Mishmerei Cholim“ (Young Watchers of the Sick). The society carries on broad activity in the field of night watches at the sickbed, gives out medicines and nurses poor sick people. Because of its small funds the institution is conducting a recruitment drive, which deserves to be supported.
—o—
He bought himself a „bargain“...
On Piłsudski Street in Katowice Mr. Yitzchak Hirszlender came upon two unknown persons, who declared that they wanted to sell 2 diamond rings because they lacked money for the expenses of the journey to Palestine.
H. took this at face value and bought the „diamonds“ for 80 zł.
—o—
General meeting of the Będzin Charity Society
Next Monday at 9 in the evening a general meeting of the Jewish Charity Society will take place in the premises of the „Merchants' Society“.
It is desirable that the members come to the meeting, at which a number of important public matters will be dealt with.
The third quarter-ticket of the 100,000 zł.

[State Lottery — sponsored item (advertorial).] The caprice of luck goes by remarkable ways. When four friends, employees of the gmina administration of Derażne, Kostopol county, Messrs. Paweł Drabot, Sergiusz Epifanowicz, Jan Płaskowski and Łukasz Połanienko[?], decided to club together to buy a quarter-ticket of the State Lottery, various signs in heaven and on earth showed that they must buy number 137.071. They applied to the lottery collector's office to send them that number. It turned out, however, that the number had already been sold, and the collector's office sent them another number, which is nonetheless similar: the same opening digits and also[?] the same sum of digits, namely 19. In this way the above-mentioned became partners in number 137.215.
It seems that all the „signs“ on earth and in heaven were no deception, since it turned out that it was precisely a stroke of luck that the requested number was missing, because this gave the colleague-partners the chance to receive part of the main prize, which fell in the first class of the 30th State Lottery. Each of the participants will receive 5,000 zł., which for them is almost an estate. Encouraged by the success, they have now decided to hold regularly, in partnership, two quarters of different tickets, believing that luck will smile on them again and that in one of the further classes they will win a considerable sum.
Naturally this is quite possible. Anyone who plays can win; one should therefore get a ticket for the second class as quickly as possible, because the drawing begins as early as 17 July. 306W
A Keren Kayemet Committee Founded in Bystra

[Keren Kayemet LeIsrael — Bystra.]
In Bystra a committee was founded these days, which is conducting intensive work for the benefit of the K.K.L. [Keren Kayemet LeIsrael, the Jewish National Fund]. In the short time the committee has already managed to collect about 70 zł.
The committee consists of: S. Frenkel (chairman), A. Z. Bornsztajn, Miss Szenberg, Miss Cygo [?], Miss Mandelbaum and two young women from the “kibbutz”.
—o—
The Strike of the Sosnowiec Shochtim — Settled
[Sosnowiec — Community.]
On Wednesday a strike of the shochtim (ritual slaughterers) broke out at the Sosnowiec slaughterhouse, because they are not being paid their full salaries (“pensions”).
In connection with this the Sosnowiec [community] president came to the slaughterhouse and brought it about that the shochtim returned to work, promising them at the same time that he would make efforts to have their grievances properly settled.
