Notes of the Week

[Notes of the Week — abroad and Poland.] In Germany civil war has broken out. There are many killed; the Czech and French borders have been closed to the fleeing stormtroopers.
—o—
In Eastern Galicia there has been a flood, which caused considerable damage.
—o—
The President in Danzig has declared that the Senate will not permit Jews to be harassed.
—o—
From an unknown cause the City Hall (Rathaus) in Vienna has burned down.
—o—
As of the 1st of this month a telephone connection has been opened between Moscow and all the cities of Poland.
—o—
In Łódź the well-known firm of Ludwig Geyer has gone bankrupt.
—o—
Herzl Memorial in Bystra.
We are written from Bystra:
Last Monday evening, on the initiative of the well-known Zionist activist R' Shlomo Frenkel, a memorial service of mourning took place in the villa "Sielanka" [printed "Shielanka"], in connection with the 30th anniversary of the death (yahrzeit) of Dr. Herzl.
The memorial is opened by Eng. Mr. Barensztajn (Będzin), and on current affairs Messrs. Yosef Cinz and Yitzchak Bursztyn speak (in Hebrew).
Then the pupil Chana Barensztajn (Będzin) and Miss Diamant give recitations.
The recitation "The Golden Chain" ("Di goldene keyt") is performed by Mr. Seichtfal[?].
A warm closing speech (shalom-speech) is delivered by Mr. Yitzchak Wigadzki[?] (Będzin), and with the singing of "Hatikvah", performed by the choir of the local "kibbutz", the solemn memorial is closed.
A large number of visitors from Zagłębie took part in the memorial.
The Festivities in Honour of “Sea Day” in Zagłębie

[Zagłębie — Sea Day.] The festivities began on Thursday evening. On Third of May Square in Będzin a number of organisations assembled, among them Jewish ones too, and after the siren signals a procession formed as far as the "Przemsza", where a series of impressive festivities took place. "Hakoach" made a fine showing with its orchestra at its head, but when gymnastic numbers had to be performed, this was done by members of the Sosnowiec "Maccabi".
On the "Przemsza" dozens of illuminated "wianki" (wreaths) floated to the strains of several orchestras.
The festivities in Sosnowiec, Dąbrowa and the surrounding places also turned out impressive.
The Jewish population took a warm part in the festivities.

What's New in Upper Silesia?

[Upper Silesia — Königshütte; Betar.]
Betar Flag Unveiling in Königshütte.
On Sunday the flag unveiling of "Brit Trumpeldor" was celebrated in Königshütte, with the participation of Betarim and Hayalim (soldiers) from Upper Silesia and Zagłębie, who assembled in the square of the Jewish community, where the member of the Betar Commissariat (Netsivut), Mr. Y. Chrust, takes the report from those assembled. Then all go in closed ranks to the synagogue, where the cantor with the choir sings the appropriate psalms. "Then Rabbi Dr. Kalberg delivers a brilliant speech, in which he stresses the historical significance and sanctity of a flag for the Jewish people.
Amid solemn silence Rabbi Kalberg unfurls the flag, reciting the appropriate prayer as he does so.
After that Rabbi Kalberg takes the oath from commander (mefaked) Brand and the flag-bearer Barkowski.
In the name of the Betar Commissariat Mr. Chrust speaks, handing the flag over to commander Brand. After the prayer a march-past takes place before the house of the Jewish community, which is taken by Rabbi Dr. Kalberg, a member of the district command of the Kielce voivodeship, Commandant Glidman, Commandant Zaki (Katowice), Com. Kleiner (Mandoszew [so printed; probably Modrzejów]) and commander Brand (Königshütte).
In the evening a festive Herzl Academy took place in the Reidensberg hall. The academy is opened by commander Brand, and then greetings are given by: Eng. Unger in the name of the Jewish community in Königshütte, Waga (Brit HaTzohar), Levi (Brit HaHayal, Bielsko), Glidman (Brit HaHayal, Będzin), Kleiner (Brit HaHayal, Magroszew [so printed; probably Modrzejów]), Rosenberg (Betar, Zawiercie), Triger (Betar, Sosnowiec), Rosenbaum (Betar, Jęzor), Szapiro (HaTzohar, Königshütte), Rabbi Blumenfeld (Königshütte). A storm of applause greets the address of Mr. Grubner (Beuthen), who brings greetings in the name of the Jewish association of the State Party in Beuthen, "Betar". At the end speeches are given by Messrs. Chrust and Schwaeber.
With the singing of Hatikvah the Herzl Academy is closed.

[Upper Silesia — short news items from the column „What's New in Upper Silesia?“; Katowice, Zabrze, Knurów, Kostuchna, Rybnik and more.]
On Saturday a break-in was carried out at the office of the Hungarian Consulate in Katowice. The burglars broke open the iron safe, but found no cash at all there.
—o—
Pickpockets
While buying cigarettes at a kiosk on Dworcowa Street in Katowice, Mr. Lender of Katowice had a considerable sum of money stolen from his pocket.
—o—
Two Big Motor Accidents
On Sunday motor accidents occurred in Zabrze and beyond Gleiwitz. 8 passengers, among them a woman and a child, were seriously injured.
—o—
Tragic Accident While Putting Out a Spirit Stove
Mrs. Halda in Wełnowiec wanted to put out the spirit stove after cooking. At that moment her clothes caught fire and she was completely enveloped by the flames. Despite the quick rescue the woman died of her wounds; her husband, who saved her, is also seriously injured.
—o—
Polish Scouts from America in Katowice
On Tuesday a group of 60 Polish scouts from America arrived in Katowice. The guests were received by a special committee. In the evening a dinner was given for them at the „Savoy“ hotel.
—o—
Tickets with an Earlier Date
For the convenience of the public, the railway directorate in Katowice has authorised the sale of tickets two days in advance for those travelling to congresses, celebrations, summer holidays, etc.
—o—
„Heil Hitler“ on the Insurgents' Monument
In Knurów the local Hitlerite hooligans hung up Hitlerite placards in several places. On the monument to the insurgents „Heil Hitler“ was written.
The hooligan deeds aroused bitterness among all the inhabitants. The Polish press demands a strict inquiry into who the guilty are.
—o—
Tragic Death of Two Workers While Decorating for the „Sea Festival“
In Kostuchna several workers were busy putting up a decoration at the local zinc works in honour of the „Sea Festival“. At a certain moment the scaffolding collapsed and two people were killed on the spot.
—o—
Suicide of an Unemployed Jew
In the South Park in Katowice the 53-year-old Paul Frei hanged himself. The cause is unemployment and want.
—o—
Outing of „Maccabi“
On the 7th of this month „Maccabi“ in Nowa Wieś[?] is holding a garden outing; by the reckoning it turns out that the day of the festivity falls on Sabbath...
—o—
Memorial Service for the Murdered Minister Pieracki
Last Sunday a mourning memorial service for the tragically perished Minister Pieracki took place in the Rybnik synagogue. The Jewish population took part in the memorial en masse. Representatives of the military and local authorities were also present.
After the memorial had been conducted by the cantor Mr. Kalmus, the rabbi Dr. Kalberg delivered a speech in which he pointed out the great loss of Minister Pieracki.
With „Boże, coś Polskę“ the memorial was closed.
—o—
The Interest-Free Loan (G. Ch.) Fund in Rybnik
The G. Ch. [gemilut chasadim, interest-free loan] fund in Rybnik is developing steadily and is growing both in the number of members and in its income; thanks to this the board has decided to raise the amount of the loans from 100 to 200 zł.
—o—
Anti-French Demonstrations in Zabrze
In Zabrze (German Upper Silesia) anti-French demonstrations took place; the speakers presented the French military as brutes, and anti-French songs were sung.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Pinchas)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Pinchas
The Portion
—o—
a) "In that he was zealous for My sake among them" (25:11)
Pinchas's glory lay in "in that he was zealous for My sake among them": around him stood thousands of the tribe of Shimon, and Pinchas sanctified God's Name and killed Zimri precisely "among them" — precisely before everyone's eyes.
"Run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem… if ye can find a man that seeketh the truth" — in the houses, in hiding, you will find many righteous men; but in the streets of Jerusalem, out in the lanes, when one has to show fear of Heaven in public, there "a man that seeketh the truth" is already rare.
Kli Chemda.
—o—
b) "Wherefore say, Behold, I give unto him My covenant of peace" (ibid., 12)
Tosafot in tractate Zevachim, folio 101b, cite a Sifrei which infers from the verse "My covenant of peace" that high priests came forth only from Pinchas; and the Sifrei counts three hundred and eighty high priests (80[?] in the First Temple and 300 in the Second Temple).
The question arises: how is this inferred from the verse "My covenant of peace"?
But the Gemara (Kiddushin 66b) says that here the word is read "shalim" (with a broken vav), and the word "shalim" amounts [in gematria] to 380...
Ktonet Or.
• •
"Wherefore" — precisely because he is a zealot and sacrifices himself for the truth — "Behold, I give unto him My covenant of peace". Precisely he will bring peace among Jews, although people think that peace can only be brought when one gives up the truth...
Divrei David.
• •
Rabbi Pinchas of Korets [Korzec], who laboured extraordinarily on the virtue of "truth", was asked: Rebbe, you warn us to say only the truth; and when one needs to make peace, may one then tell a lie for the sake of peace?
Reb Pinchasl replied:
— If one wants to make peace, true peace, then one says precisely the truth, and strongly the truth, the whole truth — only thereby does one make peace...
—o—
c) "To the more ye shall give the more inheritance, and to the fewer ye shall give the less inheritance" (26:54)
Such is the nature of the Land: "to the more" — when many Jews come into the Land — "the more inheritance": the Land of Israel becomes ever larger and takes everyone in; "and to the fewer" — when few Jews come — "the less inheritance": the Land seems to shrink... As the Sages say: "It is written of it 'the land of the deer' — just as the deer's hide cannot hold its flesh", so too the Land of Israel is, as it were, stretched out when more Jews come in...
R' Yitzchak of Olik [Olkusz?].
—o—
d) "A man over the congregation" (27:16)
"The Holy One, blessed be He, does not give greatness to a man until He has tested him in a small matter, and then He raises him to greatness... And so of Moses it says 'and he led the flock to the farthest end of the wilderness' — to keep it from robbery; and the Holy One, blessed be He, took him to shepherd His people."
Shemot Rabba, section 2.
Only one who hates robbery can be a leader. "Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord, and who shall stand in His holy place?" Who is worthy to be a leader and one who serves in holiness? — "He that hath clean hands and a pure heart; who hath not lifted up his soul unto vanity"... When God set about choosing Moses as a leader, He tested him above all as to whether he was careful about robbery...
Kol Omer Kra.
• •
In a letter of Rabbi Akiva Eiger (printed in the "Agudat Sofrim") to his daughter, the Gaon writes to her that he has learned that in the little town near[?] Posen [Poznań] where his daughter lived the bath-keeper had died; he therefore asks her to lease the bathhouse for him, since he intends in his old age to leave the rabbinate and become a bath-keeper — because in his last days he wishes to earn his living permissibly and not forbiddenly...
—o—
e) "Which may lead them out, and which may bring them in" (ibid., 17)
"Which may lead them out, and which may bring them in" — and not such a leader whom the community leads around by the nose.
Ktav Sofer.
—o—
f) "And Moses brought their cause before the Lord" (26 [=27]:5)

The Slap in the Face — and How Did People React?

[Zagłębie — Sick Fund; article.]
We did not want to believe it. It seemed to us that these were empty phrases, sucked out of one's finger, of the kind that arise especially in so tense a situation as the one in which we find ourselves today.
Our grave economic situation on the one side, and all sorts of antisemitism lying in wait to exterminate us on the other, throw us more than once, and rightly so, off balance, so that we may often take fantasies and dreams for genuine reality.
A few weeks ago we brought the report that the Sick Fund (Kasa Chorych) in Zagłębie is sending out for the summer at its own expense, as every year, 250 poor children, and among them not a single Jewish child is to be found. We doubted its correctness; we could not imagine that this should be a fact, an innocent truth. Unfortunately we heard that what we had not believed was confirmed, and for a second time we wrote a note about this unbelievable injustice, reckoning that this would be quite enough for the public to react to the injustice thereby done to us. But apparently nobody in the Jewish public here felt hit, and the fact passed as if it were nothing at all, as if it had touched nobody's honour.
Last year they still gave us 50 children, and this time the "gift" has been abolished altogether. We know that Christians, no great friends of the Jews, did not believe that we could be treated so [?]; in our own circles, on the other hand, nobody took the slightest account of this unheard-of injustice.
Actually, we cannot by any means understand how one can remain indifferent to a question that degrades our honour. Possibly some people have the notion that if the Sick Fund sent 50 Jewish children along with a few hundred non-Jewish ones, this was a kind of charity that we had not earned. We, however, see the question quite differently: no favour was done to us when a little bone was thrown to us. We pay heavy money into the Sick Fund, and what was given to us came to us rightfully; we honestly earned what was ours.
And now, when such a respected institution as the Sick Fund in Zagłębie comes and says that it need give us nothing, that from us one need only take, this is without doubt a slap in the face that insults all of Jewish Zagłębie; and every Jew who possesses not only Jewish pride, but is even only averagely conscious, must feel insulted when he is ignored, when he is stamped as a citizen of the second rank, at a time when in taxes he is the first payer, the one who ruins himself; his civic duties he fulfils, however heavy and unbearable they may weigh on him.
Such treatment hurts us, because at the very least we would like to know why we are not due to be given anything this year: have we, in the course of the year, become so much richer that we no longer need anyone's help? On the contrary, let us hear an answer, let them give us reasons why we are forgotten just when we ought to be remembered.
But what hurts us even more is that we have no one to raise the question, that the leadership does not come forward [?] to react when we are wronged. And that is, after all, self-evident: as long as we do not have the representation that would raise questions and feel insulted, they are sure in that camp that no harm has been done to anybody. That is what hurts most of all. That is what pains the Jewish heart.
Where are they, our public workers; where are they, those who push so hard for a seat [on a council] and are ready to turn worlds upside down when they are disturbed in their plans?
And where are the industrialists and the big merchants and joint-stock firms, which pay tens of thousands of złoty into the sick funds? Where are they; why do they not make themselves heard, when a word from them would unconditionally be taken into account, willingly or unwillingly?
May one really remain indifferent to problems which ought to be protected [?] and cultivated by us? Can one really put up with it like this and not react to injustices when they are aimed directly at us?
True, we had not imagined that Jewish Zagłębie would remain so indifferent to the question under discussion. We could not understand that "people with hearts" could calmly look on as fifty children languish in the great heat in attic and cellar dwellings, while they could have been sent out at the expense of the Sick Fund. Unfortunately we have seen that this did happen and that the matter interests nobody. It goes without saying that this has stamped the apathetic attitude of our representatives towards the community.
We would, however, like our representatives and industrialists and important, respected merchants, who carry weight in the decisive circles, to intervene in the question and to bring it about that we receive our quota in the same measure and size as until now, so that the children may still travel this year as used to be the case in previous years; if the first group has already left, it [the quota] can be allotted to the second group.
Be that as it may, we must not remain indifferent and helpless in this question. It is a matter of principle, it is a matter of our honour, it is a matter of our prestige, which must be rescued, if you have let it fall.
If you do not want [?] — and you certainly do not want — this to fall on your conscience, you must at once take a stand on the question and carry out the appropriate intervention, which will bring the desired results.
R. Les.
When Does a Debt with a Fixed Due Date Become Payable Earlier?

[Law — law of obligations; legal explainer.]
In relations governed by commercial law there is a rule that as soon as a merchant suspends his payments, all his current debts automatically become immediately payable. The Code of Obligations [Kodeks zobowiązań] carries the same provision over into the sphere of civil obligations as well; consequently it follows that in every case where a debtor becomes insolvent, or where by his conduct he merely reduces the security given for the debt, all his debts with fixed due dates become payable at once.
Methods of Payment of Foreign-Currency Obligations

[Law — law of obligations; legal explainer.]
A money debt in foreign currency may be paid in złoty at the day's rate at the given place, unless payment strictly in the foreign currency has been expressly agreed.
In case the debtor is late with the payment date, the creditor has the right to demand that the debt in question be paid at the rate of the day on which the debt was due to be paid, or of the day on which it is paid.
Two Marranos

[Serialized story — Nazi Germany; first installment.]
Chaim Berg.
A story from Nazi Germany.

A duel of words between two diplomats.

On one of the hot days of riots in Hitler-land, a conversation took place at the Spanish legation in Berlin between the deputy of the envoy and a high-ranking German diplomat:
"Marquis!" said the German diplomat. "The Minister has sent me to express his great and deep regret over the sad incident and to convey to you his assurance that those guilty of the incident will be severely punished."
The German diplomat expected the words to act like a red-hot iron on the body. He thought the marquis would explode and pour over him the hot pitch of anger and insults, and he had diplomatically prepared himself for the attack. But he was mistaken.
"Why should the guilty be punished, Baron?" the marquis answered calmly and indifferently, as though the whole ugly incident had happened not to him but to some outside person. Yet in doing so he pulled his hand away, with a quick movement, from the fat, sweaty paw of the big German, as if with a feeling of physical disgust.
The question confounded the baron. His red face turned redder still, and sweat broke out on his forehead.
"What are you saying, Marquis! To insult a diplomat of a friendly state — that is not permissible, that cannot be tolerated..."
"The barbarians are not to blame... You taught them this, you trained them for it."
And the marquis raised his eyes and measured the German diplomat with a long look of deep contempt. Almost with disgust. And with that look he confounded the baron even more.
"We... we trained them... to insult diplomats in the street!... For God's sake, Marquis! What has come into your head? You are joking, Marquis!"
"Who else taught the police to seize poor, innocent Jews in the streets, to pull and tear out their beards and torment them barbarously? After all, the Brown Shirts wore police insignia."
The German diplomat had prepared himself for various excuses; to hear such undiplomatic talk from a diplomat he had not reckoned with. The words simply violated all the laws of diplomatic language. Do diplomats really speak so crudely and openly among themselves? What is more, and above all, he was deeply shocked that this Spanish marquis should take up the cause of Jewish beards at all — what business is it [?] of his anyway to meddle in the internal affairs of the state to which he has been sent as a diplomat? Well, when the Polish envoy takes up the cause of Jewish beards, that is diplomatic; for him it is an opportunity to show the world that the Poles are fine people. But what has the Spaniard to do with it? What a bad diplomat this marquis is!
— So the baron almost pitied him; and this in itself reminded him that the most important thing was not to answer the insult which his government and he personally had just received, but to win the diplomatic tournament. He therefore quickly mastered his seething anger, chased the angry grimaces from his broad, fat face, and broke into a good-natured laugh:
"We cannot help it, Marquis! You know, after all: 'when you chop wood, chips fly.' Ha-ha-ha! May I sit down?"
And without waiting for an invitation he sat down with a "Danke schön," took out his cigarette case and offered it to the marquis. The marquis declined. The baron lit up himself, not taking his laughing eyes off the Spaniard, who was still standing bent over with his hands on the table.
The baron glanced at the Spaniard's two small, white, womanly hands, which trembled and betrayed his suppressed agitation and anger — a great inner storm, which he tried to hide from the baron behind a feigned, nonchalant calm.
The baron already felt quite calm and ready for a diplomatic tournament, fully certain of victory over the Spaniard.
"You yourselves have only just gone through a revolution, Marquis, so you must know what a revolution is. A revolution is no parade and no opera performance that can be staged in advance down to the smallest detail."
"Yes, we went through a revolution, but we did not tear out Jewish beards in the streets and did not beat Jewish women," the marquis replied, finally sitting down at the table, as though he had thereby accepted an invitation to the tournament.
"And where would you have had Jewish beards to tear? Ha-ha-ha! You got rid of them back in 1492, and we Germans envy you terribly. If only we had done it then, when Ferdinand and Isabella drove them out. Instead we took in a good part of them and paid a heavy penalty for it."
"It is not worth casting pearls before this fat German swine," the marquis decided to himself, and pressed a button by his desk, summoning the footman.
For a while both diplomats were silent. But the temperamental Spaniard could not restrain himself:
"I will make you a proposal," the marquis broke the silence with a smile, resting his big head of thick, pitch-black hair on his small white right hand. The baron seemed to glance at the Spaniard's small, well-kept [?] womanly hands, and a tremor of desire ran through his big fat body...

The Economic Front

The long-lasting economic crisis has, it is true, struck all branches of economic life in Poland. In fact, however, it has affected trade, and especially Jewish petty trade.
The abnormal socio-economic structure of Jewish life comes out in the full measure of its strangeness and specificity precisely in times of crisis. The in any case weak, shaky economic positions of the Jewish popular masses are shaken at the very first blast of the economic storm. The chronic disease of the Jewish economic organism, which grows very much worse in a time of crisis, is still more dangerous because of external causes, which go far beyond the measure, beyond the limits of purely economic factors, since the crisis is [printed: "in"] the most convenient moment for brutal attacks on the Jewish popular mass and its very existence — on the part of those factors which seek, and wish to persuade, that they find a remedy for all their own economic ailments in the struggle against the "Jewish danger" along the whole economic front. This has lately been proven by the number of new decrees and projects of decrees. It is plain to see how petty trade does not arouse the slightest interest on the part of the state factors; on the contrary, it is pointed out that the stratum of small traders is superfluous and even harmful. This has indeed led to trade, as the vanguard of the economic front, always being hit by the various arrows that were aimed at it alone.
For example, by the tax system in force until now, which has to a certain extent ruined trade. All the various etatist experiments, the various cartels, syndicates, etc., which were aimed directly at hitting trade, and thanks to which trade lies in ruins together with the declassed merchant, who struggles with his last strength and summons superhuman heroism in order to hold on to his already weak enough trading positions, which were conquered with hard toil and diligence.
All this could still have been borne, had it already been the end of the experiments on Jewish economic life. The danger that emerges from the present situation for the future of trade becomes even more evident when one takes into account the sad prospects that appear, especially for the coming generation of Jewish merchants, in connection with the new industrial law, which hangs like the sword of Damocles over the head of the Jewish merchant and is liable to cut off the Jew's way to trade and to set up an iron wall that will not permit the considerable Jewish share in the field of commerce. The Jewish community faces hard trials in the future. All the old positions are seriously threatened. All this must be clarified in a broad public way, and at the same time demands must be put to the government to adapt the laws of trade to the laws of life.
Life is the strongest factor, time is the best teacher. All the dry theories, in their various forms, have, it is true, managed to swallow many dozens of victims and to cast fear upon the great unorganized mass of small traders, which looks with anxiety at the morrow and for which the horizon is clouded. But precisely at this moment, when despair and hopelessness begin to reign in the ranks of merchants and dealers, when the destructive spirit begins to act and is liable to poison all human energy, initiative and power of resistance, there must be set against it the eternal life-force, the creative optimism — all that is so deeply rooted in the Jewish spirit, in the Jewish soul. The inner energy must be awakened, the hard will not to let oneself be broken, to be capable of resisting and fighting everything that threatens the existence of the mass of small traders.
At the same time it must, to our great regret, be pointed out that to a very great extent the blame for the situation that has arisen falls on the passivity and lack of organization of the interested Jewish merchant circles themselves.
Never taking stock of what kind of period one is living in and in what kind of atmosphere one finds oneself, not seeing the day of today, not thinking what the day of tomorrow may bring, every individual lived only for himself.
At the present serious moment there must be an end to indifference. With the principle of all for one, one for all, a front must grow out of all the scattered and splintered forces, into one mighty power. Under a strong, purposeful [?] will to maintain the economic front, the tens of thousands of Jewish small traders, who are scattered over the remotest corners of the whole country, must grow into one large family. Not a single retailer and dealer may be missing from the ranks of the organization — under the banner of "the Central Union of Retailers and Small Traders in Poland", which has its branches in all parts of the country and which, incidentally, has already proven during its existence its sincerity and devotion to the interests of the masses of small traders.
It is perhaps superfluous to add that in all Poland in general, and in Zagłębie in particular, the Retailers' and Small Traders' Association is at the present moment the only economic institution that represents the great number of Jewish merchants and dealers, internally as well as externally. This is plain to recognize. For example, lately, from the lively and intensive work of organizing trade sections at the Retailers' and Small Traders' Association in Sosnowiec, which at the present responsible moment no longer confine themselves to caring for the member only at the tax assessment [?], so that no injustice should be done him, for a whole 10 zł a year, and to writing an appeal to the tax office for the paid-up member [?].
It can be seen from the impulsive work, the great sense of responsibility that has governed the responsible activists of the said organization, who understood the command of the hour, when everything and everyone is threatened in their existence, to answer the call of fate in order to protect the whole merchant class from a possible catastrophe. Every individual must understand the same.
When the fate of the Jewish merchant and dealer lies on the state's workbench, when with the hammer that forges the future they want to deal the last blow to the Jewish middle class, at such a responsible moment everyone must take his place in the ranks in order to create as quickly as possible the mighty power of the small traders, which shall be able to repel all the attacks and beat off all the assaults that are aimed only at the weak trading element. Such a force must be created that public opinion, the authoritative spheres, the deciding factors and the government bodies will have to reckon with it and take due interest in this class — thereby to secure a better future on the whole economic front.
A. J. Weiss.
One grosz will save the situation.

If the Będzin societies are poor, if the institutions are in need of support, then it is first and foremost the „Talmud Torah“.
The Będzin Talmud Torah has been impoverished and finds itself in a terrible state.
We have refrained from writing about this institution, because there were times when it was in a chaotic condition and the dark individuals let no one in who wanted to work in an orderly way, according to a certain system — they were afraid of fresh air. The mould that reigned there was „holiness“. The terrible state of affairs reigned there so long that everything turned into a heap of ruins, and the leaders capitulated.
Today the people's institution is in other hands, which want to bring the Talmud Torah to the point where it can maintain itself independently. The prevailing condition, however, is a terrible one: poverty whistles in the full sense of the word, there is nothing with which to pay the staff, and one must look for means so that the institution should not close.
And it is no small matter: the Talmud Torah has 400 children, and for them one needs people who will see to it that the children do not grow up ignoramuses; they must receive at least an elementary education. Of course we cannot by far be satisfied with that, because at the present moment the children of the people must receive an education that will let them find their way in life, which is becoming overgrown with thorns — above all for us Jews.
Today, however, we cannot dream of radical changes, if only because the institution is in danger of being closed, and that must not be allowed. After all, the smallest little town has its Talmud Torah, and it is surely in more comfortable conditions than the Będzin Talmud Torah — a town that has something for everything.
The present administration has come out with an appeal to the town, in which it begs that padlocks not be allowed to be hung on the Talmud Torah's gates. And they have a good way out, which is easy to carry out: they [?] ask for no more than O N E grosz, and this grosz is able to save the difficult situation from which they cannot crawl out. And who will not want to come to the help of an institution, when he knows that with his grosz comes salvation?
The institution wants nothing more than this: when you buy a loaf of bread, give one single grosz more and ask for a stamp in return. It seems that each of you and of us will fulfil this small thing, knowing that it will save the situation and that the Talmud Torah will have the possibility of developing.
So do not forget, when buying bread, to give one grosz more and at the same time to ask for the Talmud Torah stamp.
Eles.

I'm Riding Along the Line...

[Feuilleton — humorous monologue; summer lodgings.] (Monologue of a Jew who went off to rent a "letnie mieszkanie" [summer apartment]).
Conveyed by Ben Amotz.

3.
My "reception" in Bystra looked just like that of a Jewish merchant who comes to ask a Jewish "shatser" [?] to do him a favour... Even the Góral lad [highlander boy], who cracked his whip and shouted "Ksa yerdushe!" [?], also made fun of me.
— "Teraz pan przyjechał?" [So you come now, sir?] — All the apartments — he says — are already "zajęte" [taken].
— A fair question — I think to myself — but it still comes from a cabbage-head. When, then, was I supposed to come and rent an apartment? Firstly, my wife only became "duszna" [short of breath] at the end of May, and secondly, does the uncircumcised fellow know that it took several weeks until I got an interest-free loan [gmiles-khesed]...
Riding in the fiacre [horse cab] I approached the "merchants" Kalman Yona and Aharon Elazar and wanted to persuade them that the three of us together should rent a dacha in partnership.
— What kind of dacha are you looking for? — Kalman Yona asks me.
— What kind of dacha? The first thing — I say — in a Jewish neighbourhood, there should be a minyan for praying, and the main thing — there should be no shkotzim [gentile louts]; nowadays, an age of "race theory", I can't after all [?] put a finger into [their] mouth...
— Crazy or out of your mind, what do you know! — Kalman Yona gets angry — my Jewess has ordered me "guard and bewar" [sic] to rent a dacha with "wygody" [comforts].
— Namely?
— A "mieszkanie a tsush" [?], a kitchen with an oven, without bedbugs, a "wygodna" [comfortable] veranda, there should be "odpowiednie towarzystwo" [suitable company], it should be "wesoło" [jolly], so that when the "senushalkes" [?] are in town she won't be "nudzić się" [bored], and close to the market [targ], because for her, after running to buy vegetables she has to go straight off to Ciechocinek [a spa town]..
— "Yakh" [sic, for "I"] don't mean that — retorts [?] Aharon Elazar — my Jewess doesn't have such big "wymagania" [demands], but I must carry out what my daughters have ordered me.
— What "wygody" do your daughters need?
— My maidens — may they be healthy and strong — demand "przede wszystkim" [above all] — a beach, a "gęsty las" [dense forest], a pond, a "vlaskie khladnie" [?], near Szarewski's dancing, and the main thing
— "morowe chłopcy" [great lads]...
— What kind of lads do they want, exclusively Jewish ones, or may they also be shkotzim?
— You idler! What are you talking about? At home they shun a Jewish young man like real Hitlerites — so at the dacha they should go and "bawić się" [have fun] with Jewish young people? Is that a purpose for "intelligent panny" [young ladies] at summer resorts [letniska]?...
We wander from one villa to the next, visited a whole series of huts [chałupy], and everywhere got the same answer:
— "Zajęte" [taken].
One peasant woman took pity on us and wanted to rent us the cow's "room", but not in "czerwiec" [June], she says, only after "Święty Piotr" [St Peter's Day, 29 June]; then the cow is due to "be delivered"...
But what does King Solomon say? "I have laboured and I have found" — whoever searches, finds. Seeing that in Bystra we had nothing more to hope for, we did as the Jews in the wilderness: "and they journeyed from Bystra and encamped in Rajcza"...
Stepping onto the ground in Rajcza, it seemed to me that the train driver had, poor fellow, made a mistake, and instead of taking us to Rajcza he had driven me to Będzin and set me down at the Old Market.
Będzin and once again Będzin. A guess: the next city council may well "przyłączyć" [annex] Rajcza to Będzin...
But that's not what I'm after now. The main thing I want to tell you, my dear sir [panie leben], is that among our own folks I was not lost, and I managed to rent a "summer apartment" with my wife's "wygody".
My Jewess will have a flat "a tsush" [?], a kitchen with an oven, a brick cellar without bedbugs, the rain doesn't come in through the roof and the sun shines through the walls. She won't have to be bored, and above all you don't see a shaygets in broad daylight. That, nowadays, is worth all the money, especially in Rajcza...
The best "wygody" I also grabbed for my daughters: a dense forest, a pond, a "vlaskie khladnie", a dancing and an abundance of shkotzim, "all of them morowe chłopcy" [great lads].
Gentlemen, you can already wish me mazel tov. I've grabbed a "summer apartment" with all comforts. And if the One above us helps, my Jewess and my daughters will soon "sapliyen" [?] and I will become
— a "free bird"...
A Last Warning.

[Craftsmen — the crafts law and craft cards; article.] (More about the new decrees for the craftsmen).
Live long enough and you'll see it.
At long last the thing has started to move, and the danger facing Jewish handicraft has almost been called by its name[?]. One already hears some talk about it, and not only from the “leaders-misleaders” themselves. Not everyone, of course, finds his way here among all the reasons, details, etc. But the alarm that has been raised (incidentally, on our initiative) is already worth a great deal.
All along the point was that “people should also talk about it”, because our own cries and warnings struck deaf ears. Why — this question needs a separate answer:
For all 5 years the craftsmen's organisations roused, gave [warning], alarmed the public. The greater part slept, but Jewish craftsmen have their various friends, from one extreme to the other. And all these friends constantly did the opposite. They taught their followers that all the economic laws had been invented by Rosner and his comrades, and therefore — down with Rosner and his decrees! Precisely in the last crisis years great masses of young Jewish craftsmen joined, former workers and labour activists. And our labour world, you should know, does not recognise such laws.
Besides that there are still such important practical motives. When one takes out a card (incidentally, one must once and for all stop confusing the craftsman's card with a diploma, which to this day is still not compulsory.) — that is, when one registers, it can sometimes also bring the consequences of a patent [trade licence], taxes, insuring the workers, etc., and many craftsmen neither want nor are able to do that in the situation in which they now find themselves.
Here lie the most important reasons for not legalising oneself.
The smallest reason is the money question. For all 5 years, until a few months ago, obtaining a craftsman's card under normal conditions cost at most up to 10 zł.
At that time one also needed no examinations for it. Now the matter is already stricter. A special commission now judges whether one is fit to be an independent craftsman and receive a card, and so it already costs more.
But even this situation ends in about 2 months, and then such a card will not be obtainable for any money. No old craftsman will receive any right at all to run the workshop. Cards will be given only to those who complete a normal apprenticeship, hold a journeyman's examination and, after three years of work practice, pass the examination for master. Only when one has a master's diploma will one be able to obtain a card, which alone gives the actual right to run a workshop. Incidentally, the new examinations will no longer be “homely” examinations as until now. The regulations are very strict; they demand a higher threshold[?] of general education and great professional qualifications.
And on top of that, one more thing. All those who think it makes no difference — “we have lived like this until today, we'll go on living” — are mistaken. Precisely in this thought lies the catastrophe for them. All this time the names and addresses of all illegal workshops are being steadily collected in the voivodeships. And the fines can be high enough. Avoiding or getting round the law will be impossible.
At the last moment one can still save oneself. For this all forces must first be applied.
It is not merely a craftsmen's question; all those who have hindered until now must help. All forces to this front.
For those further off[?] who want to hinder even with their indifference, and for all those who want to neglect themselves — let this be a last warning.
Ts. V.[?]
A Hitlerite Victory.

[Satirical feuilleton — Nazi Germany, the “Night of the Long Knives”.] (A little feuilleton).
I had just tuned my radio to Berlin, thinking that perhaps I would hear an echo of shooting, or of shouts: “Down with Hitler, Kreuz-Donnerwetter, to all the black years!”
In the end some calm baritone voice was heard, which told about the putsch with such composure, just as if he were talking about a downpour or 36 degrees of heat!
He did not even rejoice in Hitler's victory — as if to say, what victory can one speak of here. After all, there was no war at all! Just some prank by a few hooligans (łobuzes).
In German it is called “Schurken”, but we here know what “łobuzes” means. With us too, when one wants to make small change of a movement, one says: “łobuzeria”...
In short, I heard nothing on the radio.
Nevertheless I think that the speaker's modesty is quite superfluous — he might well not have been ashamed and admitted that it was indeed a victory, a great victory; Hitlerism was already standing with half a foot over the abyss, but it caught itself in time and saved itself.
And if he had not been ashamed, he would have had to admit that he does indeed have a victory, but not yet in his pocket.
As it is written there about Haman: once you have begun to fall, it's “lipol, tipol, Gimpel”.

Radio Corner

[Radio.]
A dying person speaks into a radio microphone.
The “Daily Express” tells a remarkable story of how a dying person let it be known that she was still alive.
A certain sick woman, Mrs. O'Connor, a resident of Manchester, lay dying and was already so weakened that she could no longer speak.
The relatives who had gathered at the sick woman's bedside could only see her lips moving, but could not understand what the movements of the lips meant.
The doctor, who had not left the sick woman's side, had a happy idea. He turned to a firm that sold radio articles and asked them to send a microphone. The extraordinary receiving apparatus was connected to a loudspeaker. It was enough for the woman to make the slightest movement of her lips, and at once the microphone caught the rustle and the loudspeaker repeated it aloud.
It turned out that the sick woman was saying that she was beginning to feel somewhat better.
Hearing these words, the doctor, who had already completely given up hope of saving the patient, only then set about healing her with all his energy, and, applying every possible means of medical art, within a few weeks he put the patient back on her feet.
In this way the radio microphone has found for itself a new, important and useful field in our life.
New circulars

[Poland — government regulations and circulars; three items.]
How a neighbouring house-owner must behave when a building is threatened with catastrophe.
There are increasingly frequent cases where houses threaten to collapse and the authorities order the owners to carry out the necessary work at once in order to avert the threatening catastrophe — and then a situation arises in which a certain part of the equipment has to be set up in the neighbouring courtyard. But there are neighbouring landlords who do not permit their property to be “touched”. Rows break out which end in police reports and lawsuits.
The Minister of the Interior has therefore issued a circular with precise instructions on how the authorities must act in such cases.
Thus, if the authorities find that the ground of the neighbouring owner will have to be used, he too, exactly like the actual owner, must be drawn into the procedure; all demands that are sent to the owner of the endangered building must also be sent to the neighbouring owner, and likewise an order to permit the carrying out of the necessary work must also be sent to him.
Otherwise he has the right to prevent his ground from being touched.
The cited regulations do not take away from the neighbouring house-owner the right to come forward later with his claims by way of a civil suit and to demand appropriate compensation from the owner of the endangered house.
—o—
The convicted person will have to pay for administrative arrest sentences too.
The Ministry of the Interior explains that persons sentenced to arrest by administrative procedure must, as soon as they serve the sentence, pay the costs of their upkeep; likewise those whose fine is commuted to arrest are also obliged to do so, unless it is impossible to collect the sum in question from them because of extraordinary poverty.
In the penal orders issued it must be calculated how much the costs will amount to in case the sentence is carried out.
—o—
Value of the investment bonds.
The Minister of Finance orders in his latest circular that the bonds of the Investment Fund are to be recognised as fully valid securities which possess so-called pupillary (trustee) security. They may therefore be deposited as a caution for civil and military guarantees; they must be exchanged for money at the finance offices; and they must also be accepted without limitation, at their nominal value, at the state offices as caution and wadium (at public tenders etc.) or as security for excise, customs or transport credits granted by the State Treasury.

A Judicial Murder

[Article — the Arlosoroff murder trial; Palestine and the British Mandate.] By Sh. Rotenberg.
I stress right from the start that I am an opponent of the organisation to which Stavsky, who has been sentenced to death, belongs. Being an opponent of every reactionary movement, one must, as a matter of course, take a negative attitude towards a movement which is reactionary. But the writer of these lines does not look at events through any party spectacles; he views them solely from a purely objective, human standpoint. And if one asks the question — is Stavsky guilty of murdering Arlosoroff? — one must answer: No! Because all the "arguments" and "proofs" of his guilt are too weak for a death sentence to be handed down on their basis.
The accusation rested chiefly on the testimony of Mrs Arlosoroff. But whoever followed the court proceedings closely knows that the first descriptions Mrs Arlosoroff gave of the attackers differ absolutely from the real appearance of the accused. Besides, every one of us knows that it happens more than once that in broad daylight one meets a passer-by, greets him as an old acquaintance, and it turns out that he was a complete stranger. To err is human, an everyday phenomenon among mortals. The father of modern psychoanalytic science, Prof. Freud, can tell of many interesting curiosities of human error in everyday life. Not to mention that Mrs Arlosoroff saw the criminals on a dark night and in a state of the highest agitation.
I do not mean by this that Mrs Arlosoroff testified against the accused deliberately. I believe, rather, that, pervaded by deep grief over her misfortune and by a strong inner desire to catch the murderers, and dominated by a kind of autosuggestion, she could point to the accused, who in her opinion supposedly resemble the murderers.
Why did the court not take the more logical standpoint that the murder was of a sexual character? That, after all, is one of the frequent phenomena in the Orient, where woman is still an object of trade and not every poor devil can afford the luxury of buying a wife. It happens[?] that a poor camel-driver saves piastre by piastre all his life and fantasises about buying a wife, and very often his dream is never fulfilled, because despite the cheapness of women's flesh he still does not manage to collect the necessary minimal sum to buy a wife, even one of poor quality.
Facts of attacks on women in the Orient can be found in plenty in the daily press. Because of climatic and, as a consequence, psychological conditions, many murders take place in the East for sexual motives. Eros is there an unlimited dictator, a much mightier ruler and commander than in the countries with a temperate or cold climate. Only a short time ago the press reported a case in Palestine where a young man was seriously wounded because someone wanted to attack his girl. And as became clear from the court proceedings, the murder of Arlosoroff was carried out in a place which is known to be used by persons who meet for immoral purposes.
Further: why did the court not believe the defence witnesses, who confirmed Stavsky's alibi? Their testimony is, after all, just as weighty and clear as the testimony on the side of the prosecution.
Taking all this into consideration, one must come to the conclusion that in the Stavsky case we are dealing with a political verdict and consequently with a conscious judicial murder. It lies in the interests of the Mandatory power that there be not only the brawling[?] between Jews and Arabs, but also antagonism between Jews and Jews themselves. And only a death sentence could produce, and really did produce, the desired effect.
True to their motto "divide and rule", the English strive to carry it out throughout their whole colonial possessions, which they retain only thanks to the artificially inflamed antagonisms between the various peoples and tribes.
It is therefore the duty of all who are not narcotised by party hatred and do not want to make party capital out of the Arlosoroff case to demand a revision of the Stavsky trial, in order to save an innocent man from the claws of the British lion.

A Tale of Half a Straw Mattress... or: Heaven and Earth and “Wycieczkas”.

[Humorous feuilleton — organised excursions and the seaside.] By J. Oberżanek [?].

— Be well!
— Where am I going?
— Not to Ger [Góra Kalwaria] and not to Aleksander [Aleksandrów Łódzki].
— To the wife, at the dacha?
— What are you talking about? To the wife, at the dacha. Am I, Wolf Getzel, a Hasidic Jew, a ben-Torah, to put on a pair of sports trousers with a rucksack on my shoulders like a boy from the third form [oddział]? I am going on a “wycieczka” [Polish: an organised excursion]...
“Wycieczkas” have become the fashion now. Heaven and earth and “wycieczkas”. Every day another wycieczka: to Gdynia, to the sea; to Krynica, to Ciechocinek, to Truskawiec, to Szczekociny, to Olkusz, to Małobądz, to Goszychów[?] and other “historic” towns.
Every Monday and Thursday a different company runs the wycieczka — one time the company “Wagon-Li Knak” [a parody of Wagons-Lits/Cook], “Peas with Dumplings” [“Arbes mit kliskelekh” — a parody of Orbis], one time “Zhetetshak”[?] and one time the “Stushelets” [probably the Strzelec riflemen’s union]. Each company offers bigger “bargains”.
If “Wagon-Li Knak” does Ciechocinek with board for 3 gulden 15 groszy, along comes “Peas with Dumplings” and hands you Gdynia with the sea, just as it is, for 3.10 zł....
If “Zhetetshak” gives Zakopane for 2 gulden 45 groszy with all the “vigores”[?], along comes “Stushelets” and gives Ciechocinek for a three-groszy coin, with a snack of salt and a little glass of bath-water as a “dodatek” [Polish: extra]...
Well, it really is heaven and earth and wycieczkas!
And I tell you, in today’s crisis this is truly the best business. You know that on every wycieczka you are left with a nice couple of zlotys in your pocket; the calculation is simple:
A ticket to Gdynia costs, for example, about 30 zł. There and back — 60 zł. This, that, charoset, noodles — another 20 zł or so. So we have, as the Talmud says, 80 zł. And if “Wagon-Li Knak” gives it to me for 12 gulden, I have already earned 68 zł. And if God helps and I make two or three wycieczkas a week, I am left with some two hundred zł of “pure profit”...
Well, can there be a better business nowadays than making wycieczkas! So I really put aside all my businesses and took up tourism. Every week I make two or three wycieczkas and live the real life. I live on the train, I eat at the expense of “Wagon-Li Knak”, I board with “Zhetetshak”, my “sypialnia” [Polish: bedroom] is the bench in the carriage.
But what do you say? The jug goes to the water until its handle tears off. Yes, listen, it tore off on me — the whole tourism went sideways for me. Hear a story:
A few days ago the company “Peas with Dumplings” organised a wycieczka to the sea. I didn’t think long; I put on my wide sports breeches with the puttees, took the rucksack, packed my tallis and tefillin and went off to the company “Peas with Dumplings” to sign up.
— How much does the sea cost with you? — I asked.
— 15 gulden — answered the director of “Peas with Dumplings”.
— What do I get for the 15 gulden?
— For the 15 gulden you get the train there and back, the sea from all sides, the port, Gdynia, Hel, Karwia and Danzig as a “dodatek”.
— And what about sleeping?
— Sleeping — the director of “Peas with Dumplings” explained to me — is a question of how you want it.
— What do you mean, how? — I asked.
— It depends how you want it: a whole siennik [Polish: straw mattress] or half a siennik.
— Whichever is cheaper — I answered, and he signed me up for half a siennik.
Well, that brought me a downfall. Hear what happened with that half siennik.
After I had been shaken about all night in the carriage, I finally arrived at the sea.
— Undress! — commanded the “pshedovnik” [przewodnik, guide] of the company “Peas with Dumplings”, and in one minute everyone, old and young, men and women, stood Adam-naked, as God created them.
— What is this? — I asked.
— We’re going to the seaside “plaża” [Polish: beach].
— Well, uncle, why are you going about in clothes, eh? Why don’t you take off your trousers? — the pshedovnik asked me.
— Are you mad or out of your mind! What do you mean, I should take off my trousers in front of the whole congregation and, what is more, among strange women? I am, after all, a Jew, a ben-Torah..
I took a look around and everything went dark before my eyes: Jews and Jewesses, young men and girls, all Adam-naked, as God created them. True, they wear some scraps of little belts, just to fulfil the obligation, and that’s it... Beyond that — may God alone have mercy...
The naked males and females threw themselves into the sea, so that, may it not happen to you, my head began to spin...
What did I do? What do you mean, what did I do? I am surely not going to be the exception, so I too took off my trousers and let myself into the sea as well. I bathed together with the females and my head was spinning.
But that is not all yet. The worst downfall I had with the sleeping.
In the evening the pshedovnik “takes me to bed”, leads me off into a house, opens the door and lets me in — here you will sleep.
— May my evil, desolate dreams fall on my enemies’ heads! — so I said, when I looked at the 36 sienniks in one room, and on each siennik lay a man, a woman, two men, two women.
— No! Even if you cover me in gold, I will not lie down to sleep here! What do you mean, I should lie down in one room with strange women! I am, after all, somehow a Jew, a ben-Torah!
— You bought a ticket for half a siennik — the pshedovnik of “Peas with Dumplings” explained to me — and you will kindly lie down on half a siennik.
— What do you mean, half a siennik? How can one sleep on half a siennik, how, and who will sleep on the other half of the siennik?
— This young fellow here — he pointed out someone to me.
When I looked at my siennik-partner, everything went dark before my eyes. A “young man” who with one hand covers two like me and with one gulp swallows three like me — a lad with a pair of shoulders and with a head and a tongue — a wrecker.
The little “bokher” lay down comfortably and I had the other half of the siennik, and at every “rusz” [ruch, movement] of his elbow I saw all my great-grandmothers who rest in shining Paradise... at every “caress” of his “little hand” sparks flew before my eyes...
That “collective siennik” I will remember for a long, long time, and I will charge my children’s children that if they should ever go on a wycieczka to the sea with the company “Peas with Dumplings”, they should not take half a siennik...
How “Rapid Aid” Is Given by the Magistrate

[Będzin — Municipality and health; welfare.]
In recent weeks we were informed by Mr. Balimowski, an opiekun (welfare guardian) of the Public Welfare at the Będzin Magistrate, about the tactless conduct of Dr. Bilnik, who is the deciding person over the fate of the poor sick who turn to the Magistrate for medical aid.
Until not long ago the so-called opiekun had the right to give medical aid to the sick, and particularly to those whom doctors had certified must be sent to hospital at once.
But since the reign passed into the hands of Dr. Bilnik, the opiekuns have been deprived of the above-mentioned right to dispose of sick people — or more correctly, of Jewish sick people — regardless of the fact that another doctor certifies that the patient's condition is dangerous.
As an example of this scandalous conduct, the sad case that occurred in the poor Melcer family at 55 Podzamcze Street will suffice.
Mrs. Melcer once again [?] fell seriously ill. Unable to obtain a doctor from the Magistrate, the neighbours called in Dr. Serber [?], who declared that the condition was very serious.
With this written statement the opiekun Mr. A. D. Balimowski turned to Dr. Bilnik, the guardian of the sick souls, and literally begged him to send the woman to the Jewish hospital in Sosnowiec, or at the very least to send a doctor. Mr. Balimowski enclosed Dr. Serber's statement. But Dr. Bilnik treated with strange indifference the entreaties of the family concerned and of opiekun Balimowski, and also took no account of Dr. Serber's opinion. Moreover, Dr. Bilnik permitted himself to say that “he does not recognise any slip from the opiekuns at all.”
The neighbours of the sick woman, seeing that the situation was getting worse by the day, collected a few złoty and sent the patient to the Jewish hospital, where she indeed died on the third day. It is worth noting that the intervention and the running around to the above-mentioned doctor lasted about 10 days...
This is what the present “rapid aid” of the Będzin Magistrate looks like. As long as the sick person is not on his deathbed he cannot get the proper aid; when one comes to the above-mentioned doctor asking him to give a referral to a hospital, he declares in cold blood: “the patient isn't dying yet”...
As we are told, the opiekuns will resign. But we hold that this is still too little in the face of the outrageous fact that has occurred — that a Magistrate doctor should disregard the words of Dr. Serber, who declared that the patient must be taken into a hospital; and the catastrophe did indeed happen: a young woman, the mother of small children, has departed this world.
We cannot guarantee that the misfortune would not have happened even if the patient had been in hospital, but one must not endanger a human life, especially at a time when another doctor establishes that a human life hangs in the balance between death and life.
Let this scandalous fact not be hushed up — we demand an account of it from the Magistrate.
Extraordinary General Meeting of the Discount Bank Dissolved

[Będzin — Economy and institutions; bank.]
In the hall of the local Merchants' Association an extraordinary general meeting was to have taken place last Sunday in connection with the reorganisation of the Discount Bank.
Despite the fact that the agenda contained no more than the one single “world problem” — to set up a new board and council — all the forces of the parties around the bank were mobilised for the meeting. For a long, long time Jewish Będzin had not prepared itself for a general meeting as it did this time. Apparently, where it is a matter of carrying off a “victory,” the interest is great...
The hall is packed full. The atmosphere is like a steam bath, the air “smells” of gunpowder; one “spark” is enough and the fire flares up.
In the presence of about 170 members Mr. Lidzbarski [?] opens the meeting, which is taking place — he says — precisely on the Seventeenth of Tammuz, when the destruction of Jerusalem began on account of the Bar Kamtzas, and he appeals to those assembled to renounce their personal and party ambitions, so that the bank, which is bringing benefit at the present moment, should not have to be liquidated because of the quarrel.
Mr. Lidzbarski's words did indeed have an “effect.” Hardly had he uttered the words that he proposed Mr. A. Liwer as chairman of the meeting, than the first storm broke out on the part of the opposing side — of those grouped around the Small Traders' Association. A great uproar and tumult arose in the hall: “Secret ballot!” — voices were heard — “we don't want Mr. Liwer, but Mr. Fridler.”
After half an hour's uproar they proceeded to hold a secret ballot. Meanwhile sharp discussions were going on in every corner, which already led to blows as well, and in such a situation the policeman present dissolved the meeting.
Incidentally, it is worth noting that the very same people who stormed against Mr. Liwer's candidacy had themselves, a few hours earlier, proposed Mr. L. as chairman.

His Colleague Opened His Eyes
A Sad Fact of Present Times

[From life — a sad story.]
They married for love. He was disappointed quite quickly. Two years after the wedding he was full of regret: she is not at all as he had thought, and on top of that one really has to work for a living. And keeping a home besides [?], especially when one also becomes a father. Gone are those carefree days of bachelorhood. Especially when the home grows richer by a little child, and making a living gets ever harder and worse. The few clothes from before the wedding are wearing out, and new ones are hard to come by. His mood sinks; he becomes cross, sulky.
She, however, loves him more and more. Her husband, her child, her home — that is her paradise, and when she sees her husband sinking under the burden of worries about a living, and poverty starting to creep into every corner more and more — she becomes more active and helps earn the living.
Young, pretty — she quickly finds a way. The husband does not ask her where from and from what; at home things become more plentiful, he and she already have new clothes, and as for him — he now often has spare money [?] in his pocket, and as in those years before the wedding he is carefree again, in good humour, and again he is with his colleagues at billiards and at a game of cards.
One evening, when the games had gone well and afterwards he went out into the street with one of his colleagues, the latter suggested going to “a good place”.
“I'll take you — you'll be pleased, and perhaps it will even surprise you. In any case you'll remember tonight well... Come!”
And they went. The colleague led him somewhere into a side alley, and both disappeared into a certain house in which the promised corner of paradise was to be found.
Our hero did not have to wait there long before he saw before him — his wife — — —
— — — — — — — — — — — —
He ran home in despair, as if mad — perhaps it was not she!.. But she was not at home; soon she arrived.
“So you really didn't know?!.. Why didn't you ask yourself where the household's upkeep comes from, and where you suddenly get the means to play billiards?... On my groszy earned in shame you went off to live it up, and for that you now have your well-earned punishment!...”
Knife-sharp accusations, bitter mutual reproaches, a sleepless night. Both threaten suicide:
“But the child!... What will become of the child?”
For several days now neither has left the house.
The colleague does not deny that he deliberately took his “friend” there, so that he would see, so that he would know, and so that he would put an end to his wife's shameful and crooked path.
Open Letter — To the Kehilla Board in Będzin

[Będzin — kehilla, ritual slaughter; open letter.] To the kehilla board in Będzin.
Rumours are circulating in town that it has "succeeded" — even with the great protection of R' Itshe Meir's son — in prevailing upon the Rabbi of Będzin to agree to an arbitration (borerus) on the question of the 2 young shochtim (ritual slaughterers). People say that this arbitration is to take place very soon indeed.
As a man who has stood for many years in the work of Jewish public life in Będzin, I permit myself to ask you, respected board members: do you know to what a dangerous precedent you are giving your silent consent? What lawlessness and demoralisation you are helping to introduce into Jewish public life?
With this consent you are introducing a new Hottentot morality. Instead of fighting and rooting out such impudent tricks as were displayed by the "money-shochtim", who wanted, by the most improper means — means contrary to Jewish law and religious ethics — to grab the kehilla posts for themselves, reckoning with no one.
To achieve the "holy" war, every possible means was used, which ruined and broke the entire kehilla economy; by base informing they removed the active vice-president of the kehilla, who stood in the way of the wild appetites (by the way, it is worth dwelling separately on how the other national board members, together with the kehilla president, reacted to this step [?]). These people did not once tremble, and their conscience was not shaken, when with full awareness and calculated coldness they brought it about that in such a Jewish town as Będzin the whole Jewish population should be fed treyf, and that the lawlessness in this field should be so crying to heaven (the role of the rabbinate in the kashrut scandal is worth remembering). All this was done only in order to provide 2 young men with a livelihood.
Have you, kehilla leaders, considered what an arbitration means in such a situation? You yourselves are bringing it about that whoever forces his way in with violence and impudence will already be a "holder" (ochez, one with a claim of possession), and you will hold an arbitration with him; today it is shochtim, later it will be moyrey-hoyroes (rabbinical assistants) or other post-grabbers.
Are you really so naive as to let yourselves be caught by the cunning persons who, with their hypocrisy of supposedly "putting the kehilla in order", will smuggle in no more than the 2 shochtim and later something else... which they already have ready in their pockets, while you with your naivety help them carry out what they [?] did not manage during the Agudah majority in the kehilla.
Is this your programme, gentlemen, national Jewish board members? Did Jewish society send you into the kehilla to carry out such missions?
If you cannot cleanse the poisoned air and the accumulated filth left over from the previous rulers, it would be much more proper for you to lay down your mandates than to lend a hand to the net that is being spread in the interests of the Agudah.
The Jewish public is following your deeds.
Ploni [= "So-and-so"].
From the World of Sport.

[Sport — Zagłębie.] General meeting of the Football Union.
On Sunday the extraordinary general meeting of the Zagłębie Football Union took place in Będzin. On behalf of the Kielce union, Messrs Dr. Pilc and Malec were present. The chairman of the meeting was Mr. Sobolewski and the secretary Mr. Chorzelski [?]. The main topic of the meeting was the annulment of the autumn round of the championships. A whole series of speakers censured the activity of the Kielce head bodies, expressing no confidence in them. Very sharp in this sense were the speeches of Messrs Michalski and Walski [?], which were very strongly applauded. A longer discussion was also provoked by the decision of the Kielce head bodies, which set the 8th of this month as the date of the final between C.K.S. and "Unia"; nevertheless the Zagłębie Football Union regarded C.K.S. as champion. The head board in Częstochowa was reproached with being under the influence of certain persons, under whose pressure it issues decisions. Worth mentioning is the statement of the C.K.S. delegate, who said that although the decision of the head board in Częstochowa is an unjust one, C.K.S. will nevertheless turn out for the final.
On the motion of Mr. Lancman the entire old board was re-elected, but Mr. Walski categorically declined, declaring that he cannot accept the office of president because of the difficulties in the work on the part of the head leadership in Częstochowa. Mr. Sadowski was elected president, and in his place Mr. Brener joined the board. With that the meeting ended.

[Będzin — kehilla; the shechita affair and the arbitration.]
As our readers know, the kehilla administration in Będzin put forward the proposal that the „municipal plague“, which keeps growing on the body of the Będzin kehilla thanks to the „gift“ of the „little dollar-shochtim“ — should be settled through arbitration (borerut). The Rabbi's consent to this came only after the personal intervention of his son, R' Itshe Meir Lewin.
On the strength of the Rabbi's consent, the kehilla administration this week turned to the rabbinate, asking it to fix the place where the arbitration should take place and to announce who the arbitrators are.
To this the rabbinate replied that they cannot concern themselves with the arbitration matter, because the Rabbi did not write to them about it, nor did he tell them by word of mouth.
— So everything stays as it was again...

A Sosnowiec Young Man in the Role of a „Yoshe Kalb“ / The Court of Appeal Upholds the Sentence on the Policeman and His Accomplices from Modrzejów / The Publisher of „Błyskawica“ Before the Court / Dozens of People Stung by Bees / Thieves in the Premises of the Sosnowiec Kehilla

[Shtetl — an impostor from Sosnowiec; followed by four short news items: Modrzejów/Warsaw, Katowice, Będzin, Sosnowiec.]
During the World War a certain Anshel Klag marched off from the shtetl of Unów[?] to the front, leaving behind a wife with a 2-year-old child. Apart from the first letter nothing more was heard from him, and people held that he had fallen in the war; this assumption was accepted as correct in 1929, because a Jew came to the local rabbi and declared that he himself had seen Anshel being buried.
Last week a Jew in European dress appeared in the shtetl and asked whether people here knew Anshel Klag, whether Anshel's wife Breine[?] and the child Hirshl were still alive, etc.
A Jew, hearing the stranger's questions, cried out: „Why, that's Anshel!“ When the wife came too, she cried out quietly with a sigh: Why, that's Anshel! But the stranger took heart and let himself have a conversation with her, during which he told her that Anshel was in fact[?] alive — he is in Siberia.
The news that „Anshel has come“ spread through the shtetl, and the whole shtetl came running. But the stranger, seeing the crowd, produced a document showing that he is from Sosnowiec and that his name is actually Lindoy[?].
Next morning, when the fellow had made a „va-yivrach“ [taken flight], the shtetl understood that this was a first-class swindler who fools hundreds of people in this way.

The Court of Appeal Upholds the Sentence on the Policeman and His Accomplices from Modrzejów
Some time ago the Sosnowiec investigative authority came upon the trail of a sensational affair of policeman Jan Hahn of Mysłowice, who on the one hand was a policeman but at the same time stood at the head of a robber band.
The affair was uncovered thus:
One day the merchant Jakób Marmur came to Modrzejów, wanting to buy some horses. As it happened he met his acquaintance Jakób Rechnic, whom he told that he had a large sum of money on him. Rechnic promised the merchant to show him where one could get cheap horses, and the two acquaintances arranged to meet by the cemetery in Modrzejów.
When the merchants came together and the bargaining began with a certain Reuben Jargus, who was to supply the horses, a masked bandit suddenly sprang out from the bushes and shouted:
— I'm from the police, hand over the counterfeit money!
The merchant tried to argue that the money was not counterfeit, but then the fellow pulled out a revolver and forced the Jew to hand over the money.
The police conducted an investigation into the story, and it then turned out that the whole „deal“ had been staged by policeman Hahn, who had himself robbed the money. The district court in Sosnowiec sentenced the bandit for this to 8 years' imprisonment and his accomplices Rechnic and Jargus to 5 and 4 years.
The convicted men appealed, and this week the Court of Appeal in Warsaw heard the case. After acquainting itself with the indictment, the Court of Appeal upheld the earlier sentence.

From 1 August Tram Tickets in Zagłębie Become Cheaper

[Zagłębie — transport; tram.] From Będzin to Sosnowiec and back — cheaper by only 5 groszy.
For a long time now various bodies have intervened so that the fare for tram tickets in Zagłębie should become cheaper.
At last the tram management has agreed to this, and from 1 August the following tram fare is already in force:
From Sosnowiec to Będzin and the Remiza [tram depot] 45 gr. (formerly 50 gr.), to Dąbrowa 65 gr. (formerly 85), as far as Mieszki[?] 55 gr. (formerly 70).
Within this framework the tickets on the Czeladź line will also become cheaper. The 20-groszy tickets remain unchanged.
The tram management has also taken into account the users of monthly tickets, for whom tickets by zones are being introduced. For example, a monthly ticket for 2 zones will cost 7.50 zł., 3 zones — 11 zł., 4 zones 12.50 zł., 5–6 zones — 14 zł., 7–8 zones — 19 zł., 9–10 zones — 19 zł.
Until now a monthly ticket to Dąbrowa cost 36 zł.
Big Police Raid in Będzin County

[Będzin county — police.] In the night from Friday to Saturday the police carried out a big raid on the 'melinas' [criminal hide-outs]. The raid produced an unexpected result. About 50 suspicious persons were arrested. Weapons and explosives were also found.
The Abuses in the Sosnowiec Relief Office before the Court of Appeal

[Sosnowiec — court; unemployed.] In recent days the Court of Appeal in Warsaw dealt with the indictment against several officials who, together with unemployed persons, committed abuses in the Sosnowiec relief office for the unemployed.
At the request of the defence the trial was postponed.
A Bloody Wedding in Olkusz County

[Olkusz county — crime.] In the village of Sułoszowa (Olkusz county) a wedding took place at a village peasant's. When the guests were already drunk, revolvers, knives and the like went to work. The result: 1 guest was killed and several were wounded.
Campaign for the JNF in Bystra

[Bystra — Zionism; JNF.] In connection with the large number of Jewish guests spending the summer holidays in Bystra, a committee has been formed there which is working very energetically for the JNF [Keren Kayemet].
The committee consists of: S. Frenkel (chairman), Max Karger (secretary), Miss Mandelzon (treasurer), A. Z. Bernsztajn, Miss Cinz[?], Moshe Frenkel.
So far about 80 zł. have been collected by Mr. Bernsztajn, Miss Cinz, Miss Mandelbaum and Schönberg.
The committee is organising a memorial service on the day of Bialik's funeral in Tel Aviv.
Took 'Cash' from His Brides, and When the Opportunity Arose He Stole Things Too...

[Katowice and Będzin — crime; marriage swindler.] In Katowice a certain Tyszka (his real name is Kamiński), a well-known swindler, has been arrested. His 'occupation' was to strike up acquaintances with naive girls, to whom he presented himself as the owner of a farm in the Kresy [the eastern borderlands] who was looking for a suitable match. In this way he managed to take 'cash' [kontanty?] from his brides, and if the chance arose he also took a few things.
During the investigation it became clear that the man had used his 'practice' in Zagłębie as well. He lived with a Christian woman on the Warpie in Będzin. Fearing he would be unmasked by the Będzin police, he went off 'on tour' to Upper Silesia, where he did indeed fall into the 'trap'.
A Husband of... 14 Wives Arrested

[Warsaw and Sosnowiec — crime.] In Warsaw a certain Aron Najman, a resident of Sosnowiec, has been arrested; he traded in... wives. In all he managed to marry no more than 14 wives. Recently he married a Warsaw woman, took 4,000 zł. from her and vanished. The woman, however, tracked the bird down and handed him over to the police.
How Rent Must Be Paid by Post.

[Supreme Court rulings — rent.] The Supreme Court has issued a ruling on how rent may be paid by post. A certain tenant had a dispute with his landlord and therefore sent the rent by post, deducting the postal costs from the sum. A trial over this took place in the district court and then in the court of appeal, which saw no ill intent [?] in this on the tenant's part; the matter went on to the Supreme Court, which declared that in no case may any costs of sending the money to the landlord be deducted from the rent, and that one may also not be late with the sending past the due date.

A Father's Criminal Deed.
In Rybnik the following tragedy occurred this week.
The 37-year-old supervisor of the local psychiatric institution decided to commit suicide. To this end, last Tuesday he sent his wife away from home so that he would not be disturbed in carrying out his devilish plan.
In the evening of that same day, while his children were already asleep, he turned on the gas taps and then lay down to sleep.
In the morning, when the neighbours sensed a strong smell of gas coming from the watchman's apartment, they broke open the door and then saw the terrible sight. The supervisor and his children were already dead. The eldest child was 8 years old, the youngest — one year.
